The towers contain sprawling offices for the zulkirs' expansive entourages, elaborate chambers for meetings between zulkirs, and spaces for the creation of doors to demiplanes where rulers can meet in near-absolute privacy.

At the towers' center is the Grand Chamber, an ostentatious space draped in Thayan iconography. Here, the zulkirs gather to make infrequent official announcements, which scribes record and distribute throughout the nation.

entries.name: Adventures in Eltabbar
entries: Roll on or choose a result from the Eltabbar Adventures table to inspire ideas for games set in the city.

entries.caption: Eltabbar Adventures
rows: Retrieve a strange magical device from the {@area Necromancer's Bookshelf|075|x} for their Red Wizard patron.
Recover a missing shipment of magic items for their merchant patron, who suspects the stolen shipment is hidden in {@area Two Plateaus Shipping Company|079|x}.
Recover their Red Wizard patron's magical research, which was stolen by a rival and hidden in a spire in the {@area Ward of Towers|077|x}.
Break out an innocent friend from the {@area City Guardhouse's jail|072|x}.

data.name: Chapter 2: Thay in Danger

entries.title: The lich Szass Tam plans to raise an army of undead infused with demonic power.

entries: This chapter describes the campaign that unfolds in chapters 3–7: Operation Deadfall. In this magical spy thriller, the characters work as agents for a Thayan leader to undermine and defeat {@book Szass Tam|XDMG|8|Szass Tam}, a lich and the zulkir of necromancy. If the characters are successful, they might keep him dead for one hundred years, protecting the world from his despotic plans. If the characters fail, undead hordes infused with demonic power will overrun Thay and kill anyone who doesn't swear fealty to Szass Tam.

This chapter also provides tools for preparing and running a campaign in which espionage, political intrigue, and dangerous missions are core elements. Character creation tips and guidelines help you assist players in creating characters suited to this campaign.

entries.name: Evil Regent Rising
entries: Szass Tam is a tyrannical lich necromancer obsessed with commanding undead hordes. He envisions a Thay in which all residents bow to him or become his undead servants. (Read more about the lich in "Szass Tam" in {@area appendix B|372|x}.)

Szass Tam has spent the last 150 years plotting to take over Thay. After becoming zulkir of necromancy and gaining lichdom, he tried to harness the power of Eltab, the demon formerly trapped underneath Thay's capital. Szass Tam intended to enhance his own magic with demonic power and thereby stifle any who would oppose his rule. When he failed, he raised an army of undead, killed the zulkirs who opposed him, and declared himself regent.

A few decades ago, Szass Tam restored the zulkir council and installed loyal zulkirs to spare himself from the minutiae of rule. But rivals have overthrown those zulkirs and recognize Szass Tam only as zulkir of necromancy, not as Thay's regent. The lich is enraged that anyone dares question his authority and plots to retake control of the nation.

entries.name: Demonic Ritual
entries: Szass Tam plans to raise an army of undead to overrun Thay, then declare himself regent. He has devised a ritual he calls Malefice Mortum (pronounced MAL-uh-fis MOR-tum) that would raise an undead army while simultaneously siphoning Abyssal power from demons and infusing that energy into those undead. The resulting demonic undead, called malefites (pronounced MAL-uh-fights), glow with unholy green energy.
When the campaign begins, Szass Tam is ensconced in his lair in Thaymount, trapping powerful demons and draining their Abyssal power.

entries.name: Szass Tam's Aim
entries: Szass Tam's Malefice Mortum ritual is just his first step toward reclaiming Thay. After his malefites sweep the nation, he plans to kill any zulkirs who oppose him and seize power.

entries.name: Growing Demonic Power
entries: Szass Tam's experiments using the foul magic of his Malefice Mortum ritual have created groups of malefites that roam Thay's countryside, attacking innocents and destroying homes.

The experiments also weakened the veil between the Material Plane and the {@book Abyss|XDMG|5|Abyss}. Some demons have invaded Thay to wreak havoc, and more will pour into the region after Szass Tam's ritual is complete. (See {@adventure appendix B|AUD|9} for new demons that invade Thay.) Szass Tam doesn't care about the suffering he causes; he considers Thayans valuable only as fodder for his hordes.

entries.name: Thay's Only Hope
entries: Before this campaign, {@creature Xelnene Thrul|AUD|Zulkir Xelnene Thrul} learned of Szass Tam's plans through her spies. Thrul warned the other zulkirs that Szass Tam planned to attack Thay and betray them, but they dismissed her, insisting she was the one who coveted ultimate power.

The other zulkirs had anonymously received correspondence between Thrul and unnamed Red Wizards that indicated Thrul—the second-strongest zulkir, behind Szass Tam—planned to oust the lich and defeat the others to claim Thay's regency. Thrul eventually proved the correspondence was fabricated, but the paranoid zulkirs still don't trust her intelligence about Szass Tam. Thrul knows Szass Tam is behind the effort to discredit her, but she can't prove it.

Thrul also knows that defeating Szass Tam in combat would require the combined might of the Council of Zulkirs; without the others' help, that approach is impossible. So Thrul, a master of spycraft accustomed to working behind the scenes to achieve her goals, launched Operation Deadfall: a high-risk espionage effort to undermine and defeat Szass Tam.

In this campaign, the characters become Thrul's field agents. They're the only ones standing between Szass Tam and Thay's destruction. They should have their own reasons for wanting to save Thay. Perhaps it's their homeland, perhaps they hail from a realm that would be threatened by the lich-regent, or perhaps they're committed to affecting political change in this harsh nation.
Regardless, Operation Deadfall is extremely dangerous. Szass Tam has spies everywhere, and if he or his agents discover the operation's details, he'll murder everyone involved.

entries.name: Campaign Summary
entries: The campaign requires the characters to target Szass Tam's spy network, gather allies, and confront the lich. The plot is further outlined below.

entries.name: Chapter 3
entries: {@adventure Chapter 3|AUD|3} takes place in Eltabbar, Thay's capital. After malefites attack the bazaar, the characters are recruited into Operation Deadfall. They undertake missions to weaken Szass Tam's spy network so their future work can go undetected.

entries.name: Chapter 4
entries: In {@adventure chapter 4|AUD|4}, the characters travel to a rural tax station in the tharch of Pyarados, where they try to convince disgruntled militia members to join their fight. They also travel to an abandoned temple to seek the {@item Spirit-Binding Censer|AUD}, which could keep Szass Tam dead for one hundred years.

entries.name: Chapter 5
entries: In {@adventure chapter 5|AUD|5}, the characters travel to the hinterlands of the tharch of Eltabbar to seek aid from rebellious Red Wizards who could help the characters reach Szass Tam's ritual site discreetly. They also journey to the island of Alaor Minor to convince pirates to join their cause.

entries.name: Chapter 6
entries: The characters return to Thay's capital in {@adventure chapter 6|AUD|6}, but when they attempt to rendezvous with Thrul, they find their operation headquarters ransacked. Szass Tam's agents have discovered Operation Deadfall. After dealing with the aftermath of this exposure, the characters race to Thaymount to find the underground tunnel that leads to Szass Tam's lair. They must break through the barrier the lich has placed around the tunnel's entrance and contend with demons that flood the region.

entries.name: Chapter 7
entries: Finally, in {@adventure chapter 7|AUD|7}, the characters contend with a powerful clan of snakelike people called sarrukhs who guard the areas outside Szass Tam's ritual chamber. On entering the chamber, they find Zulkir Thrul near death and must face Szass Tam once and for all.

entries.name: Preparing the Campaign
entries: Before beginning this campaign, review the "Campaign Start" section of the {@book Dungeon Master's Guide|XDMG}. Plan to share the following information with the players prior to your game:

items.name: Campaign Length
items.entry: This campaign will likely span fifteen or more sessions.

items.name: High Level
items.entry: Characters should be level 11 when the campaign begins. If players don't already have characters of this level, they'll need to create new ones.

items.name: Spy Thriller
items.entry: This campaign combines elements of high fantasy and spy thrillers. Players should anticipate a plot that involves schemes and subterfuge in addition to fantasy action.

entries.name: Preparation
entries: Before your first session, review chapters 3–7, taking notes as needed. The campaign's details might spark ideas for character backstories to suggest to your players or for NPCs you want to emphasize.
Each chapter begins with a page to help you prepare and run it that includes the following:

items.name: Key Plot Points:
items.entry: A summary of the important elements in the chapter's story

items.name: Preparation:
items.entry: Steps to prepare to run the chapter, including the stat blocks from the {@book Monster Manual|XMM} or {@adventure appendix B|AUD|9} that you might need

items.name: Key NPCs:
items.entry: A {@adventure table|AUD|3|Key NPCs} summarizing the names, roles, stat blocks, and locations of key nonplayer characters in the chapter

entries.name: Magical Spy Thriller

entries.title: Szass Tam's ritual will weaken the veil between planes, allowing demons to pour into Thay.

entries: This campaign is a spy thriller. The fate of Thay lies on the characters' shoulders, but no one can know about their heroics. Use the guidance in this section to emphasize Operation Deadfall's high stakes, the importance of secrecy, and the danger involved.

entries.name: Running a Magical Spy Thriller
entries: A magical thriller focuses on careful planning and the use of magic while tensions run high and the stakes are higher.

For example, the characters might need to get a target—a dangerous Red Wizard—alone and convince the target to betray Szass Tam. If they arouse the target's suspicions, the characters jeopardize their clandestine mission.

Two characters, both gregarious charmers, begin chatting with the target at a bar the target frequents. An unremarkable drinker—another character—watches and whispers a {@spell Message|XPHB} spell to a fourth character, who lurks in the alley outside. The character in the alley shoos away bystanders while the gregarious characters usher the target into the alley under false pretenses. The characters have the target alone and can bribe, persuade, or intimidate the target—whatever they think will be most effective.

If this mission goes smoothly, it's thanks to the characters' coordination. Even though the characters kept cool, it's likely they—and the players—felt tension about what might happen if their plan fell apart.
Use the following suggestions to reinforce the themes of a magical thriller.

entries.name: Base of Operations
entries: The characters might have a home, a {@book Bastion|XDMG|10}, or another facility from which they decide to run their espionage activities. If they don't want to use a personal location as their base, suggest the Crystal Ball Inn as their meeting place. The inn is described in chapter 1 in "{@area Eltabbar, Thay's Capital|063|x}."

entries.name: Code Names
entries: Since the characters must not openly discuss their missions in public, Zulkir Thrul assigns code names to their targets and goals. Code names are nicknames that obscure the subject's identity, allowing the discussion of sensitive matters in public without identifying real names.

The characters might come up with code names for other aspects of their clandestine work. Encourage this tactic; the more your game leans into this staple of espionage storytelling, the more fun your players are likely to have.

In chapter 3, Thrul asks the characters to determine a code name for their group as well as one for each character. It's important for the players to like their characters' code names, since that's how others will refer to them throughout the campaign.
Roll on or choose results from the Group Code Names table and the Character Code Names table to help inspire these code names.

entries.name: Magical Tactics
entries: Level 11 characters begin play with access to powerful magical resources that can help them remain covert. Whether the characters wield spells or magic items, encourage them to avoid suspicion via creative use of magic.
If your players aren't sure how to use magic to aid their espionage activities, suggest the options below to spark their imaginations.

entries.name: Magical Reconnaissance
entries: The {@spell Greater Invisibility|XPHB} spell can allow characters to scout or sneak about unseen. Similarly, the {@spell Scrying|XPHB} spell might help them learn about a target from afar. Later in the campaign, the {@spell Teleport|XPHB} spell can help characters quickly get in and out of locations without being spotted.

entries.name: Magical Infiltration
entries: The {@spell Invisibility|XPHB} spell could help characters remain unseen in crowds; the {@spell Mass Suggestion|XPHB} spell could prompt bystanders to leave an area the party wants to infiltrate.

entries.name: Magically Hiding Evidence
entries: The {@spell Illusory Script|XPHB} spell is useful for concealing incriminating written communication from prying eyes. If the evidence is a magic item, the {@spell Nystul's Magic Aura|XPHB} spell could make it appear to be nonmagical or appear to belong to a different school of magic.

entries.name: Magically Hiding Identities
entries: In chapter 3, Thrul gives each character a {@item Masquerader's Brooch|AUD} (see {@area appendix A|341|x}) to help them hide their identities when meeting with her. Other magic items they could use to hide their identities or misdirect enemies include a {@item Hat of Disguise|XDMG} and a {@item Staff of Birdcalls|XDMG}. Similarly, the characters can use Illusion spells such as {@spell Alter Self|XPHB}, {@spell Disguise Self|XPHB}, or {@spell Seeming|XPHB} to hide their identities.

entries.name: Importance of Secrecy
entries: It's up to you whether you think the characters are doing enough to keep their activities clandestine during Operation Deadfall. If the characters aren't secretive, there should be consequences, as discussed in "Three Failures" below.

entries.name: Use Your Discretion
entries: How much being noticed during their missions gets the characters into trouble depends on the context. If a bystander notices the characters breaking into a building or attacking a target, the bystander won't automatically know the group's goal. However, if the characters do these things while discussing their plan to defeat Szass Tam, they're not respecting Zulkir Thrul's mandated secrecy. If they're usually careful, you might decide that the only witness follows the Closed Eyes tradition (see "{@area Closed Eyes|038|x}" in chapter 1) and doesn't report the characters' activities to the authorities.

entries.name: Reward Consistent Secrecy
entries: If the characters take pains to hide their espionage—always using code names and liberally employing magic to cover their trail, for example—you could skip some encounters as a reward. The campaign provides guidance on encounters in chapters 3–4 you can skip, and you might choose to skip others.

entries.name: Three Failures
entries: The characters can fail their secrecy mandate three times before their ability to complete Operation Deadfall is compromised. Each time you decide the characters seriously violate secrecy, describe one of the following events:

items.name: Dead Agents
items.entry: While the characters are in Eltabbar, they hear that Red Wizards loyal to Szass Tam have discovered and executed several spies working against the lich. The next time the characters speak with Zulkir Thrul or her agents, the characters learn the spies were working for Thrul. She believes the spies were mistaken for the characters and warns the characters to be more careful.

items.name: Enemies on Alert
items.entry: While the characters are in Eltabbar, they notice that City Watch patrols have increased. The next time the characters speak with Zulkir Thrul, she tells them the patrols are Szass Tam loyalists who are hunting the characters. She warns the characters to be more careful.

items.name: Raided Allies
items.entry: The next time the characters speak with Zulkir Thrul or her agents, they learn that several agents' safe houses were raided by Szass Tam's loyalists. She believes the loyalists were looking for the characters' hideout and warns the characters to be more careful.

entries: These events can happen in any order, and you can repeat events if you like. Once three events have happened, the next time the characters violate their secrecy mandate, they suffer a serious narrative consequence (see "Compromised Characters").

entries.name: Compromised Characters
entries: The fourth time you decide the characters seriously violate their secrecy mandate, the characters are compromised. Zulkir Thrul sends them a note (whose content is obfuscated via the {@spell Illusory Script|XPHB} spell) informing them that Szass Tam's agents have discovered their identities.
The characters have a final chance to salvage their ability to complete Operation Deadfall. Describe the following mission options and allow them to pursue one of their choice:

items.name: Destroy the Dossier
items.entry: A tiefling spy leader for Szass Tam named Nya Yar (Medium, Neutral Evil {@creature Archpriest|XMM}) has collected a dossier that implicates the characters. The characters must destroy the dossier to regain anonymity. A worshipper of Bane, Yar operates a spy outpost based in a hookah bar. Use {@area map 3.4|0f5|x} in chapter 3 for this encounter, with the dossier hidden in {@area area H2|0fa|x}. Yar and {@dice 1d4} {@creature Spy Master|XMM|Spy Masters} are in the building at all times. (If the characters attempt this mission more than once, change the spy leader's name each time.)

items.name: Fake Your Death
items.entry: The characters must convince Szass Tam's agents they're dead. To do this, the characters must spend 2,500 GP and work with Thrul's agents for 24 hours to create a scene of violent destruction in an appropriate space (the details are up to you). The agents then use {@item Spell Scroll|XDMG|Spell Scrolls} to cast {@spell Feign Death|XPHB} on each character before anonymously alerting Szass Tam's loyalists. A group can use this option once; Szass Tam's agents won't be fooled twice.

items.name: Hire the Cleaners
items.entry: The characters can give Thrul or her agents 5,000 GP to hire mages to remove evidence of the characters' recent activities by bribing witnesses, magically modifying memories, or the like.

entries: Zulkir Thrul is unwilling to pay any costs associated with salvage missions.

If the characters successfully complete a salvage mission, continue the campaign as if they hadn't violated their secrecy mandate. The characters can complete "Destroy the Dossier" and "Hire the Cleaners" as many times during the campaign as you allow.

entries.name: Character Creation
entries: This campaign is designed for four to six level 11 characters. Your players might create new characters or use characters they've played previously.

entries.name: New Characters

entries.title: Operatives distract Red Wizards while others make a hand off.

entries: New characters should be suited for a covert operation. Being adept at stealth, social skills, useful magic, and problem-solving could mean the difference between completing a mission without alerting Szass Tam's allies and blowing the operation.

Characters might have myriad reasons to undertake Operation Deadfall. Zulkir Thrul offers ample payment, of course, but this campaign is most satisfying if new characters hate Szass Tam. "{@area Thayan Adventurers|03d|x}" in chapter 1 provides more details about Thayans who pursue adventuring.

entries.name: Playing Thayan Characters
entries: Roll on or choose results from the Thayan Character Motivations table to help players develop their characters' backstories.

entries.caption: Thayan Character Motivations
rows: The character's loved one was murdered by a Red Wizard who served Szass Tam. The character has plotted against those loyalists, accepting mercenary work that targets such Red Wizards and their allies.
The character's loved one aspired to serve Szass Tam. The character tried to dissuade the loved one, who died due to their ambitions.
The character's family was prominent in Thayan society, but an ancestor opposed Szass Tam, who killed the ancestor and ruined the family. The character blames the lich for their family's misfortunes.
The character was on track to become a Red Wizard or a Thayan knight but spoke against Szass Tam, whose allies killed the character's employers. The character took mercenary work to survive.
The character's parents were in the magic items trade. They competed with Szass Tam, whose allies framed the family for treason. The character now seeks revenge.
The character is an Open Eyes rebel and might come from a long line of Thayan political dissidents. The character hates Szass Tam and other evil Red Wizards.

entries.name: Playing a Red Wizard
entries: One or more of your players might want to play a Red Wizard who opposes Szass Tam. The characters also might have pledged loyalty to Zulkir Thrul; this provides a good reason why she recruits them.

A Red Wizard character might be of any species from the {@book Player's Handbook|XPHB}. The following backgrounds are common for Red Wizards. Entries marked with an asterisk are from {@book Arcana Unleashed|AU}:
The Red Wizard Class Options table suggests classes and subclasses common for Red Wizards.

entries.caption: Red Wizard Class Options
rows: {@class Warlock|XPHB|Fiend Patron|Fiend|XPHB}, {@class Warlock|XPHB|Great Old One Patron|Great Old One|XPHB}

{@class Wizard|XPHB|Abjurer|Abjurer|XPHB}, {@class Wizard|XPHB|Conjurer|Conjurer|AU}*, {@class Wizard|XPHB|Enchanter|Enchanter|AU}*, {@class Wizard|XPHB|Diviner|Diviner|XPHB}, {@class Wizard|XPHB|Evoker|Evoker|XPHB}, {@class Wizard|XPHB|Illusionist|Illusionist|XPHB}, {@class Wizard|XPHB|Necromancer|Necromancer|AU}*, {@class Wizard|XPHB|Transmuter|Transmuter|AU}*
footnotes: *See {@book Arcana Unleashed|AU}. Encourage players who want to play Red Wizard characters to review "{@area Red Wizards|00b|x}" in chapter 1. Appendix A includes magic items Red Wizard characters might want, including a {@item Robe of Thayan Arcana|AUD} and a {@item Scarlet Spellbook|AUD}. The characters might find these items in {@adventure chapter 5|AUD|5}. {@book Forgotten Realms: Heroes of Faerûn|FRHoF} includes rules for Thayan Spell Tattoos, which you might decide are available to characters.

entries.name: Playing a Thayan Knight
entries: If one of your characters is a Red Wizard, another player might want to play a Thayan knight who serves that Red Wizard. (Thayan knights are described in {@area chapter 1|016|x}.)
A Thayan knight character might be of any species from the Player's Handbook. The following backgrounds are common for Thayan knights:
The Thayan Knight Class Options table suggests classes and subclasses common for Thayan knights.
Appendix A includes magic items a Thayan knight character might want, including a {@item Thayan Sword|AUD}. The characters might find this item in chapter 5.

entries.name: Playing Non-Thayan Characters
entries: Players need not create Thayan characters. At level 11, the heroes might be powerful mercenaries or roving adventurers from anywhere in Faerûn who happen to visit Thay while Szass Tam prepares his Malefice Mortum ritual.
Roll on or choose results from the General Character Motivations table to help players develop their characters' backstories.

entries.caption: General Character Motivations
rows: The character has sworn an oath to oppose tyranny and seek justice for the downtrodden. They believe Szass Tam is one of the world's worst tyrants and must be stopped.
The character suffered at the hands of an evil necromancer. They find Szass Tam abhorrent and believe he must be destroyed.
The character hails from a nation that borders Thay. Their homeland would suffer greatly if Thay falls to Szass Tam.
The character has close ties to benevolent necromancers or is one. The character finds Szass Tam's evil necromancy an abomination that must be stopped.
The character is fascinated by the Red Wizards' approach to magic; they might even be a mage. They fear for the safety of Red Wizards who oppose Szass Tam should he again rise to power.
The character is associated with a good god and finds association with demons hateful. Once they learn Szass Tam's plan, they decide he must be stopped.

entries.name: Existing Characters
entries: Any character from Faerûn—or another setting, if you allow it—can undertake Operation Deadfall as long as they are of an appropriate level (see "{@area Character Level|0a5|x}").

This campaign begins in Eltabbar, so work with your players to come up with a reason why their characters are in the city and why Zulkir Thrul recruits them. Roll on or choose results from the Purpose in Eltabbar table to inspire what brings the characters to the city.

entries.caption: Purpose in Eltabbar
rows: The character is an expert at retrieving kidnapped individuals. A wealthy Thayan family has paid the character to travel to Eltabbar and retrieve their scion from a powerful Red Wizard whose employ the scion wants to leave.
The character studies demonology or necromancy and has heard rumors of powerful energy spikes in Thay. The character believes this is an ill omen and has traveled to Eltabbar to investigate.

The character is a mercenary whose mysterious employer paid them to come to Eltabbar and destroy magic item shipments or sabotage meetings. The character later learns their employer works for Zulkir Thrul.

The character is a political activist who understands that when powerful nations fall under the yoke of tyranny, the whole world suffers. They've traveled to Eltabbar to investigate rumors that Szass Tam seeks to regain his regency.

entries.name: Character Level
entries: The Recommended Character Levels table indicates the level characters should be when they begin each chapter.

At designated points in the campaign, the characters should have enough XP to reach the required level for the next part of the story. If you're using a method of level advancement that doesn't rely on XP, the characters gain a level when the campaign says so.

data.name: Chapter 3: Operation Deadfall
entries: {@i Embark on a mission to defeat Szass Tam}.

entries.title: Malefites attack Eltabbar's bazaar.

entries.name: Key Plot Points
entries: The following information is key to this chapter's story:

items.name: Malefite Attack
items.entry: Malefites attack Eltabbar's Bazaar Ward. After the monsters are dispatched, the characters are summoned to a nearby tailor shop, Wrynn's Bespoke Vestments. There, Zulkir {@creature Xelnene Thrul|AUD} recruits them into Operation Deadfall: a secret undertaking to undermine and defeat {@creature Szass Tam|AUD}.

items.name: First Tasks
items.entry: The zulkir tasks the characters with neutralizing three spies key to Szass Tam's operations: a gambler, a landlord, and a racketeer.

items.name: Turn the Courier
items.entry: The zulkir then orders the characters to infiltrate the headquarters of Szass Tam's intel courier. There, they can force him to provide information vital to their cause or kill him.

entries.name: Preparation
entries: Before running this chapter, prepare as follows:

items.name: Step 1
items.entry: Read the "{@area Running This Chapter|0aa|x}" section, including "{@area Character Advancement|0ab|x}."

items.name: Step 2
items.entry: Familiarize yourself with the Key NPCs table below. Two NPCs—{@area Xelnene Thrul|379|x} and {@area Wynston Wrynn|0bf|x}—recur throughout the campaign, while others might make repeat appearances.

items.name: Step 3
items.entry: Bookmark the stat blocks below, which appear in the {@book Monster Manual|XMM} and on D&D Beyond unless otherwise noted. If a stat block appears in appendix B, an asterisk appears after its name:

entries.caption: Key NPCs
rows: Szass Tam's intel courier and owner of Two Plateaus Shipping Company
Human owner of a gambling den
Human Red Wizard, gambler, and spy target
Human tailor and Zulkir Thrul's spy master
Human zulkir of evocation and Operation Deadfall leader

entries.name: Campaign Background
entries: As the campaign begins, the characters are in {@area Eltabbar|063|x}, the capital of Thay. Thayan politics are always volatile, but the current atmosphere feels like a powder keg.

The lich {@book Szass Tam|XDMG|8|Szass Tam}, zulkir of necromancy, has recently made several alarming public proclamations. Pointing to hostile neighbors and the dangers of unchecked magical experimentation at home, Szass Tam demanded the other zulkirs reestablish his regency to protect Thay and help it grow richer from its magic item trade. They balked but made no public response. Surprisingly, Szass Tam then went silent; no one has seen or heard from him for some time.

Unknown to any but Zulkir {@creature Xelnene Thrul|AUD}, who opposes the lich wholeheartedly, Szass Tam has retreated to Thaymount to prepare for a heinous ritual he calls Malefice Mortum. (See {@area chapter 2|084|x} for more information about his plot.) Soon, the characters will become embroiled in a struggle to stop Szass Tam and save Thay from certain doom.

entries.name: Running This Chapter
entries: This chapter begins as the characters wander through the Bazaar Ward in Eltabbar, depicted on map 1.2 in chapter 1. "{@area Eltabbar, Thay's Capital|063|x}" in chapter 1 includes numerous places the characters might want to visit during this chapter, such as shops, taverns, and an inn.

entries.name: Character Advancement
entries: The characters should be level 11 when this chapter begins. They should have enough XP to advance to level 12 before they embark on their second mission. They should reach level 13 by the end of this chapter. If you're using a method of level advancement that doesn't rely on XP, the characters gain levels at these points.

entries.name: Terror at the Bazaar
entries: In recent weeks, Szass Tam's experiments using the foul magic of his Malefice Mortum ritual have created rampaging hordes of malefites throughout Thay, including many in Eltabbar. One such horde—a {@creature death tyrant|XMM} and {@creature Skeleton|XMM|skeletons}—awakened deep in the {@book Underdark|XDMG|8|Underdark, The} beneath the capital. The death tyrant drove the group through a passage that led to the Bazaar Ward's canals to vent their Abyss-fueled murderousness on the living above.

When the campaign begins, ask the players why their characters are browsing Eltabbar's Bazaar Ward together. Perhaps they seek a specific trinket or want to enjoy one of Eltabbar's most luxurious wards on this energetic Market First Day. Whatever the reason, the characters wander through the part of the bazaar shown on map 3.1.
Read or paraphrase the following:

The city's trees are blossoming, cranes flock to the canals, and permanent weather magic brings gentle rain and warm breezes. It's the first day of the month of Tarsakh, and the bazaar's merchants have just unveiled a new batch of goods and attractive discounts.
The market is crowded with shoppers—Medium and Small {@creature Commoner|XMM|Commoners} and {@creature Noble|XMM|Nobles} of various species.

entries.name: Bazaar Features
entries: This section of the bazaar is situated on a bridge that spans a canal in the center of the Bazaar Ward. The bridge section of the bazaar has the following features.

entries.name: Buildings
entries: Two buildings lie to the south. The buildings' doors are unlocked.

entries.name: Lin's Capes and Cloaks
entries: To the west is Lin's Capes and Cloaks, a shop that specializes in fashionable outerwear. Proprietor Teeva Lin (Medium {@creature Noble|XMM}), a genial and cultured human, sells nonmagical pieces ranging in cost from 10 GP to 500 GP.
She also has magic garments for sale, whose costs are listed in parentheses:

entries.name: The Jeweled Crane
entries: To the east is the Jeweled Crane, which specializes in nonmagical brooches. Made from gold decorated with precious gemstones, these pieces cost anywhere from 100 GP to 1,000 GP apiece. Jeweler Garend Gil (Medium {@creature Noble|XMM}), a self-absorbed human, owns the shop.

entries.name: Fruit Displays
entries: On the bridge's eastern half are four displays of fresh fruits, including apricots, pears, plums, and pomegranates. The displays are tended by the gregarious elf Jayleen (Medium {@creature Noble|XMM}), who hand-selects the produce from farmers every day. Individual fruits cost 1 SP.

entries.name: Supply Cart
entries: A cart with cleaning supplies stands in the northeast corner. The cart provides {@table Cover|XPHB|Half Cover} to anyone behind it.

entries.name: Tents
entries: Merchants have erected several tents along this portion of the bridge. Each sells merchandise as described below.

entries.name: Northern Tents
entries: The tents along the north side of the bridge display bolts of beautiful textiles in all colors but red, including silk and satin brocade. These are the wares of the orc Ven Terrytooth (Medium {@creature Noble|XMM}), who chats genially with customers and brags about his good relationship with several Red Wizards. Each bolt of cloth weighs 1 pound and costs between 10 GP and 30 GP.

entries.name: Central Tents
entries: The central tents display {@item Spyglass|XPHB|Spyglasses}, from simple pieces made with polished steel to ones fashioned from gold encrusted with gemstones. The serious and bespectacled human Val Vann (Medium {@creature Noble|XMM}) tends to the wares, which her grandfather crafts in their home in the Mages' Ward. The Spyglasses cost from 1,000 GP to 5,000 GP.

entries.name: Southeastern Tent
entries: The southeastern tent displays precious spices, including cloves, cinnamon, cardamom, and saffron. The intellectual proprietor, a human named Meri (Medium {@creature Noble|XMM}), sells the spices in 1-pound jars. Jars of cloves or cinnamon each cost 3 GP, while jars of cardamom and saffron each cost 15 GP.

entries.name: Malefite Attack
entries: Allow the characters to interact with NPCs in the bazaar for a few minutes. Then read or paraphrase the following:

Bloodcurdling screams fill the air as the crowd suddenly flees east in a panic. You decipher a warning cry amid the chaos: "Skeletons! Run for your lives!" Half a dozen skeletons, their eyes glowing green, advance while swinging rusty blades.

Shambling across the bridge are six {@creature Skeleton|XMM|Skeletons} that were raised in one of Szass Tam's recent experiments. The skeletons fight the characters and anyone near them on the bridge, focusing on the characters after the first character acts.

On {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} count 0 of the second round of combat (losing ties), a {@creature Death Tyrant|XMM} erupts from the canal and flies toward the characters. Read or paraphrase the following:
Bursting from the canal is an enormous, flying orb of desiccated flesh, its slavering maw filled with gnashing teeth. Its single eye glows with green energy.
The death tyrant, whose lair is in the {@book Underdark|XDMG|8|Underdark, The}, fights the characters until destroyed.

entries.name: Fleeing Crowd
entries: Thirty vendors, customers, and bystanders are on the bridge when the attack begins. They try to flee during the first round of combat, making the bridge {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} during that time.

entries.name: Development
entries: If combat lasts more than 6 rounds, five human Red Wizards (Medium {@creature Archmage|XMM|Archmages}) who belong to the City Watch rush onto the scene to dispatch the monsters. After the battle, these Red Wizards grumble about increasing incidents involving strange undead monsters, but they refuse to answer any questions from the crowd or the characters.
The watch members immediately depart the area. If civilians are dead or injured (see "After the Attack"), the Red Wizards say they aren't versed in healing magic and promise to send healers.

entries.name: After the Attack
entries: It's up to you whether civilians are injured or die in this attack. If the characters acted heroically, you might decide everyone in the crowd escapes. If the characters fled the attack, you might decide some of or all the civilians on the bridge die.

entries.name: Shaken Crowd
entries: No matter how the characters acted, the crowd returns to the bridge after the attack while vendors clean up the disarray.

If the characters defeated the monsters without the City Watch's help, Jayleen (see "{@area Fruit Displays|0b2|x}") thanks them profusely and offers them as much free fruit as they want. The other vendors and shoppers also hail the characters as heroes.

entries.name: Mysterious Messenger

entries.title: Wynston Wrynn

entries: A human man with long hair and a neatly trimmed beard, dressed in beautifully made clothing, approaches a character of your choice.
The man clasps the character's hand, into which he places a small piece of folded parchment. He says only, "I'm glad I found you, my friends," before walking away.
The man is Wynston Wrynn (Medium, Neutral Good {@creature Spy Master|XMM}), who came to the bridge to deliver the parchment and witnessed the battle's last moments.

If the characters follow Wrynn after he hands them the parchment, the man asks them to accompany him. He won't divulge details, but he promises that an offer awaits them that they'll want to consider.

entries.name: The Parchment
entries: The parchment contains a note written by Zulkir Xelnene Thrul, whom the characters meet later in this chapter. The zulkir has cast the {@spell Illusory Script|XPHB} spell on the parchment; to anyone but the characters, the note looks like a list of grocery items.
When the characters unfold the parchment, give the players a copy of the Mysterious Note handout.

entries.title: Handout: Mysterious Note

entries.name: Development
entries: Wrynn's Bespoke Vestments is a few blocks northeast. Any characters from Eltabbar recognize the name of the shop and know its location. Otherwise, the party can learn the shop's location from any bystander.

entries.name: Wrynn's Bespoke Vestments
entries: Wrynn's Bespoke Vestments has stood in the heart of Eltabbar's Bazaar Ward for centuries. This family-owned tailor shop has a sterling reputation for selling fashionable and beautifully made clothes. The shop has a coveted license to produce red clothing for Red Wizards.

For the last twenty years, the tailor shop also has clandestinely served as headquarters for the spy operations of {@area Xelnene Thrul|379|x}, zulkir of evocation. Seventh-generation shop owner Wynston Wrynn is the zulkir's spy master. Thrul visits the shop only in disguises she crafts using the {@spell Alter Self|XPHB} spell or by using the {@spell Teleport|XPHB} spell to arrive in a secret back room.

entries.name: Shop Features
entries: The shop has the following features.

entries.name: Ceilings
entries: The shop's ceilings are 15 feet high.

entries.name: Doors
entries: The shop's doors are made of wood. Secret doors (marked with an {@i S} on the map; {@dc 20} to notice) lead to Wrynn's office ({@area area W3|0d1|x}). The front door has a lock; it's Complex (1 minute to pick) and of Superior quality ({@dc 20}). (See "Doors" in the {@book Dungeon Master's Guide|XDMG|2|Doors}.)

entries.name: Hours of Operation
entries: The shop remains open with its front doors unlocked from sunup to sundown unless Wrynn has left the building. In that case, the tailor places a sign that says "Please return later" on the front door, which he locks.

entries.name: Lighting
entries: Picture windows along the shop's western walls bathe the display and fitting areas ({@area area W1|0ca|x}) in {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} during the day. In the workshop and secret office (areas {@area W2|0cf|x} and {@area W3|0d1|x}), sconces with {@spell Continual Flame|XPHB} spells cast on them emit {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB}.

entries.name: Valuables
entries: A cashbox holds coins in {@area area W1|0ca|x}, and {@area area W3|0d1|x} holds coins and gems. If Wrynn discovers the characters have stolen any of these, he politely asks for their return. If the characters refuse, the next time they talk with Zulkir Thrul (see "{@area How to Meet with the Zulkir|0e0|x}"), she demands the valuables' return on threat of dismissal from her service.

entries.name: Shop Locations
entries: The following locations are keyed to map 3.2.

entries.name: W1: Display and Fitting Areas

entries: Beams of natural light illuminate this elegant shop. Racks of beautiful clothing for all genders stand near the entrance, where an orc man and an elf woman browse. On a desk to the east are a stack of parchment, an ink pot, and a quill.

Farther into the shop, mannequins dressed in tasteful satins, silks, cottons, and corduroys stand near tall windows, while a stepped dais in the shop's center features dressing mirrors. Two humans, a man and a woman in well-tailored waistcoats with measuring tapes draped around their necks, each adjust a mannequin's outfit.
The display and fitting space is the shop's primary area. Curtained changing areas flank the dais.

entries.name: Bystanders
entries: See "{@area Private Audience|0d4|x}" for what happens when the characters enter this area.

entries.name: Front Desk
entries: Wrynn or his employees record purchases and provide customers with receipts at the front desk. In a drawer is an unlocked cashbox with the day's earnings; there are 2,500 GP inside.

entries.name: Clothing Costs
entries: There are fifty sets of {@item Fine Clothes|XPHB} in the shop in addition to other custom clothing pieces. Prices range from 5 GP for a small piece, such as a silk scarf or neckerchief, to 5,000 GP for sets of items. Customers must request prices for custom items from Wrynn or his employees.

entries.name: W2: Workshop

entries: A long worktable and racks fill this cramped but organized space. Arranged meticulously on the table are shears, chalk, awls, needles, thread, and measuring tapes, along with folded piles of clothing. A stack of leather-bound ledgers sits on a shelf along the western wall.
Wrynn performs custom tailoring in this workspace; most production work occurs elsewhere. The ledgers note transactions for the last six months.

entries.name: W3: Secret Office

entries: This tidy room includes a desk in the southeast corner and tables along the east and west walls. The tables hold neatly arranged stacks of coins and open sacks of gemstones.
The valuables in this room are payments from wealthy clients. Stacked on the desk is business correspondence.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: There are 25,000 GP in various coins here on the tables, as well as gemstones worth 10,000 GP in total.

entries.name: Private Audience
entries: Browsing the shop's wares is an orc man—actually Zulkir Thrul under the effects of an {@spell Alter Self|XPHB} spell—who ignores the characters until Wrynn beckons them into his workshop.

The other browser is a terse elf named Gerleine (Medium {@creature Noble|XMM}), who announces, "Wynston, I've decided." She carries a blue satin frock to the desk along the north wall and pays the tailor, who writes her a receipt before she leaves.

The human man and woman are Wrynn's employees, Cora Finn and Tate Vonn. After Gerleine leaves the shop, Wrynn approaches his two employees and quietly asks them to take a break. They also leave the shop.

Once the characters, Wrynn, and the disguised Xelnene Thrul are the only people in the shop, the tailor places a sign that says "Please return later" outside the front door. He approaches the characters.
Read or paraphrase the following:

"My name is Wynston Wrynn, and I own this shop," the man says in a warm voice. "I respect the trust you have extended by meeting me here. However, before we can speak candidly, I ask you to extend that trust a bit further. Please follow me." The man gestures to the nearby orc before adding, "This man is with us."

Wrynn and the disguised zulkir then step into the workshop ({@area area W2|0cf|x}) and slip into the secret office ({@area area W3|0d1|x}), beckoning the characters to follow. If the characters seem suspicious or balk, the tailor assures them again about a promising offer, emphasizes the importance of this meeting, and asks for their trust.

In the secret office, the disguised zulkir waves her hands in a complex pattern, and a shadowy door appears on the east wall; Thrul has cast the {@spell Demiplane|XPHB} spell. Wrynn and the zulkir step through the door, again beckoning the characters to follow.

entries.name: Zulkir Thrul's Demiplane
entries: When the characters walk through the shadowy door, read or paraphrase the following:

Sconces shed soft, yellow light over this beautifully furnished office, which boasts oak furniture upholstered in maroon velvet. A gleaming desk sits to the south, along with nearby seats and a plush armchair. A wraparound sofa and a table bearing crystal wineglasses sit to the north across from a cozy armchair nook.

The demiplane's layout appears on map 3.3. The wood-paneled space is bathed in {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} from wall sconces with {@spell Continual Flame|XPHB} spells cast on them. From this office, Zulkir Xelnene Thrul—assisted by Wynston Wrynn—conducts her clandestine activities. The desk's drawers hold encoded dossiers supporting those activities.

After walking through the door, the disguised zulkir settles into the chair behind the desk. Wrynn sits in the armchair beside her. Once the characters are ready to hear the zulkir's proposal, read or paraphrase the following:

The orc man lifts his head regally and closes his eyes. When he opens them, his appearance transforms. You now see a pale human woman with piercing blue eyes and a shaved head covered in tattoos. She wears the unmistakable red robes of a Red Wizard.

"Thank you for your patience," the woman says in a strong, mellifluous voice. "I am Xelnene Thrul, Red Wizard sage and Thay's zulkir of evocation. You've already met Wynston Wrynn, my spy master and the man I trust most in this world.

"I have invited you here to discuss a matter of utmost importance. I won't waste words: I intend to hire you to stop the lich Szass Tam, zulkir of necromancy, before he unleashes destruction on Thay and murders or subjugates all who resist him. This enterprise will be long, dangerous, and—if successful—without public recognition. But it is necessary to save countless lives. You may ask me any questions you have before you give me your answer."
If the characters are unfamiliar with Thay's zulkir council or with {@book Szass Tam|XDMG|8|Szass Tam}, Thrul shares the information about those topics presented in {@area chapter 1|017|x}.

entries.title: Zulkir Xelnene Thrul and her spy master, Wynston Wrynn, seek to recruit the characters.

entries: Thrul can provide the following information about Operation Deadfall:

items.name: Why Target Szass Tam/Why Is Thay in Danger?
items.entry: The zulkir shares the information in "{@area Demonic Ritual|084|x}" and "{@area Thay's Only Hope|087|x}" in chapter 2. "The terrible attack you witnessed today at the bazaar is merely a by-product of Szass Tam's plan. As you can see, he is no longer content with simply sitting on Thay's ruling zulkir council. He seeks to become Thay's tyrant once more, and if he succeeds, his obscene servants will kill thousands. Thay will fall yet again into generations of suffering. Even death will not be a reprieve for Szass Tam's victims; he'll simply raise them as undead horrors to serve his whims. We can't allow this to happen."

items.name: What Are You Paying?
items.entry: "If you agree, I'll pay you each a topaz worth 500 GP today. Consider it a down payment. After you complete each mission, I'll give your group a magic item of your choice from this list." The zulkir gives the characters the list of magic items in "{@area Mission Rewards|0da|x}" below. "You may also keep any money and magic items you find during your service. If you defeat Szass Tam, we will discuss a further reward."

items.name: Are We in Danger If We Join the Operation?
items.entry: "Szass Tam has spies everywhere. If any catch wind of your involvement, they'll hunt you down and kill you. Szass Tam will hunt me down, too."

items.name: What's the Plan for the Operation?
items.entry: "First, you will undermine Szass Tam's spy network. Once his spy network is disrupted, you will gather allies to our cause. Finally, you will confront the lich and stop his ongoing ritual. You may try to kill him, but stopping his ritual is more important."

items.name: What's in It for You?
items.entry: "If Szass Tam's ritual succeeds and he seizes leadership, some zulkirs might ally with him to save themselves. I am unwilling to do this. Szass Tam is evil, and I will not turn a blind eye to his murderous ways. For my resistance, he will certainly kill me. If you succeed, I live and keep my position on the council—but more importantly, you'll prevent immense suffering for Thay's people. I would gladly die for my nation, and I refuse to allow it to fall into Szass Tam's hands again. This is why I need your help."

items.name: Who Else Is Part of the Operation?
items.entry: "Only you, should you agree, as well as me and Wynston. I have other operatives, but they know nothing of this operation."

items.name: Won't Szass Tam Revive If We Kill Him?
items.entry: "Normally, he'd revive in a matter of days. However, my scholars believe interrupting his ritual would require the lich to start it anew, setting him back years. In addition, I will ask you to retrieve an item that would keep the lich dead for one hundred years—more than enough time for Thay to fortify its defenses should Szass Tam try to return to power later."

items.name: Why Not Confront Szass Tam Yourself?
items.entry: "I can't confront Szass Tam myself and hope to win. No one zulkir—or even three or four zulkirs—could. All seven of us would need to unite against the lich. I've tried to form such an alliance, but Szass Tam has undermined my credibility with them. I have shown them as much proof as I can, to no avail. Alas, we must handle this situation discreetly and on our own. We are Thay's only chance."

items.name: Why Recruit Us?
items.entry: "Your considerable skills have come to my attention. I believe you would be excellent operatives and that you are up to this task." If the characters dislike Szass Tam or are dedicated to Thay, Thrul tells them these factors make them attractive candidates, too. If the characters acted heroically to defeat the undead earlier in the chapter, she points to this as proof of their capabilities.

items.name: What If We Say No?
items.entry: "I will wipe your memory with a {@spell Modify Memory|XPHB} spell, and this conversation will never have happened."

entries: Once Thrul answers the characters' questions, read or paraphrase the following:
The zulkir steeples her fingers together and fixes you with a serious stare.
"So, adventurers, what is your answer? There is no turning back once you agree. Respond wisely."
When the characters agree to join Operation Deadfall, Thrul gives a small smile and hands each of them a topaz, as promised.

entries.name: Mission Rewards
entries: Each time the characters complete a mission, Thrul will give the group one magic item listed below. The characters can tell Wrynn which item they've chosen anytime after completing the mission, but they can't choose the same item twice. They receive their reward via anonymous courier before the end of the following day.
The zulkir's list follows:

entries.name: Operation Deadfall
entries: Read or paraphrases the following:
Zulkir Thrul leans forward, the gravity of her words reflected in her formal tone and posture.

"Thank you for joining this cause. You're now operatives of Operation Deadfall. Before I describe the parameters of our undertaking, think of code names for yourselves and your group. Wynston and I will refer to you by these code names at all times; we will never use your real names.

"Refer to Wynston as the Sparrow. Refer to me as the Crane. Szass Tam is the Hydra. When outside this office, always use these code names. We will assign code names to other targets and goals as needed.

"Above all, this operation is secret. You must never reveal anything about Operation Deadfall to anyone unless I authorize it. You may ask questions of no one but myself or the Sparrow, and always discreetly.
"Publicly, you don't know me or the Sparrow, and we don't know you. Remember, the Hydra's eyes are everywhere."

entries.name: Code Names
entries: Thrul uses code names with all her operatives, not just for Operation Deadfall. Using code names for Operation Deadfall's objectives will help ensure the characters don't mention key mission details in public.
If your players struggle to come up with code names, help them using the guidance in "{@area Code Names|093|x}" in chapter 2.
The zulkir then lays out the following parameters of Operation Deadfall.

entries.name: How to Meet with the Zulkir
entries: Once the characters have chosen their code names, Zulkir Thrul addresses them again. Read or paraphrase the following:

"I will assign you missions in this office. When you have completed a mission, return to the shop in disguise. Disguise yourselves differently each time. The Sparrow will know who you are. Request your reward from him, and give him any intel you found to pass on. He will contact you when it's time for our next meeting. When you arrive here for the meeting, he will contact me. I will appear in the shop shortly, and we will enter this office in the same manner as today. After you report about your previous mission, I will give you details about the next.
"When the time is right, you will confront the Hydra. All your missions leading to that moment will assist you in this task."

To help with their disguises, Thrul gives each character a {@item Masquerader's Brooch|AUD} (see {@area appendix A|341|x}) shaped like a crane, an animal frequently depicted in Thayan artwork and fashion. She tells the characters always to incorporate a white crane feather into their disguises when they visit the shop to help Wrynn identify them.

She also gives the characters one of a pair of {@item Sending Stone|AI|Sending Stones}; the stone has an image of a sparrow carved on it. She tells them that Wrynn has the other stone but instructs them to use the stone to contact him only when necessary. The zulkir forbids the characters from contacting her directly.

entries.name: If the Party's Cover Is Blown
entries: The zulkir informs the characters that she reserves the right to dismiss them from her service if they don't remain clandestine. If she dismisses them, she will use {@spell Modify Memory|XPHB} or a {@item Spell Scroll|XDMG} {@i of} {@spell Wish|XPHB} to wipe their memories.
If Thrul dismisses the characters, the campaign ends for them. See "{@area Importance of Secrecy|099|x}" in chapter 2 for more about what happens if characters don't maintain secrecy.
If the characters worry about keeping Operation Deadfall secret, share the advice for staying clandestine from "{@area Running a Magical Spy Thriller|091|x}" in chapter 2.

entries.name: First Mission

entries: Once the characters understand Operation Deadfall's parameters, read or paraphrase the following:
"Your first mission, operatives, is to neutralize three of the Hydra's spies," says Zulkir Thrul. "Doing so will ensure our future activities avoid suspicion.

"One spy, the Gambler, reports disloyal Red Wizards. Another, the Landlord, informs on the Hydra's business rivals. The third, the Racketeer, informs on activists who oppose the Hydra's return to regency. Anyone deemed a threat is killed.

"I will divulge everything I know about these individuals, including where to find them. I care not how you neutralize them, as long as they cease working for the Hydra. If you gain assurance from a target that they'll stop spying or leave the city, tell the Sparrow, and he will dispatch other operatives to ensure the target's honesty."
"Report back here when you have completed this mission. As always, this conversation never happened."
Thrul then shares the following details about the three targets.

entries.name: The Gambler
entries: Thrul tells the characters the following about the Gambler:

items.name: Name
items.entry: The Gambler's real name is Thellania Marr.

items.name: Physical Description
items.entry: Marr is a human with a shaved and tattooed head, and tattoos on her face and arms. She wears red robes and a cape with spiked shoulders.

items.name: Target Details
items.entry: Marr is a Red Wizard who works for Szass Tam. She informs his agents about Red Wizards who oppose the lich's desire to regain his regency.

items.name: Neutralization Benefit
items.entry: If Marr is neutralized, public dissent against Szass Tam will increase among Red Wizards. More importantly, should rumors of Operation Deadfall emerge, Szass Tam's suspicion will likely shift toward publicly dissenting Red Wizards and away from Thrul and her agents.

items.name: How to Neutralize
items.entry: Thrul knows where Marr participates in illegal gambling in the evenings. The games take place in the back room of a small bar in the Apprentices' Ward called the Hooded Lantern, to which the zulkir gives the characters directions. Thrul suggests the characters approach Marr at the Hooded Lantern and convince her to stop working for Szass Tam.

entries: When the characters are ready to confront the Gambler, see "{@area The Hooded Lantern|0ed|x}."

entries.name: The Landlord
entries: Thrul tells the characters the following about the Landlord:

items.name: Name
items.entry: The Landlord's real name is Pryas Nym.

items.name: Physical Description
items.entry: Nym is a bald human who sports a heavy blond beard.

items.name: Target Details
items.entry: Nym is a landlord and magical goods inspector who informs Szass Tam's agents about influential merchants who disparage the lich's bid for the Thayan regency.

items.name: Neutralization Benefit
items.entry: If Nym is neutralized, public dissent against Szass Tam will increase among merchants. Reports of the lich's sabotage of business rivals might also emerge, weakening his political support.

items.name: How to Neutralize
items.entry: Nym owns an apartment building in Eltab's Ward called Nym Building 3, to which Thrul gives the characters directions. Each night, Nym goes door to door to harass those who are late paying rent. Thrul suggests the characters approach Nym during his rounds and convince him to stop working for Szass Tam.

entries: When the characters are ready to confront the Landlord, see "{@area Nym Building 3.|102|x}"

entries.name: The Racketeer
entries: Thrul tells the characters the following about the Racketeer:

items.name: Name
items.entry: The Racketeer's real name is Rathan Jur.

items.name: Physical Description
items.entry: Jur is a bald goliath who wears studded leather armor and wields a scimitar.

items.name: Target Details
items.entry: Jur is an extortionist and cousin to several Red Wizards. Jur offers "protection" from these Red Wizards, but in reality, he and his goons use that excuse to extort money from a large neighborhood. Szass Tam recently demanded these Red Wizards' loyalty, and in turn, the mages have instructed Jur to find out who opposes Szass Tam's plan to regain Thay's regency.

items.name: Neutralization Benefit
items.entry: Jur's intel has led to the deaths of multiple wealthy neighborhood activists, among whom were Thrul's key informants on Szass Tam's movements in Eltabbar. If Jur is neutralized, activists will feel safer and Thrul will stop losing informants.

items.name: How to Neutralize
items.entry: Thrul knows the location of an alley in the Lower Ward where Jur and his goons meet with his extortion victims every evening. Thrul suggests the characters approach Jur there and convince him to stop working for Szass Tam.

entries: When the characters are ready to confront the Racketeer, see "{@area Lower Ward Alley|115|x}."

entries.name: Leaving the Demiplane
entries: Once the characters join Operation Deadfall and receive their first mission, each character earns 4,100 XP.

When the characters leave the demiplane, Wrynn and Thrul follow. The zulkir dismisses her {@spell Demiplane|XPHB} spell, and the door in {@area area W3|0d1|x} disappears. She casts the {@spell Teleport|XPHB} spell and departs, while Wrynn remains in his office.

entries.name: Speaking with Wynston Wrynn
entries: If the characters want to know more about Wrynn, he chats with them in his secret office ({@area area W3|0d1|x}).

entries.name: Wrynn's Family
entries: The tailor's family has owned and operated this shop for seven generations. The Wrynns are a respected family among Eltabbar's artisans, renowned for the high-quality clothes they make for the city's wealthy merchants, Red Wizards, and elite families.

entries.name: Wrynn's Story
entries: Wrynn has always had a deep sense of right and wrong, and he hates the injustices evil Red Wizards visit on the populace. He hates Szass Tam even more; to Wrynn, the only thing worse than inflicting suffering and death on innocents is using necromancy to animate their bodies to commit more terror. Reserved and eminently self-controlled, Wrynn learned as a child that it's better to keep one's strong feelings hidden while working in the background to effect change.

Wrynn and Thrul crossed paths as youths at the Tower of the Arcane in the Apprentices' Ward. Thrul was already promised to a powerful Red Wizard as an apprentice. The two bonded over their mutual dislike of state-sanctioned cruelty and their commitment to a fairer Thay. Thrul recognized Wrynn's potential as an operative even then, and once she ascended in the Red Wizards' ranks, she made him her spy master. Wrynn regards Thrul as an older sister and considers her family, as she does him.

entries.name: Order of Operations
entries: You can run "The Hooded Lantern," "Nym Building 3," and "Lower Ward Alley" in any order. Allow the characters to choose the order they want to confront the spies in.

entries.name: The Hooded Lantern
entries: The grimy tavern known as the Hooded Lantern is on the northern side of the Apprentices' Ward along one of the city's many canals. The tavern's water comes from the canal, and the constant groaning of the waterwheel behind the building reverberates throughout the tavern. This conceals the sound of the gamblers in the back room. Gambling is legal in Eltabbar as long as gambling houses pay heavy taxes; this tavern doesn't pay the taxes.

entries.name: The Hooded Lantern Features
entries: The Hooded Lantern has the following features.

entries.name: Canal
entries: The canal's water level is 10 feet below street level. The water is 10 feet deep.

entries.name: Ceilings
entries: The tavern's ceilings are 15 feet high.

entries.name: Constant Din
entries: Because several buildings on this block use it to supply water, the waterwheel outside the tavern operates nonstop, creating an awful din of grinding and screeching. As a result, inside the tavern, Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks that rely on hearing are made with {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}.

entries.name: Doors
entries: The tavern's doors are made of wood. The front door remains unlocked while the establishment is open, from dawn until midnight. When the place is closed, the front door is locked. The doors to the storeroom and gambling den (areas {@area H2|0fa|x} and {@area H3|0fc|x}) are locked whether the tavern is open or closed. All locks are Simple (1 action to pick) and of Superior quality ({@dc 20}). The bartender Knudrek (see {@area area H1|0f6|x}) has keys for all doors.

entries.name: Lighting
entries: Small sconces throughout the tavern cast {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} in interior areas. The grimy windows let in little natural light.

entries.name: Windows
entries: The tavern has three unlocked windows: a window on the east side of the barroom and another on the west ({@area area H1|0f6|x}), and a window above the water basin in the storage room ({@area area H2|0fa|x}). Medium or smaller characters who want to climb through them can do so easily.

entries.name: The Hooded Lantern Locations
entries: The following locations are keyed to map 3.4. Descriptions assume the characters visit the tavern in the evening, when gambling goes on. If they visit the tavern earlier, they see the people described in the gambling den ({@area area H3|0fc|x}) enter the establishment.

entries.name: H1: Barroom

entries: High-top stools line a bar to the north. Two cloaked patrons sit at a nearby table, clutching drinks. Behind the bar stands a burly human man wearing an apron, his face lined with scars and wrinkles.

The human bartender is Knudrek (Medium {@creature Gladiator|XMM}). The orc patrons, Strak and Gert (Medium {@creature Commoner|XMM|Commoners}), glower at the characters and provide one-word answers if anyone attempts conversation with them. They are custodians who work nearby and just want everyone to leave them alone. If a fight breaks out, Strak and Gert flee.

Knudrek was renowned as a gladiator in the city, but he has long since retired. He now runs this tavern and the gambling den in the back room ({@area area H3|0fc|x}), taking a cut of the money that changes hands. He pays no taxes on that income.

On his apron, Knudrek wears a faded badge depicting two muscular, interlocking arms. A character examining the badge can take the {@action Study|XPHB} action and make a {@dc 12} Intelligence ({@skill History|XPHB}) check. On a success, the character realizes the badge represents a local gladiatorial league called Elite Gladiators.

entries.name: Chatting with Knudrek
entries: When the characters enter, Knudrek nods to them but offers no welcome. Patrons can purchase three different types of ale for 1 SP each.

If the characters ask about gambling here, Knudrek denies any knowledge unless they mention his badge and speak favorably about the city's gladiators. Knudrek then reveals he was once a grappler in Elite Gladiators, as well as the information below.

entries.name: Joining the Gambling
entries: As an {@action Influence|XPHB} action, a character can try to convince Knudrek to let them gamble and make a {@dc 15} Charisma ({@skill Deception|XPHB} or {@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) check. On a success, Knudrek invites them to the game in the back room ({@area area H3|0fc|x}). Entry costs 25 GP per person.
If they pay the fee, Knudrek escorts them to the gambling den.

entries.name: H2: Storage
entries: The door to this room is locked (see "{@area The Hooded Lantern Features|0f2|x}").
This room holds kegs of ale and shelves for crates of mugs and other miscellany.
A window in the northwest wall above a water basin overlooks the canal.

entries.name: H3: Gambling Den

entries.title: From Left to Right: the Gamblers Belinda, Thellania Marr, Gilda, and Terk.

entries: The door to this room is locked (see "{@area The Hooded Lantern Features|0f2|x}").

Around a long table sit four people: a white-haired human woman in purple robes with a lizard sitting on her knee, a bearded human man wearing a heavy cloak, a brawny orc woman wearing heavy armor, and a human woman with a shaved head wearing the distinctive robes of a Red Wizard. The four are playing cards, placing money and magic items on the table as collateral.
These are the gamblers:

items.name: Belinda
items.entry: Belinda (Medium {@creature Cultist Fanatic|XMM}) is a white-haired human woman.

items.name: Gilda
items.entry: Gilda (Medium {@creature Assassin|XMM}) is an orc woman.

items.name: Terk
items.entry: Terk (Medium {@creature Assassin|XMM}) is a human man.

items.name: Thellania Marr
items.entry: This human Red Wizard (Medium {@creature Cultist Hierophant|XMM}) is the characters' target.

entries: The gamblers play a card game called three wizards, in which the highest-ranking hand after three rounds of play wins.

If Knudrek escorts the characters, the gamblers welcome them. Otherwise, a character can claim the bartender has allowed them to gamble. The character must take the {@action Influence|XPHB} action and make a {@dc 16} Charisma ({@skill Deception|XPHB}) check. On a success, the gamblers welcome the characters into the game. On a failure, the gamblers begin combat.

If combat happens while Knudrek isn't in this area, he hears the commotion and enters the fight at the beginning of the third round of combat, insisting the characters leave. All combatants fight to the death.

entries.name: Speaking with Thellania
entries: If the characters want to speak with Thellania, she says one of them must win a game before she'll talk to them. The gamblers tell the characters one person from their group can play at a time; the others must watch.

To win a game, a character must bet 400 GP or an Uncommon magic item and make three {@dc 12} Charisma ({@skill Deception|XPHB}) or Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB}) checks. On three successes, the character wins back their collateral plus 1,600 GP. Thellania also agrees to speak with the characters in the barroom ({@area area H1|0f6|x}) or outside, as the characters choose. (She will not speak with them in the gambling den.) On a failure, she ignores the characters.
Each character may play one game. Afterward, Knudrek or the gamblers ask them to leave, but tell them if they want to play more, they can come back the next night before the game starts.
The gamblers stay in the tavern for another two hours. Thellania stays to gather her belongings, then leaves five minutes after the other gamblers.

entries.name: Neutralizing the Gambler
entries: Thellania isn't particularly loyal to Szass Tam. A character can take the {@action Influence|XPHB} action to try to convince her to stop spying. The character makes a {@dc 15} Charisma ({@skill Intimidation|XPHB} or {@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) check; if they give Thellania a magic item that's Rare or rarer, the check automatically succeeds.

On a success, Thellania promises to stop spying and keeps her word. If the characters press her, she agrees to leave town temporarily and allows the characters to escort her to the city gates as a guarantee. On a failure, Thellania begins combat.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: Thellania wears a {@item Heward's Handy Haversack|XDMG} with 500 GP within it.
Bets from previous rounds on the table include the following:

items: Two {@item Elemental Gem|XDMG|Elemental Gems} (emerald and red corundum)

entries.name: Development
entries: If the characters kill Thellania or convince her to stop spying, Thellania is neutralized as a spy, and each character earns 4,100 XP.

entries.name: Nym Building 3
entries: Nym Building 3, a drab, two-story apartment building in Eltab's Ward, is adjacent to the River Eltar. The building's owner, Pryas Nym, owns several similar structures across the city. Of Nym's holdings, this building lies in the city's poorest neighborhood. He enjoys making nightly rounds to intimidate tenants and harass those whose rent is late.

entries.name: Nym Building 3 Features
entries: The building has the following features.

entries.name: Apartment Layout and Residents
entries: Each apartment (areas {@area N2|10d|x}, {@area N3|10e|x}, {@area N5|113|x}, and {@area N6|114|x}) contains a modest living space, kitchen, and bedroom.
The inhabitants are impoverished and have no belongings of value. Strangers terrify them, as any outsiders are likely to be Nym's goons. Residents won't answer the door if the characters knock.

entries.name: Ceilings
entries: The building's ceilings are 10 feet high.

entries.name: Doors
entries: The building's doors are made of wood. The front door is left unlocked. Doors to the apartments (areas {@area N2|10d|x}, {@area N3|10e|x}, {@area N5|113|x}, and {@area N6|114|x}) are locked. The locks on the doors are Simple (1 action to pick) and of Inferior quality ({@dc 10}).

entries.name: Lighting
entries: The building's windows allow {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} into the apartments during the day. At night, there is {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} if the residents are at home and awake (areas {@area N2|10d|x} and {@area N3|10e|x}) and {@variantrule Darkness|XPHB} otherwise (areas {@area N5|113|x} and {@area N6|114|x}). Interior hallways (areas {@area N1|10b|x} and {@area N4|10f|x}) are lit with a few sconces that cast {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} in the area at all hours.

entries.name: Walls
entries: The walls between apartments are made of thin wood and plaster. Characters can hear loud noises coming from any area in the building.

entries.name: Windows
entries: The building's windows are big enough for a Medium or smaller creature to fit through. Windows on the first floor stand 3 feet above the ground. Windows on the second floor are 15 feet above the ground. The windows are locked from the inside.

Characters within 5 feet of a window on the inside of the building can take the {@action Utilize|XPHB} action to open the window. From the outside, a character can take the {@action Utilize|XPHB} action to try to pick a window's lock using {@item Thieves' Tools|XPHB}, completing the task with a successful {@dc 15} Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand|XPHB}) check.

entries.name: Nym Building 3 Locations
entries: The apartment building has two floors with similar floor plans.

The following locations are keyed to map 3.5. Descriptions assume the characters arrive in the evening, when Nym visits the building to harass the tenants. If the characters show up earlier, they eventually see Nym and his three associates enter the building (see area N1); resident Varrel Phor is inside his apartment ({@area area N6|114|x}).

entries.name: N1: Entryway

entries: Dim light flickers from sconces along the walls in this dingy, empty hallway.

This hall affords access to the first-floor apartments (areas {@area N2|10d|x} and {@area N3|10e|x}). A character who takes the {@action Study|XPHB} action to listen carefully in the hall hears murmuring voices in the western apartment (area N3).

entries.name: N2: Lower Eastern Apartment
entries: Inside the eastern apartment on the first floor live the halfling couple Melda and Markus Fiddlestand (Small {@creature Commoner|XMM|Commoners}). The Fiddlestands are eating a modest dinner of bread and boiled radishes after a long day laboring on a nearby construction site.

entries.name: N3: Lower Western Apartment
entries: Darvin Dorn and his teenage son Rufus (Medium {@creature Commoner|XMM|Commoners}) are humans who rent the western first-floor apartment. They're solving a crossword puzzle together after working their fruit stand all day.

entries.name: N4: Upstairs Hallway
entries: If the characters enter this area while Nym is present read or paraphrase the following text; otherwise, this hall is empty.

An angry shout rings throughout this hall: "You know what'll happen if you're late again!" Three muscled ruffians, one clad in heavy armor, taunt a whimpering man slumped at their feet. The speaker, one of the ruffians, is a bald man with a blond beard. A robed woman with horns leers nearby, her mouth twisted in a cruel smile.

The armored ruffian with the blond beard is the human Pryas Nym (Medium, Neutral Evil {@creature Warrior Commander|XMM}), the characters' target. The other ruffians are the humans Nora Nym and Horace Nym (Medium, Neutral Evil {@creature Bandit Deceiver|XMM|Bandit Deceivers}), Pryas's cousins. The horned woman, the tiefling Vareina (Medium, Neutral Evil {@creature Mage|XMM}), works for Pryas. All four fight the characters if the characters interrupt their bullying.

The gang is accosting the human Varrel Phor (Medium {@creature Commoner|XMM}), who lives in the upper eastern apartment ({@area area N6|114|x}) and works as an apprentice for a nearby blacksmith. The gang threatens to injure Phor if he doesn't pay his rent on time.

entries.name: Fighting the Landlord
entries: Pryas Nym is a cruel and sycophantic man who's loyal to Szass Tam. Nym fights to the death. If he dies, his cronies surrender; they don't work for Szass Tam.

entries.name: Development
entries: Killing Pryas Nym neutralizes him as a spy, and each character earns 4,100 XP. If the characters resurrect him, Nym fawns on them, promising to stop spying and even to leave town if the characters insist. He follows through with that promise.

entries.name: N5: Upper Western Apartment
entries: An orc woman named Feridine (Medium {@creature Commoner|XMM}) lives in the western apartment on the second floor. She is napping before her night shift as a bartender at a nearby tavern.

entries.name: N6: Upper Eastern Apartment
entries: The human Varrel Phor lives in the eastern apartment on the second floor. He is currently in the upper hall ({@area area N4|10f|x}) enduring Nym's bullying.

entries.name: Lower Ward Alley
entries: When workers in smithies and shops in the Lower Ward depart at dusk, a local racketeer, Rathan Jur, commandeers an empty alley to meet with those he extorts. A cruel goliath man, he relishes violence.
The following sections assume the characters come to the alley during the evening. Jur doesn't visit this area during the day.

entries.name: Alley Features
entries: The alley, shown on map 3.6, has the following features.

entries.name: Balconies
entries: Near the alley's southern end, balconies to the east and west overlook the alley. The balconies are 10 feet above the ground.

entries.name: Buildings
entries: The buildings that flank the alley are made of wood and have flat roofs 20 feet above the ground.

entries.name: Doors
entries: The buildings' doors are made of wood and locked. The locks are Simple (1 action to pick) and of Good quality ({@dc 15}).

entries.name: Ladder
entries: A 20-foot-tall ladder that maintenance workers use during the day leans against the side of a building to the southwest.

entries.name: Lighting
entries: Sconces with {@spell Continual Flame|XPHB} spells cast on them shed {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} throughout the alley at street level. The rooftops are in {@variantrule Darkness|XPHB}.

entries.name: Encountering Rathan Jur
entries: If the characters arrive during the day, they see normal foot traffic come and go from nearby businesses, but Rathan Jur doesn't appear.

Once the alley becomes deserted, the characters have about an hour to prepare for the confrontation. If they wait in the area for Jur to arrive, they see the goliath and two human associates walk to the center of the alley, followed shortly by a frightened orc man.
If the characters don't confront the group immediately, read or paraphrase the following:
