A bald, armored goliath man with a scimitar belted to his hip grins and pounds his fist into his palm. He jeers at an orc man wearing simple robes, saying, "You better pay up, Ruther. Accidents happen all the time. In fact, I feel like my fist is about to slip." The goliath punches the orc. Two smug-looking human women standing beside the goliath burst into laughter.

The goliath is Rathan Jur (Medium, Neutral Evil {@creature Bandit Crime Lord|XMM}), and the humans are Rettene and Carla (Medium, Neutral Evil {@creature Bandit Deceiver|XMM|Bandit Deceivers}). The three fight the characters if the characters interrupt their bullying.
The orc man (Medium {@creature Commoner|XMM}) is named Ruther. The punch reduces him to 3 HP. If the characters don't intervene, Jur punches Ruther again, reducing him to 2 HP.

entries.name: Engaging with the Racketeer
entries: Jur isn't particularly loyal to Szass Tam, but threats alone won't get him to agree to stop spying. But if the characters reduce him to 20 HP or fewer, he promises to leave town immediately. He keeps his word and allows the characters to escort him out of town as assurance.

entries.name: Development
entries: If the characters kill Jur or convince him to leave town, they have neutralized him as a spy, and each character earns 4,100 XP.

entries.name: Concluding the Mission
entries: If the characters neutralize the spies Thellania Marr, Pryas Nym, and Rathan Jur, their mission is successful.

entries.name: Mission Reward
entries: As the zulkir promised, the party is entitled to one magic item from the list in "{@area Mission Rewards|0da|x}" earlier in this chapter. Remind them to tell Wrynn which item they've chosen. Additionally, each character earns 4,100 XP.

entries.name: Returning to the Zulkir
entries: When the characters are ready to receive their next mission from Zulkir Thrul, they should return to Wrynn's Bespoke Vestments as instructed in "{@area How to Meet with the Zulkir|0e0|x}" earlier in this chapter. The details of what's happening in the shop when the characters arrive are up to you. The zulkir soon shows up in a new disguise created using the {@spell Alter Self|XPHB} spell, appearing as an elderly gnome woman with golden spectacles and long, purple robes.

When Wrynn, the characters, and the disguised zulkir are alone, the tailor locks the front door and ushers everyone into the shop's secret office (area W3 on {@adventure map 3.2|AUD|3|Map 3.2: Wrynn's Bespoke Vestments}). Thrul casts the {@spell Demiplane|XPHB} spell and escorts the group through the shadowy door that appears on the wall.

entries.name: Second Mission
entries: Read or paraphrase the following speech from Thrul when the characters are ready to receive their second mission:
"Operatives, you've taken three of the Hydra's pawns off the board. Your next target is bigger.

"The Hydra's intel courier in Eltabbar, the Messenger, owns the Two Plateaus Shipping Company. The Messenger receives reports from the Hydra's spies at his company's headquarters and reports them to the Hydra via allied Red Wizards.
"My spies have also learned that despite his outward loyalty to the Hydra, the Messenger is stealing magic items from the Hydra's shipments. If the Hydra knew, the Messenger would be dead.
"We need to disrupt the Hydra's spy operations in the city. While you could simply kill the Messenger, learning what intel he's passing on would help us stay one step ahead of the Hydra.

"I recommend you use evidence of the Messenger's thefts to blackmail him into sharing the information he receives with us before he sends it to the Hydra. The Sparrow will provide details about a dead drop the Messenger should use. If you succeed at blackmailing the Messenger, give him that information.

"Operatives, this task won't be easy. We haven't scouted the company's interior, and we don't know what evidence of the Messenger's skimming might exist. If you must kill the Messenger, I will still consider this mission a success.
"Do you have questions?"
More information about the Two Plateaus Shipping Company appears in {@area chapter 1|079|x}.
The zulkir can provide the following information to the characters:

items.name: How Do You Suggest We Infiltrate the Company?
items.entry: "You could sneak into the building, but doing so is risky. I suggest you pose as individuals who the Messenger would expect on site: clients, workers, or potential business partners. The company has a receptionist who deals with all visitors. If you can convince this receptionist, whose details are unknown to us, that you're supposed to enter the building, this task might go smoother."

items.name: How Is the Messenger Stealing from the Hydra?
items.entry: "The Hydra uses the Messenger's company to send magic items his workshops have produced to buyers throughout the region. Before the shipments leave Eltabbar, the Messenger steals one or two items. The buyer assumes the workshops mispacked or lost them, and they are reported as losses. The Messenger does this only occasionally, so he hasn't gotten caught."

items.name: What Do You Know About This Company?
items.entry: "The Two Plateaus Shipping Company is located in the Warehouse Ward on the shores of Lake Thaylambar. The company ships trade goods and magic items in bulk from entrepreneurs, mostly Red Wizards, to clients. The staff works a day shift and a night shift. Given the Messenger's secret work for the Hydra, I expect the building has magical defenses but don't know their nature. We believe the Messenger stays on site at all times."

items.name: How Will We Recognize the Messenger?
items.entry: "The Messenger is a bearded, middle-aged human man named Iskan Iskari. I know no more, I'm afraid."

items.name: What Evidence Against the Messenger Should We Find?
items.entry: "Look for anything that proves the Messenger has been stealing: ledgers, lists of lost items, receipts from fences, and hidden items marked as lost. You'll need as many pieces of evidence as possible to convince the Messenger we have enough information to turn him in to the Hydra."

items.name: Will We Find Intel Destined for the Hydra There?
items.entry: "Perhaps; bring back any information you find that might prove valuable. We can use all the information we can get."

entries: After the zulkir answers the characters' questions, she provides directions to the Two Plateaus Shipping Company.

entries.name: Dead Drops
entries: Before they leave the shop, Wrynn hands the characters a sheet of paper with the location of the dead drop—a public waste bin in the Warehouse Ward—and a list of days and times.
If the characters convince Iskari to turn against Szass Tam, they must give him this paper; he should deliver intelligence there according to this schedule.

entries.name: Unwelcome Company
entries: If the characters haven't remained discreet about their intent to confront Szass Tam, rumors have begun to swirl around the city. If the characters have remained discreet, skip this encounter. (See "Importance of Secrecy" in {@area chapter 2|099|x} for more about emphasizing discretion and guile.)

As the characters head to the Two Plateaus Shipping Company, a gang of Szass Tam's operatives accosts them. Use {@adventure map 3.6|AUD|3|Map 3.6: Lower Ward Alley} for this encounter, though it takes place in the Warehouse Ward.
Read or paraphrase the following:

Four figures block your path: three humans, armored and with weapons drawn, and a tiefling in black robes emblazoned with a fist-shaped symbol. The tiefling shouts, "You dare oppose Szass Tam? Time to find out what happens next, fools."

These operatives are the tiefling man Daris Dredd (Medium, Neutral Evil {@creature Archpriest|XMM}), a priest of Bane who believes Szass Tam is destined to rule Thay, and the humans Ferron Tor, Werther Rudd, and Xerta Xon (Medium {@creature Bandit Deceiver|XMM|Bandit Deceivers}). They're low-level agents of Szass Tam who bully anyone who speaks out against the lich. They fight the characters to the death.

entries.name: Two Plateaus Shipping
entries: The building that houses the Two Plateaus Shipping Company is both the company's headquarters and Iskari's base of operations, from which he sends Szass Tam information from the lich's spy operations in the tharch of Eltabbar. The shipping company often deals with dangerous clients and expensive goods, so Iskari employs capable guards to discourage any agents sent to sabotage rivals' shipments and burglars.

entries.name: The Messenger
entries: The Messenger's real name is Iskan Iskari. He is a {@creature Rakshasa|XMM} disguised as a human Thayan. He uses the {@spell Disguise Self|XPHB} spell to cloak his true form, appearing as a bald, broad-shouldered, broad-chested human with a dark beard. Undisguised, he resembles a humanoid tiger covered in pale fur with dark stripes. In any form, Iskari has a forked tongue, hinting at his true nature.

Iskari holds the keys to the locked trunks and drawers in the storeroom ({@area area T5|144|x}), the drawer in the break room ({@area area T12|159|x}), his office ({@area area T14|161|x}), and his quarters ({@area area T15|167|x}). During the day, Iskari usually works in his office, although you can place him elsewhere in the building. At night, he sleeps in his quarters (area T15).

entries.name: Iskari's Scam

entries.title: Iskan Iskari and an employee inventory a shipment of magic items for a Red Wizard client.

entries: The workers and guards at Two Plateaus Shipping Company don't know that Iskari has been stealing magic items from clients and selling them. Iskari doesn't fear many of his clients—but he is afraid of Szass Tam. He carefully hides any evidence of his scam.

entries.name: Securing Evidence
entries: If the characters want to convince Iskari to work against Szass Tam, they must secure one or more pieces of evidence that prove Iskari has stolen from the lich. The characters recognize when something they find is evidence. They can find four pieces of evidence, which are in the following areas:

items.name: Area T5:
items.entry: Stolen {@item Mantle of Spell Resistance|XDMG}

items.name: Area T10:
items.entry: Document listing items that were supposedly lost in transit

items.name: Area T12:
items.entry: Receipt for stolen items sold to a fence

items.name: Area T14:
items.entry: Stolen {@item Nine Lives Stealer Longsword|XDMG|Nine Lives Stealer (Longsword)}

entries.name: Blackmailing Iskari
entries: When the characters interact with Iskari, a character can take the {@action Influence|XPHB} action to try to convince him that they know about his scam and will inform Szass Tam unless Iskari cooperates. The character then makes a Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) check. The DC of that check depends on how many pieces of evidence the characters have when they confront Iskari, as noted in the Blackmailing Iskari table.

Although Iskari serves Szass Tam, he is greedy and self-centered. Iskari lies about stealing magic items unless the characters have three or more pieces of evidence or convince him to work against Szass Tam.
If the characters convince Iskari to work against Szass Tam, they must give him the instructions described in "{@area Dead Drops|126|x}."

entries.name: Development
entries: If the characters find three or more pieces of evidence, each character earns 4,700 XP.

entries.name: Shipping Company Features
entries: Unless otherwise specified, the shipping company has the following features.

entries.name: Ceilings
entries: The building's ceilings are 15 feet high. The loading dock ({@area area T16|16b|x}) has no ceiling.

entries.name: Doors
entries: The doors in the shipping company are made of wood, and most are unlocked.

entries.name: Secret Doors
entries: Unless otherwise noted, secret doors (marked with an S on the map; {@dc 18} to notice) blend in with the surrounding surfaces from the outside but are obvious from the inside. They're unlocked and swing inward on hidden hinges. Iskari; shipping agents Alik Nal, Korla, and Cam; and the building's guards know about the secret areas, but the company's other employees don't.

entries.name: Lighting
entries: Inside the building, lamps with {@spell Continual Flame|XPHB} spells cast on them emit {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB}. The loading dock is in {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} during the day.

entries.name: Windows
entries: The windows near the building's front entrance are unlocked and large enough for a Medium or smaller creature to climb through.

entries.name: Window Traps
entries: The windows are trapped from the outside with a wire that sends a jolt of electricity through intruders. The traps are denoted by a T on the map. A creature that touches the outside of a window gets shocked. The creature makes a {@dc 15} Constitution saving throw, taking 28 ({@dice 8d6}) Lightning damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

entries.name: Detecting the Traps
entries: A creature can take the {@action Search|XPHB} action to inspect a window. They make a {@dc 18} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check; on a success, the creature finds the wire. The traps are built into the window's structure and can't be disarmed, but once detected, the wire is easily avoided when climbing through a window.

entries.name: Shipping Company Locations
entries: The following locations are keyed to map 3.7. The shipping company operates around the clock. If the characters visit during the day and return at night (or vice versa), the same number of staff members occupy each area. Except for Iskari, they are different individuals.

entries.name: T1: Reception

entries: The walls of this reception area are decorated with landscapes of Thay's rocky plateaus. At a central desk sits a young human man with red hair and freckles. He greets you with a smile.
"Welcome to Two Plateaus Shipping Company! How can I help you today?"

The human receptionist is Thom (Medium {@creature Noble|XMM}). If the characters fight Thom, he flees into area T2a, using his key to bypass the trap (see {@area area T2a–b|13c|x}). In 2 minutes, Iskari and the guard from {@area area T7|149|x} arrive and confront the characters.

entries.name: Gaining Entry
entries: As an {@action Influence|XPHB} action, a character can try to convince Thom they need to go inside the building. The character then makes a {@dc 15} Charisma ({@skill Deception|XPHB} or {@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) check. On a successful check, Thom escorts the characters into a waiting room (area T2a), using a key that bypasses the trap on the door (see area {@area T2a–b|13c|x}).

Thom tells them to wait while he summons a shipping agent. In 20 minutes, Alik Nal arrives from the shipping office ({@area area T10|154|x}). If the characters request to meet with Iskari, Thom tells them it will be an hour before the owner is free; he never arrives.
On a failure, Thom demands the characters leave and flees into area T2a if they don't.

entries.name: Traps
entries: The locks on the doors to the east and west are trapped, as described below.

entries.name: T2a–b: Waiting Rooms
entries: The doors leading from reception ({@area area T1|138|x}) to the waiting rooms are locked. The locks are Complex (1 minute to pick) and of Superior quality ({@dc 20}).

The locks on the doors to the east and west are each outfitted with a poisoned needle trap, as described in {@trap Poisoned Needle|XDMG}, except the Constitution saving throw is {@dc 15}, and the Poison damage is 22 ({@dice 4d10}).
Comfortable armchairs are nestled against the walls, while doors lead to the lobby and farther into the building. Portraits of Red Wizards standing in powerful poses adorn the walls.
Clients wait here to speak with shipping agents.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: The paintings depict powerful Red Wizards—allies of Szass Tam and Iskari. These four portraits by renowned Thayan artist Taryn Gill are worth 2,500 GP apiece.

entries.name: T3: Southeast Hall

entries: A narrow hall stretches about forty feet west to east, with two doors on the south wall and one on the northeast corner.
The sounds of crates being moved and packed in the nearby hall and warehouses (areas T6–T9) are audible here.

entries.name: T4: Dummy Office

entries: This office contains a small desk with drawers against the west wall. A door leads north.
Old shipping paperwork lies scattered atop the desk, but none seems recent. This office primarily serves as a buffer between the rest of the company and the secret storeroom (area T5).

entries.name: Secret Door
entries: A secret door on the east wall opens into area T5. See "{@area Shipping Company Features|12f|x}" for details on this door.

entries.name: T5: Secret Storeroom

entries: Two steamer trunks sit against the north wall. Doors lead east and west.

Iskari tells Alik Nal and the guards that items clients have forgotten are kept here, but in reality, he uses this space to store stolen goods. The doors lead to the dummy office ({@area area T4|141|x}) and a warehouse ({@area area T7|149|x}).

entries.name: Blackmail Evidence
entries: The trunks are both locked. As a {@action Utilize|XPHB} action, a character can try to pick a lock using {@item Thieves' Tools|XPHB}, accomplishing the task with a successful {@dc 18} Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand|XPHB}) check.
The west trunk holds twelve nonmagical cloaks. Underneath them is the {@item Mantle of Spell Resistance|XDMG} mentioned in the document found in the shipping office (area T10).
The east trunk holds fourteen nonmagical cloaks plus a small purse with 50 GP inside.

entries.name: T6: Northeast Hall

entries: Double doors dot this hall's east and west walls; another door stands in the southwest corner. Three human workers mill about. The hall is otherwise empty aside from a few wooden crates.
The three workers are the humans Xenk, Jera, and Lilah (Medium {@creature Bandit Deceiver|XMM|Bandit Deceivers}).

The workers assume the characters are authorized to be here unless they look like obvious intruders. In that case, the workers fight the party, shouting for help from workers and guards in nearby warehouses (areas T7–T9). Those individuals arrive to join the fight at the beginning of the third round of combat.

entries.name: T7: Warehouse A

entries: This warehouse is filled with crates. Three goliath workers loiter, and an orc woman wearing studded leather armor guards the double door.

The three goliath workers—Jorah, Jumah, and Karis (Medium {@creature Bandit Deceiver|XMM|Bandit Deceivers})—await word on when the next boat is scheduled to arrive in the loading dock ({@area area T16|16b|x}). The guard is the orc Dora Brokenjaw (Medium {@creature Bandit Crime Lord|XMM}), who demands the characters leave when she notices them.

As an {@action Influence|XPHB} action, a character can insist they're authorized to be here. The character makes a {@dc 18} Charisma ({@skill Deception|XPHB}) check. On a success, the staff allows the characters to go about their business. On a failure, the guard begins combat and the workers flee. Should combat begin, the guards from areas T8 and T9 arrive at the end of the second round of combat.

entries.name: Crates
entries: This room holds twenty-one crates. Ten crates contain 20 pounds of flour and are worth 50 CP apiece; another eleven contain 20 pounds of wheat and are worth 20 CP apiece.

entries.name: Secret Door
entries: A secret door near the southeast corner leads to the storeroom {@area (area T5|144|x}). See "{@area Shipping Company Features|12f|x}" for details on this door.

entries.name: T8: Warehouse B

entries: This warehouse is filled with crates. A human man wearing studded leather armor guards the double door.
The guard is the human Rian Jon (Medium {@creature Assassin|XMM}), who demands the characters leave when he notices them.

As an {@action Influence|XPHB} action, a character can insist they're authorized to be here. The character makes a {@dc 16} Charisma ({@skill Deception|XPHB}) check. On a success, the guard allows the characters to go about their business. On a failure, the guard begins combat. Should combat begin, the guards from areas T7 and T9 arrive at the end of the second round of combat.

entries.name: Crates
entries: This warehouse holds twenty crates. Ten contain canvas textiles and are worth 10 GP apiece. Another ten contain cotton textiles and are worth 100 GP apiece.

entries.name: T9: Warehouse C

entries: This large warehouse is filled with barrels and crates. A tiefling woman wearing studded leather armor guards the double door in the west wall.
The guard is the tiefling Terra Senpher (Medium {@creature Bandit Crime Lord|XMM}), who demands the characters leave when she notices them.

As an {@action Influence|XPHB} action, a character can insist they're authorized to be here. The character makes a {@dc 18} Charisma ({@skill Deception|XPHB}) check. On a successful check, the guard allows the characters to go about their business. On a failure or if they're caught stealing, the guard begins combat. Should combat begin, the guards from areas T7 and T8 arrive at the end of the second round of combat.

entries.name: Barrels and Crates
entries: Ten barrels contain burlap and are worth 10 GP apiece; another ten crates contain linen textiles and are worth 100 GP apiece.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: A crate in the southeast corner contains the following (all but {@item Walloping Ammunition|XDMG} appear in appendix A):

entries.name: T10: Shipping Office

entries: An elf man wearing gray robes sits at this room's desk, writing with a quill on a roll of parchment. A shelf full of ledgers sits against the south wall, and doors lead to the north, west, and east.
The elf man is Alik Nal (Medium {@creature Mage|XMM}), a shipping agent. Nal is recording the details of a recent shipment.

Nal demands the characters leave if he notices them, barking that he's too busy to speak with them. If they won't leave, he fights them. Should combat begin here, the guards from areas T7–T9 join the fight at the end of the second round of combat.

As an {@action Influence|XPHB} action, a character can try to convince Nal to leave the room or allow them to peruse the ledgers. The character then makes a {@dc 17} Charisma ({@skill Deception|XPHB} or {@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) check. On a success, Nal assents to the request. If he discovers the characters have deceived him, he fights them.

entries.name: Blackmail Evidence
entries: Hidden among the ledgers on the shelf is a document listing magic items Iskari has reported to clients as lost:

items: {@item Nine Lives Stealer Longsword|XDMG|Nine Lives Stealer (Longsword)}

entries: The words "fenced" appear next to the entries for the broom, helm, lantern, and {@i Sending Stones}.

Iskari has fenced all but the {@i Mantle of Spell Resistance} and the {@i Nine Lives Stealer (Longsword}), which are in the secret storeroom ({@area area T5|144|x}) and his office ({@area area T14|161|x}), respectively. If the characters have found either of these magic items, they realize those are the items mentioned in this list.

entries.name: T11: West Hall

entries: Plush carpet covers the floor of this hall, which is lined with seascapes showing the Thayan coast.
Iskari takes his most valued clients to his office ({@area area T14|161|x}) through this hall.

entries.name: T12: Break Room

entries: This room's table and chairs are spartan, its walls and floors undecorated. Two desks sit along the south wall; the one to the west has a drawer.
This area serves as a break room for the guards in the warehouses (areas T7–T9).

entries.name: Blackmail Evidence
entries: The western desk's drawer is locked. A character can take the {@action Utilize|XPHB} action to try to pick the lock using {@item Thieves' Tools|XPHB}, accomplishing the task with a successful {@dc 18} Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand|XPHB}) check. Inside the drawer lies a handwritten receipt for the following items, sold for 200 GP apiece:

entries.name: T13a-c: Small Storage Rooms
entries: These rooms are used for storage.

entries.name: T13a
entries: This room holds small shipments (see "{@area Treasure|16a|x}").

entries.name: T13b
entries: This room is empty.

entries.name: T13c
entries: The shelves in this room hold office and cleaning supplies, which have no value.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: A character who searches area T13a finds several carefully packed crates full of glass vials and bottles; the boxes hold eight {@item Potion of Healing|XDMG|Potion of Healings} in total.

entries.name: T14. Iskari's Office
entries: The door from the hallway into the office is locked. The lock is Complex (1 minute to pick) and of Superior quality ({@dc 20}). On bypassing the door, read or paraphrase the following:

Sitting behind the heavy desk in this spacious office is a bearded, broad-shouldered man wearing a purple cloak and a scowl. A glass orb sits on the desk. Beside the desk looms a stone statue of a soldier. A bookshelf stands in the northeast corner.

Company owner and intel courier Iskan Iskari ({@creature Rakshasa|XMM}) sits here wearing his human disguise (see "{@area The Messenger|12a|x}" earlier in this chapter). The statue ({@creature Stone Golem|XMM}) animates and fights the characters if combat begins in this room. Before the statue animates, a character must succeed on a {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check to discern its magical nature.

The characters can try to convince Iskari to work against Szass Tam as described in "{@area Blackmailing Iskari|12d|x}" earlier in this chapter. If the characters don't try to talk to Iskari, when he realizes they are intruders, he and the golem begin combat. Iskari fights until reduced to 50 HP. He then attempts to flee into his quarters and through the trapdoor (see {@area area T15|167|x}).

entries.name: Blackmail Evidence
entries: The desk's bottom drawer is locked. A character can take the {@action Utilize|XPHB} action to try to pick the lock using {@item Thieves' Tools|XPHB}, accomplishing the task with a successful {@dc 18} Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand|XPHB}) check. On a successful check, the drawer opens, revealing the {@item Nine Lives Stealer Longsword|XDMG|Nine Lives Stealer (Longsword)} mentioned in the document found in the shipping office ({@area area T10|154|x}). Iskari is debating whether to fence or keep this item.

entries.name: Intel
entries: The drawer in the table to the south is locked. A character can take the {@action Utilize|XPHB} action to try to pick the lock using {@item Thieves' Tools|XPHB}, accomplishing the task with a successful {@dc 18} Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand|XPHB}) check. Inside the drawer is a piece of folded parchment. When the characters read it, read or paraphrase the following:
When you unfold this parchment, you see the following written in Common in a halting hand:

"A militia of disgruntled former soldiers has formed in Pyarados. They hate all Red Wizards, especially Szass Tam. Their leader is Fallon, whose family members were Szass Tam's enemies and were justly punished years ago. Fallon tries to rally the region against Szass Tam's impending regency and needs to be dealt with.
"Place this note in the shipment marked for Zoltir Zith to ensure it reaches our esteemed regent."

An agent of Szass Tam recently gave this note to Iskari, who intends to send it to the lich in an upcoming shipment bound for Thaymount. This note foreshadows the characters' mission to recruit Fallon and the Pyarados militia in {@area chapter 4|17a|x}.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: The glass orb on the table is a {@item Driftglobe|XDMG}.

entries.name: T15: Iskari's Quarters
entries: The door to this chamber is locked. The lock is Complex (1 minute to pick) and of Superior quality ({@dc 20}).
This room contains a narrow bed. A large rug covers most of the floor. To the south is a closet.

entries.name: Secret Door
entries: Underneath the trunk in the closet is a secret trapdoor that opens into a hidden tunnel. This trapdoor is marked with an S on the map. The tunnel leads out of the building and emerges just above Lake Thaylambar's water level.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: The closet contains a trunk, which is locked. A character can take the {@action Utilize|XPHB} action to try to pick the lock using {@item Thieves' Tools|XPHB}, accomplishing the task with a successful {@dc 18} Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand|XPHB}) check. On a successful check, the trunk opens.
Inside the trunk are Iskari's valuables:

entries.name: T16: Loading Dock

entries: Standing on this wooden loading dock are two gray-robed humans who gesture while speaking to an orc man wearing a black robe emblazoned with a fist-shaped symbol. The dock surrounds an empty boat slip, to the east of which sits a crane. A mechanism stands along the west wall. The slip's doors are closed, making it inaccessible to passing boats. The area has no roof.

The robed humans are the shipping agents Korla and Cam (Medium {@creature Mage|XMM|Mages}). They are showing the boat slip to a prospective client, the orc Grosh (Medium, Neutral Evil {@creature Archpriest|XMM}), who worships Bane and owns a magic item business.

If they notice the characters, they're incensed at the interruption. Grosh fights the characters while the agents flee to retrieve a guard. Should combat begin here, the guard from {@area area T9|150|x} arrives at the end of the second round of combat.

entries.name: Boat Slip
entries: The water here is 40 feet deep.

entries.name: Crane
entries: The 10-foot-tall crane has a heavy hook block. A creature standing next to the crane can take the {@action Utilize|XPHB} action to swing its hook block, knocking over any creatures in its path. Each creature standing next to the crane except the character swinging the hook block must succeed on a {@dc 15} Dexterity saving throw or take 7 ({@dice 2d6}) Bludgeoning damage and have the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

entries.name: Mechanism and Outer Doors
entries: The mechanism to the west controls the outer doors. A character standing next to the mechanism can take the {@action Utilize|XPHB} action to open or close the doors. The doors and adjacent walls are 15 feet tall.

entries.name: Concluding the Mission
entries: If the characters kill Iskari or convince him to work against Szass Tam, their mission is successful.

entries.name: Mission Reward
entries: The characters should tell Wrynn which magic item they want from the list in "{@area Mission Rewards|0da|x}" earlier in this chapter. Additionally, each character earns 4,700 XP.

entries.name: Reporting Spy Intel
entries: If the characters found the spy intel note in {@area area T14|161|x} and share its contents with Wrynn, he looks thoughtful and tells the characters he's not surprised to hear that Szass Tam's agents have targeted the militia.
Sometime after the characters complete their first or second mission, Wrynn sends them a gift via an anonymous courier to express his thanks for the work they've done so far.

The details are up to you, but at your discretion, a parcel arrives where one or more characters stay. The parcel is a cherrywood box wrapped in black satin. The box is lined with purple velvet, on which sit a number of elegantly embroidered handkerchiefs equal to the number of characters. Ask each player their character's favorite color; that's the color of the handkerchief Wrynn has given them.
The box also contains a note. When the characters read the note, give the players a copy of the Gift Note handout.

The details are up to you, but at your discretion, a parcel arrives where one or more characters stay. The parcel is a cherrywood box wrapped in black satin. The box is lined with purple velvet, on which sit a number of elegantly embroidered handkerchiefs equal to the number of characters. data.name: Chapter 4: Peril in Pyarados
entries: {@i Recruit soldiers and recover an ancient artifact.}

entries.title: Heroes battle ancient guardians outside the Temple of the Red Knight.

entries.name: Key Plot Points
entries: The following information is key to this chapter's story:

items.name: Approach the Militia
items.entry: The characters travel to rural Pyarados in eastern Thay, where they must help a militia repel a demonic attack, then ask the militia to protect the region from Szass Tam's hordes.

items.name: Retrieve the Censer
items.entry: The characters also must infiltrate a nearby ancient temple to the Red Knight and retrieve the {@item Spirit-Binding Censer|AUD}, which can ensure {@creature Szass Tam|AUD} remains dead for one hundred years if they kill him.

entries.name: Preparation
entries: Before running this chapter, prepare as follows:

items.name: Step 1
items.entry: Read the "{@area Running This Chapter|177|x}" section, including "{@area Character Advancement|178|x}." Decide with your players which mission the characters will tackle first or run them in the order presented.

items.name: Step 2
items.entry: Familiarize yourself with the Key NPCs table below.

items.name: Step 3
items.entry: Bookmark the stat blocks below, which appear in the {@book Monster Manual|XMM} and on D&D Beyond unless otherwise noted. If a stat block appears in appendix B, an asterisk appears after its name:

entries.caption: Key NPCs
rows: Ezkaar Softhoof, Tilda Ven, and Yaris
{@creature Centaur Trooper|XMM} and {@creature Warrior Veteran|XMM|Warrior Veterans} (Medium, Neutral Good)
Human leader of the Pyarados militia
Goliath Thayan knight who serves Omina
Human and tiefling militia members under attack by demons
Human Red Wizard besieging the Pyarados militia's base
Human, only survivor of an undead attack in the ancient temple
Human tailor and Zulkir Thrul's spy master
Human zulkir of evocation and Operation Deadfall leader

entries.name: Running This Chapter
entries: This chapter takes place after the characters have completed their missions in Eltabbar.

entries.name: Character Advancement
entries: The characters should be level 13 when this chapter begins. They should have enough XP to advance to level 14 before they embark on their second mission in this chapter. They should reach level 15 by the end of this chapter. If you're using a method of level advancement that doesn't rely on XP, the characters gain levels at those points.

entries.name: Returning to the Zulkir
entries: When Wynston Wrynn summons the characters to the shop to meet with the zulkir, they find him busy writing receipts at the desk in the otherwise empty shop.

Wrynn ushers the characters into the secret office and whispers into a {@item Sending Stones|XDMG|Sending Stone}. A few moments later, Zulkir Thrul arrives via the {@spell Teleport|XPHB} spell, undisguised. She casts the {@spell Demiplane|XPHB} spell and escorts the group through the shadowy door that appears on the wall.

entries.name: Third and Fourth Missions
entries: When the characters are ready, read or paraphrase the following:
"Operatives, you've done well disrupting the Hydra's agents in Eltabbar," Zulkir Thrul says. "It's time to lay groundwork outside the city.

"Your next two missions are in the tharch of Pyarados. One is to secure an alliance with a militia, code-named the Bodyguards, that can greatly help our cause. The second is to retrieve a powerful magic item, code-named the Artifact, from an ancient temple of the Red Knight.
"Both objectives are near each other. You may accomplish these goals in whatever order you wish.

"The Hydra conducted experiments with foul magic in this area. His activities thinned the veil between planes, and reports indicate that fiends rampage throughout the area. Protect yourselves, and stay alert.
"Before you depart, please take this {@i Sending Stone}—then I'll answer your questions."

Before answering their questions, the zulkir hands the characters one of a pair of {@item Sending Stones|XDMG}. She asks them to give it to Fallon Nor, the militia's leader, to report about any rising activity related to Szass Tam and his allies. Wrynn keeps the other stone. The zulkir instructs the characters to tell the militia only that they will communicate with a trusted associate called the Sparrow.
Thrul can provide the following information about both missions:

items.name: How Will We Get to Pyarados?
items.entry: "You may find your own way there, or I can give you two {@item Spell Scroll|XDMG|Spell Scrolls} {@i of} {@spell Teleport|XPHB}: one to transport you near your destination, and one to return you home. If you use the scrolls, however, you must teleport to where I describe and approach your missions on foot to avoid appearing hostile." If the characters want the scrolls, the zulkir hands them over now."

items.name: Where in Pyarados Are These Missions?
items.entry: "The locations of both missions are a few miles from a fork in a rural trail branching east off the Minor Road. The militia is based in an old station called Tax Station Number 18; it lies about five miles south of the fork. The temple is five miles north of the fork and is built into the side of a sheer cliff."

entries: Thrul can provide the following information about the Bodyguards:

items.name: How Can We Convince the Bodyguards to Ally with Us?
items.entry: "There is no need to lie to the Bodyguards. They hate the Hydra. Tell them you aim to defeat him, and that any information they provide will help that cause. Tell them that if you succeed, reinforcements from Eltabbar will come to help them, but they can't be spared while the Hydra remains a threat. As usual, keep my name out of your discussions, but you may reveal that you have a powerful patron. Let them know they aren't alone in their struggle, and I suspect they will want to help us."

items.name: How Will They Help Operation Deadfall?
items.entry: "The Bodyguards roam the region protecting the locals from monster attacks. Since the Hydra's experiments here have attracted fiends and animated undead, his allies might arrive soon to marshal those menaces to overwhelm eastern Thay. We need them to tell us if that happens."

items.name: What Can You Tell Us About the Bodyguards?
items.entry: "{@area Pyarados's tharchion|058|x} refuses to send its official army outside the tharch's capital despite the many fiend and malefite attacks against Pyarados's rural population in recent months. The Bodyguards are former soldiers who want to defend their neighbors against these attacks. Their leader is a former commander named Fallon Nor, whose family was killed here in Eltabbar years ago after speaking out against the Hydra. Nor's hatred for the Hydra burns brightly, and I'm certain she'll ally with us if you ask."

items.name: Should We Expect Trouble at Their Base?
items.entry: "Count on it. It's no secret Fallon Nor hates the Hydra, and since the Hydra's network is silencing his enemies, the Bodyguards are in danger. That, combined with the reports of roving fiends and malefites, means you could face significant threats near the base."

entries: The zulkir can provide the following information about the Artifact:

items.name: What Can You Tell Us About the Temple?
items.entry: "The temple is ancient and notoriously deadly to treasure hunters; no explorers are known to have survived. I know little about the site, but it's reputed to hold a powerful magic item that's vital to our cause."

items.name: Why Do We Need the Artifact?
items.entry: "The Artifact is a mighty magical censer written about vaguely in the rarest history books. It was created by this area's ancient people to protect themselves against otherworldly monsters. I believe the Artifact has the ability to trap the Hydra's soul—not indefinitely, but at least long enough to give Thay a chance to prepare to resist his inevitable future schemes. If I'm correct, using the Artifact against the Hydra in your coming conflict is just as important as interrupting his ritual."

entries: After the zulkir answers the characters' questions, she gives them directions to {@area Tax Station Number 18|182|x} and to the {@area Temple of the Red Knight|1a3|x}.
When the characters are ready to recruit the Bodyguards, see "Pyarados Militia." When they are ready to seek the {@item Spirit-Binding Censer|AUD}, see "{@area An Ancient Temple|19c|x}."

entries.name: Pyarados Militia
entries: The Bodyguards may be ragtag, but they are highly trained former soldiers. In recent weeks, they have patrolled eastern Pyarados, helping locals fend off demons and undead. Militia members don't know Szass Tam's plans, but they know something terrible is amiss.

entries.name: Militia's Commander
entries: The militia's leader is Fallon Nor, a former commander in Pyarados's military and human scion of a once-powerful noble family in Eltabbar. Thirty years ago, during Szass Tam's regency, the Nors spoke against the lich's cruelty. Enraged, Szass Tam unleashed a horde of undead on the family's estate that killed dozens, including Nor's parents. A housekeeper escaped with baby Fallon, who grew up in rural Pyarados with an adoptive family.
Brusque but kind, Nor hates the Red Wizards—and Szass Tam in particular. The other soldiers admire her bravery and trust her with their lives.

entries.name: Imminent Threat
entries: Thrul is rightly worried about the militia's safety. Right before the characters arrive, a Red Wizard traveled to Tax Station Number 18, intent on wiping out the militia to curry favor with Szass Tam. A human demonologist named Omina, this Red Wizard soon discovered that nearby marauding demons had slipped onto the Material Plane during Szass Tam's previous experiments. Omina allied with the demons and launched an assault on the militia, along with her Thayan knight, the goliath Garos.

entries.name: Eastern Pyarados Trail
entries: Once the characters come within a half mile of Tax Station Number 18, read or paraphrase the following:
Fifty feet down the trail, an armored human man and woman and a centaur woman block the trail, blades drawn. "Stop!" shouts one of the soldiers. "State your—"

His command becomes a pained shout as a seven-foot-tall, mantis-like monster leaps from behind a boulder near him and slices his shoulder with a clawed arm. Two clawed fiends ambush the other soldier, who screams in rage. The soldiers turn to face the monsters in battle.

Much farther down the trail, a flying woman in Red Wizard robes points and laughs before rushing toward the stone keep on the horizon. A warrior wearing spiked armor and bearing a greataxe flies at the wizard's side.
Use map. 4.1 for this encounter.

The militia members are the humans Tilda Ven and Yaris (Medium, Neutral Good {@creature Warrior Veteran|XMM|Warrior Veterans}) and the centaur woman Ezkaar Softhoof ({@creature Centaur Trooper|XMM}). The monsters are an {@creature Abveku|AUD} demon and two {@creature Glabrezu|XMM|Glabrezus}. If the characters don't intervene, the demons kill Yaris and Tilda after 2 rounds of combat. The demons kill Ezkaar after the next round.
If the characters join the combat against the demons immediately, the demons focus on them in the fight. In this case, Yaris and Tilda are each reduced to 46 HP, and Ezkaar is unharmed.

The human Red Wizard is Omina (Medium, Neutral Evil {@creature Mage|XMM}), who has cast the {@spell Fly|XPHB} spell on herself. The goliath warrior with her is Garos (Medium, Neutral Evil {@creature Berserker Commander|XMM}), Omina's Thayan knight, on whom the wizard has cast the {@spell Fly|XPHB} spell using a {@item Spell Scroll|XDMG}. Omina and Garos are headed to the tax station's battlements ({@area area S5|196|x}) to oversee the demons' attack on the keep. When this combat begins, they are 160 feet away from the northernmost area depicted on map 4.1.

entries.name: Development
entries: If the characters save them, the militia members are grateful but worried about their compatriots. They run toward Tax Station Number 18, shouting for the characters to help them defend the keep against the Red Wizard and her knight.

entries.name: Tax Station Number 18
entries: The militia's keep was once a tax station where tharch officials collected tolls from miners headed from Pyarados city to the mines in the Sunrise Mountains' foothills. Traffic has been sparse in recent years, though, so the tharchion closed the keep, and it has fallen into disrepair. The former tax station remained empty until the Pyarados militia formed and co-opted it.

The militia has been using the keep as a garrison, surviving off supplies donated by local miners. Recently, travelers the militia has saved from malefite attacks have stayed in the keep as they recovered from their ordeals.

entries.name: Approaching the Station
entries: Read or paraphrase the following when the characters approach the station's courtyard ({@area area S1|18a|x}):

Before you rises a squat fortress besieged by fiends. Near the fortress's gate, two red-skinned abominations and a serpentine horror with six arms battle three outmatched soldiers struggling to stand their ground. On the battlements, a red-robed woman and armored knight survey the scene smugly, a serpentine monster by their side.

entries.name: Station Features
entries: The station has the following features.

entries.name: Ceilings
entries: Inside the keep, the ceilings in areas S2 and S3 are 30 feet high, the ceiling in {@area area S4|195|x} is 40 feet high, and the ceiling in the basement ({@area S6|198|x}) is 15 feet high.

entries.name: Lighting
entries: During the day, {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} illuminates the keep's interior. Sunlight streams through the partially collapsed roof, and light sconces illuminate interior rooms (areas {@area S3|190|x}, {@area S4|195|x}, and {@area S6|198|x}).

entries.name: Partially Collapsed Roof
entries: Part of the roof over the keep's interior ({@area area S2|18d|x}) has collapsed, leaving a pile of rubble.

entries.name: Station Locations
entries: The following locations are keyed to map 4.2. Descriptions assume the characters aid the militia during the attacks described. If they don't, in 10 minutes Omina, Garos, and the demons kill every member of the militia, as well as the locals hiding in the basement, then leave the area.

entries.name: S1: Courtyard

entries: Two enormous, red-skinned fiends with two arms resembling a human's and two more ending in massive claws are battling three soldiers. A six-armed, serpentine monster slavers nearby.

The monsters are two {@creature Glabrezu|XMM|Glabrezus}, which each have 100 HP remaining, and a {@creature Marilith|XMM}, which has 150 HP remaining. If the characters intervene, the demons leave the soldiers alone and focus on fighting the characters. In this case, the soldiers (Medium {@creature Warrior Veteran|XMM|Warrior Veterans}), are reduced to 49 HP and retreat down the trail. The stone doors to the station's main chamber (area S2) are open.

entries.name: Development
entries: The soldiers are Kellen Tol and Merias, both humans, and Serafina, a tiefling. If they survive the fight, they thank the characters and frantically beg them to help the militia members trapped inside the keep.

entries.title: If the characters don't act quickly, demons murder the inhabitants of the tax station.

entries.name: S2: Main Chamber

entries: Chaos has erupted in this chamber, where desks and bunk beds have been smashed to kindling by the enormous quadrupedal monster pummeling the closed stone doors to the northeast. A smaller door stands in the southwest corner, and ten feet above, a gantry surrounds the room.
The monster is a {@creature Rendelith|AUD}. Areas with rubble in them are {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB}.

entries.name: Gantry
entries: Ladders in the southwest corner, one on each side of the square tower, lead 10 feet up to the chamber's gantry.

entries.name: S3: Audience Chamber
entries: The doors to this chamber are made of stone and locked. The lock is Simple (1 action to pick) and of Superior quality ({@dc 20}). (See "Doors" in the {@book Dungeon Master's Guide|XDMG|2|Doors}.) In addition to the lock, the soldiers have barricaded the door with planks from smashed chairs; opening the door requires a successful {@dc 25} Strength check if the soldiers inside don't remove the barricades. The soldiers agree to remove the barricades only if the characters shout through the door that the demons are dead. Otherwise, Fallon Nor (see below) refuses to let the characters inside the room or speak with them.
When the characters enter the room, read or paraphrase the following:

This sparse office is furnished with a threadbare rug and a desk. Standing before the desk is a harried-looking human woman with a greatsword. Four soldiers—two orcs and two goliaths—huddle against the northern wall. A staircase to the south leads upward.

entries.name: Meeting the Soldiers
entries: The woman near the desk is the militia's commander, Fallon Nor (Medium, Neutral Good {@creature Warrior Commander|XMM}). The four soldiers are two orcs named Garth and Letta and two goliaths named Bram and Marta (Medium {@creature Warrior Veteran|XMM|Warrior Veterans}).

entries.name: Commander Nor
entries: Nor's top priority is ensuring the militia's members are safe. She won't talk to the characters while any enemies still attack the fortress. See "{@area Concluding the Mission|1da|x}" for more about talking with Nor.

entries.name: Secret Trapdoor
entries: A secret trapdoor (marked with an S on the map; {@dc 20} to notice) lies underneath the thin rug in the room's center. The trapdoor leads to the basement ({@area area S6|198|x}).

entries.name: S4: Southwest Tower
entries: A staircase winds upward, terminating in a door that leads to the roof.
The cramped staircase leads 30 feet upward.

entries.name: S5: Battlements

entries: A human woman in red robes with tattoos covering her face flies just above the battlements, surveying the chaos beneath her with a wicked smile. A goliath knight with his face similarly tattooed floats beside her, while a six-armed fiend stands on the roof, looking ready to leap through the hole into the areas below.
Omina (Medium, Neutral Evil {@creature Mage|XMM}) and Garos (Medium, Neutral Evil {@creature Berserker Commander|XMM}) survey the battles below. The demon is a {@creature Marilith|XMM}.
These three fight the characters if the party enters this area. All three fight to the death; Omina shouts praise to Szass Tam through the entire fight, though Garos stays silent.
If the characters have defeated the monsters elsewhere in the keep, Omina, Garos, and the demon confront them and start combat.

entries.name: S6: Basement

entries: Cots are set up here alongside piles of food, water, and other survival supplies. Half a dozen disheveled, scared people huddle in groups, whispering fearfully.
The people here—six {@creature Commoner|XMM|Commoners} of various species—have been staying at the station after malefites attacked them nearby.
If the characters defeat all the demons in the keep, these folk erupt in joy and herald the adventurers as saviors.

entries.name: Concluding the Mission
entries: If all the militia members survive, Fallon Nor profusely thanks the characters. If any members die, she asks the characters to restore them to life. If the characters decline, Nor understands the characters' reasons. She asks the characters to join her and the surviving militia members in a moment of respectful silence to honor the dead's sacrifice.

If Nor and any other militia members survive the ordeal, Nor agrees to ally the militia with the characters against Szass Tam. She accepts the {@item Sending Stones|XDMG|Sending Stone} and agrees to report activity in the area related to Szass Tam and his allies. She is pleased to hear about the characters' goal and promises to do anything she can to help take the lich down.
If no other militia members survive, Nor refuses to ally with the characters.

entries.name: Mission Reward
entries: If the characters' mission is successful, they receive one magic item from the list in "{@area Mission Rewards|0da|x}" in chapter 3. Remind the characters to tell Wrynn which item they've chosen as their reward. For bringing Nor and the militia into the fold of Operation Deadfall, each character earns 5,400 XP.

entries.name: An Ancient Temple
entries: When the Mulhorand empire ruled this region, it was inhabited by a warrior people. Their leader, a tiefling named Khamune, dreamed that the Red Knight promised to help his people win independence from the Mulhorandi if they followed her teachings.

Though worship of the Red Knight was almost unknown at the time, Khamune persuaded his people to worship her. He built a temple dedicated to her, declared himself her high commander, and led an uprising against Mulhorand using strategies the deity inspired.

Eventually, the Mulhorand empire crushed the uprising. Khamune fell in battle, and his followers entombed him and other honored dead in the temple along with magical treasures. They magically sealed the temple and scattered into the surrounding lands. Worship of the Red Knight then faded in the region.

entries.name: Trail to the Temple
entries: As the characters travel to the temple, a horde of malefites confronts them on the trail.
Read or paraphrase the following:

A foul wind momentarily chills you to the bone. On the horizon, you see a black-armored knight marching toward you, eyes glowing a malevolent green. Around the knight shamble eight skeletons alight with bright-green flames.
Use {@adventure map 4.1|AUD|4|Map 4.1: Eastern Pyarados Trail} from "Eastern Pyarados Trail" for this encounter.
A {@creature Death Knight|XMM} and eight {@creature Flaming Skeleton|XMM|Flaming Skeletons} fight the characters on sight.

entries.name: Development
entries: After the battle, a character can take the {@action Search|XPHB} action to look for the malefites' tracks. The character makes a {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Survival|XPHB}) check. On a success, the character can follow the malefites' trail, which leads three miles off the road the characters travel.

entries.name: Graveyard
entries: The malefites' tracks end at an overgrown graveyard with nine crumbling headstones. The largest headstone reads, "Here lies Greta Zann, champion of Pyarados, who fell to the Mulhorandi 978 DR." The other headstones are illegible.

The graves are open and empty. A faint wisp of green energy glows at the bottom of each grave. A character can take the {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine the graves and make a {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) check. On a success, the character realizes that Szass Tam's foul magic recently animated the corpses.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: At the bottom of Zann's grave is an {@item Oil of Sharpness|XDMG} that she never had a chance to use.

entries.name: What's Next
entries: The characters can easily find their way back to the road that leads to the temple.

entries.name: Temple of the Red Knight
entries: The Temple of the Red Knight in Pyarados is built into a sheer limestone cliff at the foot of the Sunrise Mountains.

entries.name: Lost Research Team
entries: Although the outside of the temple suggests it's abandoned, an eccentric Red Wizard archaeologist named Nazemm, a human from the city of Pyarados, recently entered the complex with a team of spellcasting academics to learn about this ancient group of Red Knight worshippers. The team decoded the temple's entry requirements (see {@area area E1|1ac|x}) and ventured inside, bypassing the building's traps and locked doors.

Unfortunately for the academics, Nazemm accidentally invoked an ancient inscription meant to protect Khamune's tomb ({@area area E10|1d3|x}) from Mulhorandi robbers. The invocation awakened several undead within the complex, including Khamune.

entries.title: The Red Knight's Holy Symbol

entries: These undead slew Nazemm and most of his team members. Their bodies lie scattered about the temple. The sole survivor, Valzaa, hides in a sarcophagus in Khamune's tomb, desperately hoping to escape.

entries.name: Temple Features
entries: The temple has the following features.

entries.name: Ceilings
entries: Interior ceilings in rooms are 30 feet high. Hallway ceilings (including areas {@area E2|1b3|x}, {@area E6|1c5|x}, and {@area E8|1cc|x}) are 15 feet high.

entries.name: Doors
entries: The temple's doors are made of stone. The door to the temple is locked (see {@area area E1|1ac|x}). Interior doors are unlocked except for the door in the worship chamber ({@area area E5|1be|x}) that leads to the eastern hallway ({@area area E6|1c5|x}). (See "Doors" in the {@book Dungeon Master's Guide|XDMG|2|Doors}.)

entries.name: Secret Doors
entries: Unless otherwise noted, secret doors (marked with an S on the map; {@dc 18} to notice) blend with the surrounding walls.

entries.name: Lighting
entries: The entire temple is in {@variantrule Darkness|XPHB}, except the worship chamber ({@area area E5|1be|x}), where torches shed {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB}. Descriptions assume characters have a way to see in the dark.

entries.name: Mummy Lord's Lair
entries: The Temple of the Red Knight is the lair of Khamune, who has risen as a mummy lord. The temple has the features of a mummy lord lair described in the {@creature Mummy Lord|XMM|Monster Manual}.

entries.name: Temple Locations

images.title: Map 4.3: Temple of the Red Knight

entries: The following locations are keyed to map 4.3.

entries.name: E1: Temple Entrance

entries: A five-foot-wide copper bowl on a marble base sits before this imposing temple facade, which consists of limestone pillars supporting a rock overhang extending from the sheer cliff. Beneath the overhang, a small door is recessed into the cliff. Flanking the bowl are two red granite statues of knights, their hands touching sheathed swords. Strange writing is carved into every inch of the pillars.
The temple's entrance once welcomed the Red Knight's faithful.

entries.name: Door
entries: The door to the temple is locked from the outside. The lock is Complex (1 minute to pick) and of Superior quality ({@dc 20}).

entries.name: Statues
entries: The statues near the bowl are golems. One uses the {@creature Iron Golem|XMM} stat block, and the other uses the {@creature Stone Golem|XMM} stat block. The statues fight the characters if they try to open the door without performing the rite described below.

entries.name: Copper Bowl
entries: The empty bowl's marble base is carved with ancient writing meant to keep the temple sealed. Khamune's people built a workaround into the seal, however, in case their descendants ever returned to reclaim the temple.

The writing's language is similar to ancient Mulhorandi. A character who speaks Mulhorandi can translate the writing by taking the {@action Study|XPHB} action and succeeding on a {@dc 18} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check.

The writing says, "Though we have failed, through strategy we may yet succeed. When you return, O children, offer the Crimson General a gift. Speak these words and pour any magical or sacred elixir into the bowl to achieve victory."

entries.name: Performing the Rite
entries: Anyone who learns the translation realizes it means that one must pour any magic potion or a flask of {@item Holy Water|XPHB} into the bowl while speaking the translation aloud in any language. A character can do so as an action.
If a character performs the rite, the temple door unlocks and remains unlocked for 5 minutes. The door isn't locked from the inside.

entries.name: The Pillars' Writing
entries: Consisting of unique arcane runes, the writing covering the pillars is magical and dates to the tomb's construction. As a {@action Study|XPHB} action, a character can examine the writing and make a {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB} or {@skill History|XPHB}) check. On a success, the character determines that the writing invokes the temple's ancient magic, which has prevented Szass Tam's experiments from transforming the temple's dead occupants into malefites.

entries.name: E2: Entry Tunnel

entries: Steep steps in this cramped tunnel lead downward, then the hall turns north.
This hallway leads deeper into the complex.

entries.name: Secret Door
entries: A secret door at the first bend in the tunnel leads to the temple's central hallway ({@area area E8|1cc|x}). See "{@area Temple Features|1a5|x}" for details. Should the characters pass this secret door after exploring {@area area E3|1b6|x} and not finding the secret door there, they have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on finding the secret door in this hall.

entries.name: E3: Entry Chamber

entries: This chamber's four pillars are covered in ancient writing, and murals adorn the walls. Eight upright sarcophagi stand against the walls, their lids scattered around the room. Within each sarcophagus is a motionless, desiccated body. On a central dais, a fifteen-foot-tall, red stone statue of a knight drawing her sword overlooks the area.

When a character steps onto the center dais, the eight {@creature Ghast Gravecaller|XMM|Ghast Gravecallers} in the sarcophagi animate and fight the characters. These are lieutenants of Khamune who rose in undeath to defend the temple when the academics invoked the protective inscription in Khamune's tomb ({@area area E10|1d3|x}).

entries.name: Hidden Compartment
entries: The base of the central statue contains a hidden compartment ({@dc 20} to notice). The compartment is locked. A character can take the {@action Utilize|XPHB} action to try to pick the lock using {@item Thieves' Tools|XPHB}, doing so with a successful {@dc 18} Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand|XPHB}) check. The compartment contains a {@item Potion of Speed|XDMG}.

entries.name: Murals
entries: The murals all show images of a knight in red armor standing tall above a force of smaller warriors. The knight leads a valiant charge against unarmored warriors led by a tall man in pharaonic garb.

entries.name: Pillars
entries: A character who speaks Mulhorandi can translate the writing on the pillars by taking the {@action Study|XPHB} action and succeeding on a {@dc 18} Intelligence ({@skill History|XPHB}) check.

The writing tells the story of the followers of "Khamune, the sacred high commander." Characters who read the story learn the information about Khamune's people in "{@area An Ancient Temple|19c|x}" earlier in this chapter.

entries.name: Secret Door
entries: A secret door in the northeastern wall behind a sarcophagus leads to the temple's worship chamber (area {@area E5|1be|x}); see "{@area Temple Features|1a7|x}" for details.

entries.name: E4: Storage Chamber

entries: This small chamber holds only shreds of rotted cloth and wood and other refuse.
This room once held sacks of grain and other supplies, but anything of interest here has rotted away.

entries.name: E5: Worship Chamber

entries: Murals of supplicants praying to a red-armored knight adorn these walls and the south door. Four pedestals hold lit torches, while a pedestal with a skull resting atop it is in the room's center.
This was once a room where the Red Knight's faithful meditated on battle strategies. When they sealed the temple, they installed a trap here to prevent intruders from moving farther inside.

entries.name: Dart Trap
entries: There's a pressure plate on this room's floor, which is denoted by a T on the map. The pressure plate triggers a poisoned darts trap, as described in the {@trap Poisoned Darts|XDMG|Dungeon Master's Guide}, except the Dexterity saving throw DC is 15, and each dart deals 14 ({@dice 4d6}) Poison damage.

entries.name: Locked Door Puzzle
entries: The door to the hallway to the south ({@area area E6|1c5|x}) is locked. The lock is Complex (1 minute to pick) and of Superior quality ({@dc 20}).

A character who takes the {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine the door realizes the mural shows a magical way to unlock it. The mural depicts supplicants raising their hands in praise to the Red Knight. The supplicants stand in a line, and each but the one on the westernmost edge holds a torch.
If the characters take the torches from the nearby pedestals and stand in a formation that matches the mural, the door unlocks.

entries.name: Pedestals with Torches
entries: Each pedestal holds a torch lit with a {@spell continual flame|XPHB} spell. A character can remove a torch easily (no action required).

entries.name: Secret Door
entries: In the tunnel to the east, the door to {@area area E3|1b6|x} is plainly visible.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: The skull on the central pedestal obscures a receptacle containing the following:

entries.name: E6: Eastern Hallway

entries: This long hallway runs from north to south. Five alcoves that hold sarcophagi punctuate the east side of the wall. Down the hall, the desiccated body of a robed figure lies slumped on the ground.
This hallway holds the sarcophagi of Khamune's lieutenants. These lieutenants were not raised from the dead when Nazemm invoked the inscription in Khamune's tomb ({@area area E10|1d3|x}).

entries.name: Corpse
entries: This hall holds the body of Ralpheen, a human apprentice of Nazemm. A character can take the {@action Search|XPHB} action to examine Ralpheen's wounds and make a {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Medicine|XPHB}) check. On a success, the character determines that Necrotic damage killed him recently. (The undead mage in area E7 slew him.) If the characters can speak to Ralpheen, he tells them everything in "{@area Lost Research Team|1a4|x}" earlier in this chapter, except he doesn't know Valzaa is still alive.

entries.name: E7: Tomb of the Resting Wizard

entries: This chamber appears to be a magical workshop. Two tables covered in rotting books, flaking scrolls, and strange implements stand along the west wall. A heavy desk sits in the southeast corner, and unlit braziers dot the room's corners. A thick layer of dust covers everything.

A mage named Teketh who once served Khamune died here. Her skeleton was disturbed by Ralpheen, Nazemm's apprentice (Ralpheen's body lies in {@area area E6|1c5|x}). The skeleton crumbled to dust save for its skull, which animated (use the stat block of a {@creature Demilich|XMM}, except Teketh has no lair and lacks the Undead Restoration trait). Teketh killed Ralpheen, then retreated here and now rests underneath the desk.

entries.name: Disturbing Teketh
entries: If any character searches the desk in the room's southeast corner, Teketh fights the characters, following them into other areas of the temple if necessary.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: The following magic items lie scattered atop the tables in this room:

items: {@item Figurine of Wondrous Power|XDMG|Figurine of Wondrous Power (silver raven)}
{@item Spell Scroll|XDMG} {@i of} {@spell Aura of Vitality|XPHB}

entries.name: E8: Central Hallway
entries: This long hallway stretches the length of the temple, east to west. A corridor near the east end leads north, while one near the west end leads south; just past it, the hallway ends at a door. A robed body lies crumpled near the west corridor.
This hallway runs east to west through the center of the temple. The eastern corridor leads to the tomb of the high commander ({@area area E10|1d3|x}).

entries.name: Corpse
entries: The central hall holds the body of Nadia, a human apprentice of Nazemm. A character can take the {@action Search|XPHB} action to examine Nadia's wounds and make a {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Medicine|XPHB}) check. On a success, the character determines Nadia died recently after taking Slashing and Necrotic damage from a Melee weapon. (The undead general in {@area area E9|1cf|x} slew her.) If the characters can speak to Nadia, she tells them everything in "{@area Lost Research Team|1a4|x}" earlier in this chapter, except she doesn't know Valzaa is still alive.

entries.name: Secret Door
entries: The secret door to the entry tunnel ({@area area E2|1b3|x}) is plainly visible from this side.

entries.name: E9: General's Tomb

entries.title: An ancient general rises as a death knight to fight the characters.

entries: Lines of ancient writing cover this chamber's walls. On the far side of the room stands a suit of armor and a weapon rack holding two swords and a mace. A stone sarcophagus stands at the center of the chamber atop a five-foot-high platform; its lid has been pushed aside. Additional closed sarcophagi lie to the east and west.

This is the burial chamber of Khamune's general, Mekuni. Now a {@creature Death Knight|XMM}, Mekuni lies in the central sarcophagus while her two loyal strategists lie in the flanking tombs. Mekuni killed Nadia, the apprentice in the central hallway ({@area area E8|1cc|x}), after the apprentice disturbed her rest; the general then returned to her sarcophagus.
When a creature moves more than 5 feet into the room, Mekuni rises to fight the characters, along with two {@creature Wraith|XMM|Wraiths} that rise from the sarcophagi on either side of the room.

entries.name: Writing
entries: A character who speaks Mulhorandi can translate the ancient writing on the wall by taking the {@action Study|XPHB} action and succeeding on a {@dc 18} Intelligence ({@skill History|XPHB}) check.
The writing tells of the loyalty of a general named Mekuni, Khamune's second in command. Mekuni and her strategists, Dalni and Hamsu, died defending Khamune from Mulhorandi assassins.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: In each of this chamber's corners sits an ivory jar emblazoned with the Red Knight's symbol and worth 500 GP.
The following armor and weapons sit on the far side of the room:

entries.name: E10: Tomb of the High Commander

entries: The tomb's heavy stone doors hang open, revealing a large central sarcophagus on a raised dais. The sarcophagus's lid, covered in ancient writing, has been pushed to the ground. Two open sarcophagi lie to the south and east, while a closed sarcophagus rests to the west. Murals and ancient script adorn the walls.
Lording over a slumped, red-robed body is a tiefling mummy with glowing red eyes and wearing ceremonial armor. Two desiccated warriors stand at attention next to the mummy.

The mummy is Khamune ({@creature Mummy Lord|XMM}), the high commander of the Red Knight, who was interred here. The two warriors were Khamune's personal guards. They each use the stat block of a {@creature Berserker Commander|XMM}, except their creature type is Undead. The creatures fight the characters on sight, following them into other parts of the temple if necessary.

entries.name: Corpse
entries: The body is Nazemm, the Red Wizard and archaeologist who led the ill-fated expedition into the temple. Nazemm read aloud the writing inscribed on Khamune's sarcophagus lid, which awakened many of the dead interred in the temple. If the characters can speak to Nazemm, he tells them everything in "{@area Lost Research Team|1a4|x}" earlier in this chapter, except he doesn't know Valzaa is still alive.

entries.name: Hiding Apprentice
entries: If the characters stand within 5 feet of the closed sarcophagus to the west, they hear whimpering. Inside the sarcophagus hides the only survivor of Nazemm's research team: a human apprentice named Valzaa (Medium, Chaotic Good {@creature Mage Apprentice|XMM}). If the characters remove the lid, they find Valzaa hiding beside a dead guard who didn't animate with the rest. Once she realizes the characters aren't enemies, Valzaa begs them to escort her back to the city of Pyarados. She can tell the characters everything in "{@area Lost Research Team|1a4|x}" earlier in this chapter.

entries.name: Lid Inscription
entries: The magic in the sarcophagus's lid inscription is gone now that Nazemm accidentally activated it. A character who speaks Mulhorandi can translate the ancient inscription on the lid by taking the {@action Study|XPHB} action and succeeding on a {@dc 18} Intelligence ({@skill History|XPHB}) check.
The inscription says, "Our high commander remains vigilant in death. The Red Knight shall visit horrors on those who disturb his peace."

entries.name: Murals and Writing
entries: The chamber's walls are covered in murals of a tiefling man wearing red armor, as well as lines of ancient writing. A character who speaks Mulhorandi can translate the writing on the wall by taking the {@action Study|XPHB} action and succeeding on a {@dc 18} Intelligence ({@skill History|XPHB}) check.

The writing tells how Khamune served his people and the Red Knight and fought the Mulhorandi. He won numerous skirmishes before the empire crushed the uprising; each time, Khamune gave the spoils of these battles to his soldiers, never keeping any riches for himself.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: In each of this chamber's corners stands an ivory jar emblazoned with the Red Knight's symbol and worth 500 GP.
Inside Khamune's sarcophagus lies the {@item Spirit-Binding Censer|AUD} (see {@area appendix A|358|x}), the Artifact the characters seek.

entries.name: Concluding the Mission
entries: The characters' mission is successful if they retrieve the {@item Spirit-Binding Censer|AUD}.

entries.name: Mission Reward
entries: If the characters' mission is successful, they receive one magic item from the list in "Mission Rewards" in {@area chapter 3|0da|x}. Remind the characters to tell Wrynn which item they've chosen as their reward. Additionally, each character earns 6,200 XP.

entries.name: Szass Tam's Agents
entries: If the characters haven't remained discreet about their intent to defeat Szass Tam, the lich's operatives track the characters down when they return to Eltabbar. You can skip this encounter if the characters have remained discreet. (See "{@area Importance of Secrecy|099|x}" in chapter 2 for more about emphasizing discretion and guile.)
On the other hand, even if the characters have remained discreet, you might run this encounter if the characters failed either mission in chapter 2.
Use {@adventure map 3.6|AUD|3|Map 3.6: Lower Ward Alley} for this encounter, though it takes place in the Lower Ward.
Read or paraphrase the following:

Three figures blink into existence in front of you: two humans with shaved, tattooed heads wearing red robes and a hulking, horned fiend with leathery wings and curving horns. The fiend chuckles in a deep, menacing tone while one of the humans points at you. "We know you stand against our liege," she says. "Szass Tam will reward us handsomely for bringing him your heads!"

The humans are the lich's operatives, siblings and Red Wizards named Onar and Parah Lang (Neutral Evil {@creature Archmage|XMM|Archmages}), who are diabolists. Accompanying the Red Wizards is a {@creature Horned Devil|XMM} allied with their family. Onar cast the {@spell Teleport|XPHB} spell on the group to ambush the characters.
The siblings hope Szass Tam will hand them control of Eltabbar if they eliminate the characters. The Red Wizards and devil fight the characters to the death.

data.name: Chapter 5: Rebel Alliances
entries: {@i Seek aid from dissident Red Wizards and pirates}.

entries.title: From Left to Right: the Red Wizards Abadesh, Darvyn Yev, Iorru, Sabinia Dau, and Zeil

entries.name: Key Plot Points
entries: The following information is key to this chapter's story:

items.name: Ally with Dissident Red Wizards
items.entry: The characters travel to a hidden tower outside Eltabbar to enlist the help of iconoclastic mages in reaching Szass Tam's ritual area.

items.name: Recruit the Pirates
items.entry: The characters travel to Thay's island tharch to ask a band of pirates to attack ships carrying foci Szass Tam needs to boost his ritual.

entries.name: Preparation
entries: Before running this chapter, prepare as follows:

items.name: Step 1
items.entry: Read the "{@area Running This Chapter|1e1|x}" section, including "{@area Character Advancement|1e2|x}." Decide with your players which mission the characters will tackle first or run them in the order presented.

items.name: Step 2
items.entry: Familiarize yourself with the Key NPCs table below.

items.name: Step 3
items.entry: Bookmark the stat blocks below, which appear in the {@book Monster Manual|XMM} and on D&D Beyond unless otherwise noted. If a stat block appears in appendix B, an asterisk appears after its name:

entries.caption: Key NPCs
rows: Human dissident Red Wizard and owner of the Veiled Tower
Human leader of pirate crew at Blackrock Cove
Lich plotting to conquer Thay and primary target of Operation Deadfall
Human tailor and Zulkir Thrul's spy master
Human zulkir of evocation and Operation Deadfall's leader

entries.name: Running This Chapter
entries: This chapter takes place after the characters have completed their missions in Pyarados.

entries.name: Character Advancement
entries: The characters should be level 15 when this chapter begins. They should have enough XP to advance to level 16 before they embark on their second mission in this chapter. They should reach level 17 by the end of this chapter. If you're using a method of level advancement that doesn't rely on XP, the characters gain levels at those points.

entries.name: Returning to the Zulkir
entries: When the characters go to Wrynn's Bespoke Vestments to meet with Zulkir Thrul, they find Wynston Wrynn thanking a young elf man who's leaving the shop with his arms piled high with {@item Fine Clothes|XPHB}.

The tailor ushers the characters into the shop's secret office and whispers into a {@item Sending Stones|XDMG|Sending Stone}. A few moments later, Zulkir Thrul arrives via the {@spell Teleport|XPHB} spell, undisguised. She casts the {@spell Demiplane|XPHB} spell and escorts the group through the shadowy door that appears on the wall.

entries.name: Fifth and Sixth Missions
entries: After the characters tell the zulkir about their previous missions, she gives them details about their next ones. Read or paraphrase the following:
"Operatives, we approach your confrontation with the Hydra," says Zulkir Thrul. "However, you first must accomplish two tasks.

"You must visit a tower cloaked in illusions, called the Veiled Tower. Within it are five dissident Red Wizards, code-named the Mavericks, who are vocal about their hatred for the Hydra. These Red Wizards seek a magical way to access the area of Thaymount you must infiltrate to stop the Hydra's ritual. You must convince the Mavericks to share their magical knowledge with you.

"In addition, I want you to travel to Blackrock Cove on the island Alaor Minor. Parlay with the pirates lairing there, code-named the Blades, and ask them to destroy each ship on a list I'll give you. These ships belong to Red Wizards and carry foci the Hydra needs to empower his ritual; without the foci, he will be easier to defeat.
"You may complete these tasks in any order."
The zulkir then hands the characters a piece of parchment containing the names of four ships:

The zulkir explains that the list is cloaked with an {@spell Illusory Script|XPHB} spell. The characters can read it, as can Captain Sharlei, the pirates' leader, but to anyone else, the writing looks like a list of common spell components.
The zulkir can provide the following information about the dissident Red Wizards:

items.name: Who Are the Mavericks?
items.entry: "Their leader is an urbane human man named Darvyn Yev. The others are the humans Zeil, Abadesh, and Iorru, and the tiefling Sabinia Dau, who's an old friend of mine. These Red Wizards have vocally opposed the Hydra and have correctly deduced he plans to violently regain his regency. They fear he might send assassins, so they're hiding in the Veiled Tower, which belongs to Darvyn."

items.name: What Can You Tell Us About the Mavericks?
