items.entry: "They all hate the Hydra, but they're not exactly benevolent. They're interested in self-preservation first and self-aggrandizement second; one might call them cowardly. But if you tell them your plans to stop the Hydra, I suspect they'll ally with us."

items.name: What Magical Technique Are They Developing?
items.entry: "They're devising a magical way to travel to a specific location near the Citadel in central Thaymount. Sabinia maintains a fortress near the Citadel; I suspect they hope to teleport near it to ride out the Hydra's impending attack. This fortress lies close to Castle Thrul, my family's keep, which holds an old underground passageway into the Citadel. When the time is right, this is how you'll strike at the Hydra."

items.name: Why Can't We Go to Thaymount Another Way?
items.entry: "Thaymount is covered in magical effects that prevent teleportation and magical travel. Even flying to Thaymount is dangerous, as the cliffs that surround the plateau are heavily trapped and guarded by the Hydra's agents. The only safe place to travel to is Szul, but the Hydra knows about every creature that arrives there. The Hydra is unlikely to suspect that foes will teleport to and shelter at his doorstep, though. I believe this is the best way for you to travel to Thaymount." For more about Thaymount's magical effects, see "{@area Magic on Thaymount|270|x}" in chapter 6.

entries: The zulkir can provide the following information about the pirates of Blackrock Cove:

items.name: How Should We Get to Blackrock Cove?
items.entry: "The portal will take you to Ala City, where I suggest you hire a boat. If you hire a boat captain, don't tell them details and don't bring them into the Blades' hideout. I don't recommend you use magic to travel to the cove, since the Blades might assume you're enemies. You aren't there to fight the Blades, so make it clear you're not a threat."

items.name: Who Are the Blades?
items.entry: "Most are disgraced former members of the Thayan navy, led by Captain Sharlei. Rumor claims she went into hiding after killing a Red Wizard."

items.name: Why Are the Blades in Blackrock Cove?
items.entry: "Large ships find Blackrock Cove difficult to navigate, though Captain Sharlei can hide her vessel there easily. Rumor also claims an ocean spirit protects the cove from intruders. It's hogwash, but Red Wizards have tried and failed to attack the Blades many times. Approach cautiously, operatives."

items.name: Will the Blades Destroy These Ships?
items.entry: "I believe they will, as long as you convince them the ships aim to help the Hydra. Bear in mind the Blades likely will want something from you in return. Do what you must to win them to our cause."

items.name: Why Don't We Destroy These Ships Ourselves?
items.entry: "I have only the ships' names, not their locations. But the Blades watch all ships' movement. They should have no problem hunting these four ships."

items.name: What Ritual Foci Do These Ships Carry?
items.entry: "The ships carry cursed skulls of slain fiends that will empower the Hydra's ritual. These skulls are hundreds of years old and harbor incredible evil power. Once the skulls reach mainland Thay, the Hydra's associates will arrange for quick delivery to him via teleportation. That must not happen."

entries: After Thrul answers questions, she provides directions to the Veiled Tower and Blackrock Cove:

"To reach both destinations, you must first travel thirty miles west of the city, where the River Eltar flows down the cliffs of the Second Escarpment. There, near a waterfall, you'll find a curious rock formation that looks like a V.
"Near the rock formation stands the Veiled Tower, where the dissident Red Wizards hide. To find the tower, you must pierce the illusions that conceal it.

"To reach Blackrock Cove from the rock formation, travel two miles north along the escarpment's base. Find a rocky outcropping that looks like a skull, and enter the cave at its base. You'll find a permanent magical portal there.
"The portal leads to Ala City on the island Alaor Major. There you can hire a boat to take you to the cove, which is on the southeast coast of Alaor Minor."
When the characters are ready to approach the Mavericks, see "Veiled Tower." When they're ready to meet the Blades, see "{@area Magical Portal|212|x}."

entries.name: Veiled Tower
entries: The Veiled Tower is nestled against a cliff in the Second Escarpment near Eltabbar. Darvyn Yev, a Red Wizard scion of a prestigious family of Red Wizards, owns it. Yev's ancestors built it centuries ago.

entries.name: The Mavericks
entries: The Red Wizards in the Veiled Tower are friends who are convinced that Szass Tam soon will become Thay's regent—and are angry about it. All five are {@creature Archmage|XMM|Archmages} who are described below.

entries.name: Abadesh
entries: {@i Self-Indulgent Survivor}

items.name: Species:
items.entry: Human

items.name: Personal Goal:
items.entry: Avoid becoming the lich's servitor

entries: Abadesh was a young man during Szass Tam's last regency and remembers how readily the lich turned dissenters into undead servants. When Yev extended an invitation to hide in the Veiled Tower, Abadesh happily accepted, knowing his association with Szass Tam's enemies puts a target on his back.

entries.name: Darvyn Yev

entries.title: The Red Wizard Darvyn Yev has a deadly surprise for unwelcome visitors.

entries: {@i Egotistical Libertine}

items.name: Species:
items.entry: Human

items.name: Personal Goal:
items.entry: Protect himself from the lich

entries: Known for his dark, beautifully coiffed hair and elegant facial tattoos, Darvyn Yev is from Eltabbar, where his family commands great prestige. Despite his powerful spellcasting, he has failed to equal his forebears' magical accomplishments. He compensates for this by cultivating his appearance and indulging in luxuries. He's vocal about his belief that Szass Tam will strip all beauty and joy from Thay.

entries.name: Iorru
entries: {@i Bookish Scholar of Necromancy}

items.name: Species:
items.entry: Human

items.name: Personal Goal:
items.entry: Speak against Szass Tam freely

entries: Iorru believes in studying the forces of life and death, not using them to cow one's enemies. Iorru earned her red robes from a Red Wizard called Reng, who is Szass Tam's ally. She recently voiced her dislike of the lich to Reng, who put a bounty on her head. She hides in the Veiled Tower with her friends, whom she trusts to help protect her.

entries.name: Sabinia Dau
entries: {@i Spirited Social Commenter}

items.name: Species:
items.entry: Tiefling

items.name: Personal Goal:
items.entry: Stoke dissent against Szass Tam

entries: Sabinia Dau comes from a politically powerful, mostly human family. She is a childhood friend of Zulkir Thrul, though Dau focused more on magical research and less on politics than Thrul did. The two remain friendly and occasionally spend time together in Thaymount. ({@area The Fortress of Opposition|276|x}, Dau's stronghold in Thaymount, is detailed in chapter 6.) Dau recently published a pamphlet titled "Death to Tyrants" that singled out Szass Tam as Thay's biggest threat. Dau expects Szass Tam's loyalists to retaliate, so she hides in the Veiled Tower.

entries.name: Zeil
entries: {@i Brilliant Business Magnate}

items.name: Species:
items.entry: Human

items.name: Personal Goal:
items.entry: Avoid Szass Tam's wrath

entries: Unlike most Red Wizard business owners, Zeil treats her workers with dignity and pays them fairly. She owns a mine in eastern Pyarados, where malefite attacks have raged thanks to Szass Tam's foul magical experiments. When the area became unsafe, Zeil granted her workers paid leave. Correctly convinced that Szass Tam's rumored experiments caused the attacks, Zeil tried and failed to obtain help from multiple authorities. In a fit of rage, she attacked a contingent of Szass Tam loyalists she encountered on the High Road, blaming them for her mine's losses. Zeil barely escaped. Now she hides from the lich, who she's certain will want revenge.

entries.name: Finding the Tower
entries: When Darvyn Yev's ancestors built the tower, they cloaked it with a permanent effect similar to that of the {@spell Mirage Arcane|XPHB} spell. To any creature without {@sense Truesight|XPHB}, the tower is invisible against the cliffs.

Zulkir Thrul knows and carefully describes the tower's location, which is about 30 miles west of the city. She gives the characters each a {@item Spell Scroll|XDMG} {@i of} {@spell True Seeing|XPHB} and instructs them to use the scrolls when they're near the {@i V}-shaped rock formation that signifies the tower's location.
When the characters approach the tower, having pierced the illusion, read or paraphrase:
Through the shimmer of illusion, you see a tall tower that resembles a gigantic, faceted gemstone abutting the cliffs. Seemingly made of obsidian, the tower glistens in the sun.

entries.name: Tower Features
entries: The Veiled Tower, which stands three hundred feet high, is made of magically treated obsidian that has {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to all damage. The tower has the following features.

entries.name: Ceilings
entries: The ceilings in interior areas ({@area V4|202|x}–{@area V5|208|x}) are 60 feet high.

entries.name: Doors
entries: The doors are made of magical obsidian and have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to all damage. They are unlocked, though the exterior doors are well defended (see areas {@area V2|1fc|x} and {@area V3|1ff|x}). See "Doors" in the {@book Dungeon Master's Guide|XDMG|2|Doors}.

entries.name: Exterior Areas
entries: Areas {@area V1|1f7|x}–{@area V3|1ff|x} lie outside the tower.

entries.name: Lighting
entries: Interior areas ({@area V4|202|x}–{@area V5|208|x}) are bathed in {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB}, thanks to {@spell Continual Flame|XPHB} spells cast on artistic sconces in each chamber.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: The Red Wizards' bedrooms (areas {@area V5a–e|208|x}) contain significant treasure. If the characters are caught stealing from any Red Wizard, the Red Wizards demand their treasures be returned immediately. If a character refuses, the Red Wizards fight the characters to the death.

entries.name: Tower Locations
entries: The following locations are keyed to map 5.1.

entries.name: V1: Visitor Reception

entries: A black door knocker adorns the tower four feet above the ground. The door knocker is shaped like a human's bald, tattooed head, and around its neck is a torc that functions as a striker. There is no door in the wall.
This is a false entryway. The tower's interior can be accessed via doors in the middle tier ({@area area V2|1fc|x}) and tower apex ({@area area V3|1ff|x}).

entries.name: Door Knocker
entries: If a character takes the {@action Utilize|XPHB} action to use the knocker, a human man appears, floating beside them just above eye level.
This is Darvyn Yev. When he appears, read or paraphrase the following:
Resplendent in red robes, a flying human man with luxurious dark hair and swirling facial tattoos addresses you in a demanding tone.
"Who dares approach the Veiled Tower? State your business or be gone!"

A character can take the {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine Yev's image and make a {@dc 18} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check. On a success, the character realizes that the image is an illusion. Yev created it using a {@item Spell Scroll|XDMG} {@i of} {@spell Project Image|XPHB}.

entries.name: Gaining an Audience
entries: The characters must convince Yev they need his group's help to stop Szass Tam. A character can take the {@action Influence|XPHB} action to plead their case and make a {@dc 18} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) check. On a success, Yev says, "I see; enter the tower through the door above marked with glyphs. Speak soon. Glory to Yev!" His image disappears.

On a failure, Yev's uproarious laughter echoes off the surrounding cliffs, which begin to rumble. His image sarcastically salutes the characters before it winks out. Two {@creature Purple Worm|XMM|Purple Worms} burst from the rock near the tower 60 feet away and fight the characters on noticing them.
Yev has used a {@item Spell Scroll|XDMG} to cast {@spell Shatter|XPHB} inside the cliff to provoke the lurking worms to emerge. The worms each have 230 HP remaining.

entries.name: V2: Middle Tier

entries: Fifty feet above the ground, a ledge wraps around the tower. In the middle of the tower's south side stands a door covered in strange glyphs and images of robed wizards dramatically casting spells.

A character can take the {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine the glyphs and make a {@dc 18} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) check. On a success, the character realizes the glyphs are powerful magical wards that can be disarmed by speaking a passphrase. The character knows the passphrase includes the family name Yev, but no other details. (The characters can learn the complete passphrase, "Glory to Yev," in area {@area area V3|1ff|x}.)

entries.name: Trapped Door
entries: If a character says the passphrase in any language, the door (marked with a T on the map) is safe to open for 1 minute.

If a creature tries to open the door when no one has said the passphrase, a bolt of electricity shoots from the door. That creature makes a {@dc 15} Dexterity saving throw, taking 55 ({@dice 10d10}) Lightning damage on a failed save or half as much on a successful one.
Inside, a staircase ascends to a lounge ({@area area V4|202|x}).

entries.name: V3: Tower Apex

entries: Three hundred feet up, this platform juts from the tower's apex, overlooking a spectacular scene of lowlands to the east and cliffs to the west. A statue of a knight stands vigilant on the platform. A door in a small enclosure appears to lead inside the tower.
When a creature comes within 5 feet of the door, read or paraphrase the following:
A commanding voice emanates from the knight statue.
"To whom do you give glory? Answer correctly or be deemed intruders!"
The voice is Yev's, speaking through a {@spell Magic Mouth|XPHB} spell he cast on the statue. It triggers when a creature enters this area.

As a {@action Study|XPHB} action, a character can consider the history of the Veiled Tower as a refuge for the Yev family and make a {@dc 18} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check. On a success, they deduce the answer: "Glory to Yev," which is also the passphrase in {@area area V2|1fc|x}.

If a creature gives the correct answer in any language, the statue remains inert. Should the characters fail to answer correctly within a few seconds, the statue animates and fights them. Use the stat block of an {@creature Iron Golem|XMM}; the statue fights until destroyed.
Inside the tower, a spiral staircase descends to a lounge (area V4).

entries.name: V4: Lounge

entries: This brightly lit lounge looks comfortable and lavish, with four beautifully carved statues of mages ringing the room. Sitting around an oak table are five red-robed people—four humans and a tiefling. A dark-haired, well-coiffed human man rises to greet you.
When the characters enter the tower's lounge, each character earns 7,800 XP for gaining access to the mages' inner sanctum.

entries.name: Meeting the Mavericks
entries: The dark-haired man is Darvyn Yev, the tower's owner, and the others are Abadesh, Iorru, Sabinia Dau, and Zeil (Medium {@creature Archmage|XMM|Archmages}; see "{@area The Mavericks|1e8|x}" earlier in this chapter). If the characters didn't explain their mission to Yev in {@area area V1|1f7|x}, he demands to know why they're here.
Should the characters explain their mission, Yev chuckles and begins to speak. See "Impressing the Mavericks" below.

If the characters don't tell the Mavericks they plan to defeat Szass Tam, the mages fight them. When a mage is {@status Bloodied|XPHB}, the four statues (use the {@creature Stone Golem|XMM} stat block) join the fight against the characters.
If the characters belatedly insist they're allies, the Red Wizards stop fighting when a mage becomes {@status Bloodied|XPHB}, and the statues don't attack.

entries.name: Impressing the Mavericks
entries: When the Red Wizards realize the characters intend to defeat Szass Tam, read or paraphrase the following speech from Yev:
"Well, you've managed to enter this tower, but let's see your skills in action. Prove to us you've the mettle to face the dread lich!"

The four statues in the room fight the characters (each uses the {@creature Stone Golem|XMM} stat block). When the characters destroy one, Yev laughs and shouts, "Guardians, enough!" The other statues cease fighting and return to their original positions.

entries.name: Development
entries: Once the Mavericks are convinced the characters are strong enough to face Szass Tam, the mages share the following information in conversation.

items.name: Teleportation Ritual
items.entry: The Red Wizards are indeed working on the ritual Zulkir Thrul described. The ritual's teleportation magic targets a geographical feature in central Thaymount near the Citadel called the Mouth of Despair, which is a deep fissure in the ground.

items.name: How the Ritual Works
items.entry: The Mavericks have discovered that the fissure's floor is only weakly imbued with the anti-teleportation magic that covers the rest of Thaymount. Their ritual will punch through that area's wards, ensuring Szass Tam doesn't know they've arrived in the region.

items.name: Why They'll Travel to Thaymount
items.entry: Although they don't know details about the lich's Malefice Mortum ritual, they believe he is about to regain his regency in some horrible way. Should chaos erupt, they would feel more secure hiding in Thaymount, where they will be better equipped to magically conceal themselves. They plan to hide in Dau's nearby Fortress of Opposition until returning to public life is safe.

entries: The Mavericks agree to take the characters with them to Thaymount via their ritual. However, the ritual isn't complete; the Mavericks didn't consider Szass Tam's threat an urgent one, so they've wasted time drinking wine and crowing to each other about their achievements instead of working.

The amount of time the mages tell the characters it will take to complete their ritual depends on when the group wants to travel to Thaymount. If the characters haven't approached the pirates of Blackrock Cove yet, the mages tell the characters to return in four days. If the characters are ready to go to Thaymount now, the mages tell the characters to return tomorrow.

entries.name: V5a-e: Bedrooms

entries: This comfortable bedroom includes a bed with a plush coverlet, a beautiful chest of drawers, and a nightstand with a marble washing bowl.
These are the Red Wizards' bedrooms.

entries.name: V5a: Abadesh's Bedroom
entries: Abadesh's chest of drawers contains various coins and gems worth 15,000 GP. An {@item Elixir of Health|XDMG} and a {@item Potion of Flying|XDMG} wrapped in oilcloth lie next to a stack of gem-encrusted red robes worth 1,000 GP.

entries.name: V5b: Zeil's Bedroom
entries: Zeil's chest of drawers contains various coins and gems worth 25,000 GP. Three {@item Potion of Healing|XDMG|Potions of Healing (supreme)} are tucked underneath a gem-encrusted red robe lavishly embroidered with gold thread, worth 1,500 GP.

entries.name: V5c: Iorru's Bedroom
entries: Stacks of rare tomes about necromancy and alternative magical healing techniques lie atop Iorru's chest of drawers. The books are worth 15,000 GP total.

entries.name: V5d: Dau's Bedroom
entries: Dau's chest of drawers contains rare perfumes, oils, and coins worth 40,000 GP total. A stack of gem-encrusted satin clothes is worth 8,000 GP. Wrapped in a satin tunic is a {@item Crystal Ball of Ominous Portent|AUD} (see appendix A). Tucked behind the clothes are two {@item Spell Scroll|XDMG|Spell Scrolls} of {@spell Sending|XPHB}.

entries.name: V5e: Yev's Bedroom
entries: Yev's bedroom is a mess. Open books, notes, bones with runes etched into them, a toppled wig stand, pouches of colorful dust, and vials of dark liquids lie scattered across the bed.

A character can take the {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine the items on the bed and make a {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) check. On a success, the character realizes the items constitute the method, incantation, and spell components needed for the mages' in-progress ritual to travel to Thaymount. (To learn how the characters can use these items, see "{@area The Mavericks Are Dead|269|x}" in chapter 6.)

In Yev's chest of drawers are various coins, gems, and jewelry worth 10,000 GP total. Stacks of gem-encrusted clothes are worth 20,000 GP total. The drawers also contain three {@item Spell Scroll|XDMG|Spell Scrolls} of {@spell Project Image|XPHB} and six {@item Spell Scroll|XDMG|Spell Scrolls} of {@spell Shatter|XPHB}.

entries.name: Concluding the Mission
entries: If the characters convince the Mavericks to magically transport them to Thaymount, their mission is successful. If the characters kill the Mavericks, their mission is unsuccessful, although they can still use the partially complete ritual (see "{@area The Mavericks Are Dead|269|x}" in chapter 6).

entries.name: Mission Reward
entries: If the characters' mission is successful, each character earns 7,800 XP.

entries.name: Development
entries: If this is the first mission the characters have completed this chapter, they receive one magic item from the list in "{@adventure Mission Rewards|AUD|3|Mission Rewards}" in chapter 3. Remind the characters to tell Wrynn which item they've chosen as their reward.

If this is the second mission the characters have completed, they receive no reply if they try to contact Wrynn via their {@item Sending Stones|XDMG|Sending Stone}. Any reward they request doesn't arrive. As the characters learn in "{@area Enemy Ambush|244|x}" later in this chapter, Szass Tam has discovered Operation Deadfall. Wrynn is dead or scrambling to escape Szass Tam's minions, as described in "{@area Wrynn's Bespoke Vestments|244|x}" in chapter 6.

entries.name: Magical Portal
entries: When the characters are ready to parley with the pirates, they can easily locate the magical portal to Ala Harbor that Zulkir Thrul described. The circular portal, built into a shallow cave, is denoted with glowing blue runes carved into the ground.

The portal was created as part of a trade agreement between Eltabbar's tharchion, Zedivek Mazradash, and the Alaor's tharchion, Bavak Inkander. The tharchions encourage merchant groups to use the portal to move goods and cargo between the islands and the nation's capital.

The journey to the magical portal is uneventful, and once there, the characters need only step onto the runes to activate the portal. The portal leads to Ala Harbor, the primary harbor on Alaor Major.

entries.name: Ala Harbor
entries: Once the characters step through the magical portal to Ala Harbor, read or paraphrase the following:

This bustling harbor holds a veritable forest of masts, sails, and rigging. Uniformed sailors and merchants in plain clothes bustle across the docks. In the distance, a sign atop a small building says "Gurthay's Boat Rentals."
This busy harbor is the Thayan navy's home. More about Ala Harbor appears in {@area chapter 1|048|x}.

entries.name: Renting a Boat
entries: If the characters decide to rent a boat to reach Blackrock Cove, Gurthay's Boat Rentals is their best option.

During the day, human proprietor Rensha Voll (Medium {@creature Noble Prodigy|XMM}) works with customers. A cheerful and dedicated entrepreneur, Voll tells them she has four Keelboats (see the {@table Large Vehicles; Airborne and Waterborne Vehicles|XPHB|Player's Handbook}) that are available to rent for up to five days.

Renting a {@vehicle Keelboat} costs 5 GP per day, or 6 GP per day if the characters also wish to hire a captain to sail the vessel. The characters must pay for the rental before leaving Ala Harbor, but Voll asks no questions about their destination or intentions. She describes the Keelboats and captains listed in the Boat Rentals table.

entries.caption: Boat Rentals
rows: Moira ({@creature Pirate Captain|XMM}), a gregarious orc
Harvey Dee (Neutral Evil {@creature Pirate|XMM}), a grumpy human
Manz ({@creature Pirate Captain|XMM}), a jocular tiefling

entries: Like Voll, the boat captains don't ask questions and comply with reasonable instructions. The captains all know the way to Blackrock Cove. When the characters ask to sail to the cove, their chosen captain tells them that area is famously uninhabited, though an angry ocean spirit is rumored to menace boats that sail nearby. The captain agrees to sail to the cove only if the characters pay them an additional 150 GP. If the characters ask about pirates in that area, the captain has no knowledge of specific crews, though they know pirates often sail in the area.
Once underway, the captain stays with their ship at all times and doesn't engage in combat.

entries.name: Blackrock Cove

entries.title: A dragon turtle guards Blackrock Cove.

entries: Located on the southeast side of Ala Minor, Blackrock Cove lies about thirty miles east of Ala Harbor. Owing to the island's rocky terrain and the rumors of hostile spirits near the cove, the region has no permanent settlements. However, centuries ago a Red Wizard created a sanctum there to hold his treasures, and a pirate crew has recently made the cove their secret lair.

entries.name: Zultan's Sanctum
entries: Zultan was a Red Wizard from Eltabbar who created a hidden sanctum in Blackrock Cove over three hundred years ago. He stored his treasures there, periodically visiting to add new acquisitions.

In Zultan's old age, he realized that with no heirs to inherit his wealth, it would likely be claimed by treasure hunters. He decided to create trials in his sanctum that would allow only clever hunters to earn his treasure. See "{@area Cove Locations|223|x}" for more on this sanctum.

entries.name: Blackrock Pirates
entries: For the past two years, a crew of pirates has laired in Blackrock Cove. The pirates follow Captain Sharlei, a human former officer in the Thayan navy. A brilliant naval strategist, Sharlei has never lost a sailor in battle or at sea.

Two years ago, several Red Wizards demanded her fealty, but the captain refused to swear allegiance. Enraged, the Red Wizards conspired to kill her, but the captain killed one of them first, then deserted her post. She stole her Thayan naval ship, the {@i Sharpened Blade}, and took her most loyal sailors with her.

While looking for a place to lie low, Captain Sharlei discovered the permanent illusion Zultan created to obscure Blackrock Cove's cave. The pirates hide here, occasionally sailing toward Alaor Major to demand tribute from Red Wizards' ships.

entries.name: Reaching the Cove
entries: Read or paraphrase the following when the characters approach the cove:

Near the cove's entrance, a sandbar is visible below the water's surface. Waves lap gently against the narrow beach lining the shore. Just past the beach, rocky cliffs topped with thick foliage spike toward the sky. A roaring waterfall rushes down the cliff at the middle of the cove.

entries.name: Cove Features
entries: The cove is a natural feature consisting of an inlet connected to a shallow pool inside a cave. Areas {@area B1–B3|224|x} are exterior, while areas {@area B4–B9|22c|x} are interior, including Zultan's sanctum (areas {@area B6–B9|235|x}).
The cove has the following features.

entries.name: Cave
entries: A permanent illusion hides the cove's large, natural cave ({@area area B4|22c|x}). Shallow water covers much of its floor, just enough to allow skilled crews to pilot boats and ships inside. The cave includes a small beach to the east before a sheer rock wall, inside which Zultan built the rooms of his sanctum.

entries.name: Ceilings
entries: The cave ceiling ({@area area B4|22c|x}) is 50 feet tall. Ceilings in Zultan's sanctum are 20 feet tall.

entries.name: Cliffs
entries: Cliffs with heavy foliage surround the cove and the opening to the cave ({@area area B4|22c|x}). Creatures standing on the cliffs have {@table Cover|XPHB|Total Cover} from creatures in the cove ({@area area B1|224|x}) and vice versa.

entries.name: Doors
entries: Doors in Zultan's sanctum are made of stone and are unlocked, except for the door to the grove ({@area area B9|23e|x}). See "Doors" in the {@book Dungeon Master's Guide|XDMG|2|Doors}.

entries.name: Illusory Waterfall
entries: A waterfall appears to tumble down the cliff at the cove's center. This is an illusion resulting from a permanent effect similar to that of a {@spell Mirage Arcane|XPHB} spell.

entries.name: Lighting
entries: Exterior areas are in {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} during the day. The cave ({@area area B4|22c|x}) and ship ({@area area B5|232|x}) are in {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} during the day. Otherwise, interior areas are in {@variantrule Darkness|XPHB}. Descriptions assume the characters have a way to see in the dark.

entries.name: Sanctum
entries: Unless otherwise noted, the walls, floors, and ceilings of Zultan's sanctum are made of magically treated stone that has {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to all damage.

entries.name: Cove Locations
entries: The following locations are keyed to map 5.2.

entries.name: B1: The Cove

entries: The rippling water distorts the view of the treacherous sandbar below.

If the characters travel in a boat or are otherwise 10 feet or fewer from the water's surface, a {@creature Dragon Turtle|XMM} accosts them, fighting them when they move over the sandbar, where the water is only 15 feet deep. The dragon turtle fights until {@status Bloodied|XPHB}, then retreats.

entries.name: Pirates
entries: The sounds of the fight attract the three pirate lookouts atop the western cliff ({@area area B2|228|x}). The pirates run down the natural stairs on a southern projection of this cliff; they arrive on the west beach at the end of the first round of combat. See area B2 for details about the pirates.

When the pirates see the dragon turtle attacking the characters' boat, they laugh and egg on the monster, referring to it as "Old Snappy." The dragon turtle is {@variantrule Friendly [Attitude]|XPHB|Friendly} toward the pirates, who feed it in exchange for its aggression against enemies.

As an {@action Influence|XPHB} action, a character can attempt to communicate to the pirates that they aren't enemies by making a {@dc 15} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) check. On a success, the lookouts shout, "Stand down!" and the dragon turtle swims back to the sandbar.

entries.name: Development
entries: If the pirates atop the western cliff ({@area area B2|228|x}) notice the characters moving onto the beach, they leave their camp to confront them. They seem impressed if the characters killed the dragon turtle, but unless the characters convince the pirates they're not enemies (see above), the pirates fight them. If the pirates believe the characters aren't enemies, they take them through the illusory waterfall ({@area area B3|22a|x}) to meet with Captain Sharlei.

entries.name: B2: Pirate Lookouts

entries: A small campsite, consisting of three bedrolls and a cooking fire, sits atop this cliff.

Three pirates are here on lookout duty. These are the humans River and Zander (Medium {@creature Noble Prodigy|XMM|Noble Prodigies}) and the dragonborn Flameshield (Medium {@creature Pirate Captain|XMM}).
If the pirates notice the characters, they fight them. Characters can convince the pirates to stand down and lead them to {@area area B4|22c|x} as detailed in area {@area B1|224|x}.

entries.name: B3: Waterfall

entries: A waterfall roars from the cliff above, spraying sea-foam against the rocky wall behind it.
If the lookouts in {@area area B2|228|x} lead the characters through the illusory waterfall, they swim through the channel that leads into the cave ({@area area B4|22c|x}).

entries.name: B4: Hidden Cave

entries: Three sailors in shabby clothing stand on a stretch of sand to the east. Near them, two metallic bipedal creatures stand at attention. To the north, a sailing ship sits docked.
If the pirate lookouts from {@area area B2|228|x} escort the characters here, each character earns 9,800 XP.
The three sailors are Captain Sharlei (Medium {@creature Pirate Admiral|XMM}) and two members of her crew: the human Landor (Medium {@creature Pirate|XMM}) and the gnome Bitterstem (Small Pirate).

The pirates stole the two nearby {@creature Iron Golem|XMM|Iron Golems} and rejiggered them to protect the cave. All creatures here fight any characters not escorted by the pirate lookouts from {@area area B2|228|x}.

entries.name: Meeting the Captain
entries: If the pirates escort the characters, read or paraphrase the following:

The tallest sailor, a human woman with a silver streak through her auburn hair, smirks and beckons you to approach. "Visitors? We don't get many visitors who don't want to kill us. Captain Sharlei, at your service—maybe. What do you want?"

entries.name: The Captain's Demand
entries: If the characters explain their mission and hand Captain Sharlei the list of ships carrying Szass Tam's ritual foci, the captain looks thoughtful and says:
"If what you say is true, you're asking us to do important work. If you lie, you're still asking us to attack Red Wizards' ships—which I'm always happy to do.

"I couldn't give a fig's leaf what's true, but I'm willing to help if you do something for us. The caves beyond this cove hold rooms built by an ancient Red Wizard named Zultan, who created this waterfall illusion. He supposedly hid a fortune in gold in those rooms, but my crew and I can't get past the blasted dragon statue that protects it.

"We want the gold Zultan hid here, but more importantly, we want the map to his second sanctum—apparently it's just outside Ala Harbor. Imagine the damage we could do to Red Wizards' ships if we could strike near the harbor and immediately disappear.
"Retrieve the gold and map for us, and we'll sink the ships on your list. We'll make sure those fiend skulls are destroyed, too."

Highly educated, Captain Sharlei knows basic details about Zultan. She can share the information from "{@area Zultan's Sanctum|217|x}" earlier in this chapter. She also can tell the characters about the deadly dragon statue trap in {@area area B7|237|x}, although she doesn't know how to circumvent it.

entries.name: B5: Sharpened Blade

entries: Painted in an elegant script, the words "Sharpened Blade" adorn the sides of this hardy sailing ship. Its mast boasts a plain black flag.
The pirates' ship has a single deck and a small cargo hold. A Cannon (see the {@book Dungeon Master's Guide|XDMG}) sits atop the deck, and a dozen Cannonballs are stacked beside it.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: Inside the hold are three chests that contain 10,000 GP total and a large crate that holds 30 days' worth of {@item Rations|XPHB} for six people.

entries.name: B6: Zultan's Entry Chamber

entries: A statue of a handsome, bearded human mage occupies this chamber. As you enter, the statue's mouth speaks.
"Welcome! I am the Red Wizard Zultan. Survive the trials ahead, and vast treasure is yours."
Zultan cast the {@spell Magic Mouth|XPHB} spell on the statue. It triggers when a creature enters the room.

The statue depicts Zultan. If the characters haven't learned about the mage, a character can take the {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine the statue and make a {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill History|XPHB}) check. On a success, they know the details from "{@area Zultan's Sanctum|217|x}" earlier in this chapter.

entries.name: B7: Trial of Wit

entries: Just past the entrance, a chasm opens in the floor. Lava bubbles in a pool sixty feet below. Above the lava float three black stones, each broad enough for a single human to stand on. Across the chasm, in front of a door, a scowling red dragon statue crouches on the floor of the far side of the room.
Zultan created this challenge to keep all but the cleverest spellcasters from venturing deeper into his sanctum.

entries.name: Dragon Statue Trap
entries: The dragon statue is magical and acts as a fire-casting statue trap from the {@book Dungeon Master's Guide|XDMG|2|Traps}, except the floating stones and the spaces due north and south of the statue are the trap's pressure plates (all marked with a T on the map), and the statue exhales a 60-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone} of magical flame and deals 55 ({@dice 10d10}) Fire damage from its fixed position.
If a character disarms the trap, the chasm remains.

entries.name: Lava
entries: Molten boulders magically shoot from the lava at the bottom of this chamber. The first time a creature flies over the lava, it must make a {@dc 15} Dexterity saving throw, taking 55 ({@dice 10d10}) Fire damage on a failed save or half as much on a successful one. Additionally, any creature that enters the lava for the first time on a turn or starts its turn in the lava takes 99 ({@dice 18d10}) Fire damage.

A character can take the {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine the lava and make a {@dc 18} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) check. On a success, the character knows the boulders will stop shooting from the lava if any character casts {@spell Otiluke's Resilient Sphere|XPHB} or {@spell Globe of Invulnerability|XPHB} in this area.

entries.name: B8: Trial of Magic

entries: Two glyphs glow on this chamber's floor. An oil portrait of a handsome, bearded mage in red robes adorns the eastern wall.
The man in the portrait speaks, saying, "Step on these glyphs and impress me with a spell—or perish where you stand. You have six seconds." The painting then falls silent.
A door to the south is covered in a beautiful fresco of a serene grove.
The portrait depicts Zultan. He cast the {@spell Magic Mouth|XPHB} spell on the portrait; it triggers when a creature enters the room.

entries.name: Magical Glyphs
entries: The magical glyphs, shown on the map, are part of a dangerous effect. Each glyph is large enough for one creature to stand on. The characters should roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} and proceed with their turns in order. By the end of the first round, a character must have stood on each of the two glyphs and cast any spell. If they do so, the portrait again appears to speak (via another casting of the {@spell Magic Mouth|XPHB} spell) and says, "You may now unlock my treasure room."

If the characters don't follow the mouth's instructions, poisonous gas fills the chamber. Each creature in the room must succeed on a {@dc 15} Constitution saving throw, taking 55 ({@dice 10d10}) Poison damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. The gas dissipates after 1 minute.

entries.name: B9: Zultan's Grove
entries: The door to this area is locked with the {@spell Arcane Lock|XPHB} spell. When the characters enter this area, read or paraphrase the following:

A moonbeam illuminates a magnificent pile of treasure in a serene twilight grove. A handsome, bearded man in red robes watches over the hoard. He smiles and says, "Congratulations—my treasures are yours."
When the characters enter Zultan's grove, each character earns 9,800 XP.

This is the heart of Zultan's sanctum. Here the mage stashed significant wealth and some of his prized possessions, including notes for reaching another magical sanctum he created (see "Treasure"). The image of the grove and mage are permanent illusions.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: Zultan's treasure includes a small, magically treated parchment with a drawing of Alaor Major; a location near the harbor is marked with an X. Instructions on the map explain how to use a command word to enter a sanctum at the marked location. This is the map Captain Sharlei seeks, but the details of this location are beyond the scope of this campaign.
The treasure includes the following; magic items with a dagger (†) after their names are in appendix A:

items: {@item Potion of Invisibility|XDMG|Potion of Greater Invisibility}

entries.name: Concluding the Mission
entries: If the characters return to Captain Sharlei and give her Zultan's gold and the map, she thanks them and agrees to target the ships on the zulkir's list. The pirate captain dislikes magic items and lets the characters keep anything else they want from Zultan's treasure.

If the characters refuse to give Captain Sharlei the map or gold, she flies into a rage. She and the other creatures in the cave ({@area area B4|22c|x}) fight the characters. The pirate lookouts ({@area area B2|228|x}) hear the commotion and join the fight at the end of the third round of combat.
If the pirates agree to target the ships on the zulkir's list, the characters' mission is successful.

entries.name: Mission Reward
entries: If the characters' mission is successful, each character earns 9,800 XP.

entries.name: Development
entries: If this is the first mission the characters have completed this chapter, they receive one magic item from the list in "Mission Rewards" in {@adventure chapter 3|AUD|3|Mission Rewards}. Remind the characters to tell Wrynn which item they've chosen as their reward.

If this is the second mission the characters have completed, they receive no reply if they try to contact Wrynn via their {@item Sending Stones|XDMG|Sending Stone}. Any reward they request doesn't arrive. As the characters learn in "Enemy Ambush" below, Szass Tam has discovered Operation Deadfall. Wrynn is dead or scrambling to escape Szass Tam's minions, as described in "{@area Wrynn's Bespoke Vestments|252|x}" in chapter 6.

entries.name: Enemy Ambush
entries: After the characters finish their sixth mission, enemies accost them outside Eltabbar. Read or paraphrase the following:
A shimmering image of a desiccated man in resplendent red robes hovers in the air. Nearby are a crimson-clad human mage and three black-clad knights, whose green eyes glow through heavy helms.
The lich grins evilly; you recognize Szass Tam.

"Puny maggots," he says. "You think much of yourselves, don't you? I am amused you dare stand against me. I shall remember your conviction fondly while my lieutenants murder everyone you hold dear, starting with your little zulkir and her spy master. Operation Deadfall, indeed."
The rotting mage disappears.
Use {@adventure map 4.1|AUD|4|Map 4.1: Eastern Pyarados Trail} for this encounter.

The characters recognize the image of Szass Tam was an illusion. The mage (Medium, Neutral Evil {@creature Archmage|XMM}) is allied with Szass Tam; the knights are a {@creature Death Knight|XMM} and two {@creature Death Knight Aspirant|XMM|Death Knight Aspirants}. If the characters are flying, the mage and death knights use the {@spell Fly|XPHB} spell. The archmage and death knights fight to the death.

entries.name: Development
entries: Szass Tam's taunts reveal that he has discovered Operation Deadfall. From this moment on, the lich begins his final casting of his Malefice Mortum ritual. If the characters are within sight of Thaymount, they see a dark cloud over the plateau. Every few seconds, bolts of green lightning pierce the ominous cloud.

data.name: Chapter 6: Precipice of Oblivion
entries: {@i Battle Szass Tam's forces in Thaymount}.

entries.title: Demons are rampaging throughout Thaymount, and the Red Wizards can't stop them.

entries.name: Key Plot Points
entries: The following information is key to this chapter's story:

items.name: The Truth Emerges
items.entry: Having discovered Operation Deadfall, Szass Tam moves swiftly to crush it. The characters must dispatch the lich's allies before heading to Thaymount to seek him out.

items.name: Central Thaymount
items.entry: The characters arrive in Thaymount to find that monstrous foes and Szass Tam's forces are rampaging across the plateau. To reach the tunnel from Castle Thrul to the Citadel, where Szass Tam weaves his ritual, the characters must learn how to get past the barrier around the castle from magic researcher Saraphine Dau in the nearby Fortress of Opposition.

entries.name: Preparation
entries: Before running this chapter, prepare as follows:

items.name: Step 1
items.entry: Read the "{@area Running This Chapter|24c|x}" section, including "{@area Character Advancement|24d|x}."

items.name: Step 2
items.entry: Familiarize yourself with the Key NPCs table.

items.name: Step 3
items.entry: Bookmark the stat blocks below, which appear in the {@book Monster Manual|XMM}and on D&D Beyond unless otherwise noted. If a stat block appears in appendix B, an asterisk appears after its name:

entries.caption: Key NPCs
rows: Dragonborn Dread Legion officer attacking the Fortress of Opposition
Human Red Wizard coleader of forces assaulting Castle Thrul
Sabinia Dau's sister; trapped human inhabitant of the Fortress of Opposition
Human tailor and Zulkir Thrul's spy master
Human zulkir of evocation and Operation Deadfall's missing leader
Coleader of forces assaulting Castle Thrul

entries.name: Running This Chapter
entries: This chapter takes place after the characters have completed their missions with the dissident Red Wizards and the pirates of Blackrock Cove.

entries.name: Character Advancement
entries: The characters should be level 17 when this chapter begins. They should have enough XP to advance to level 18 before they head to Castle Thrul. They should reach level 19 by the end of this chapter. If you're using a method of level advancement that doesn't rely on XP, the characters gain levels at those points.

entries.name: Operation Deadfall's Discovery
entries: While the characters pursued their recent missions, Szass Tam discovered Operation Deadfall. The lich knows that Zulkir Thrul runs the operation, Wynston Wrynn is her spy master, and the characters are her operatives.

The lich has dispatched two underlings to crush Operation Deadfall: the vampire siblings Viln Crocus and Nara Crocus, whose lairs are both in the Citadel. He ordered Viln to kill Wrynn and the characters at Wrynn's Bespoke Vestments, and he instructed Nara to ambush Thrul elsewhere, incapacitate her, and bring her to his ritual chamber (see {@adventure chapter 7|AUD|7}).

entries.name: Return to Eltabbar
entries: When the characters return to Eltabbar, they see more signs of Szass Tam's terrible ritual magic at work.

entries.name: Rising Evil Magic
entries: The ritual's magic has weakened the veil between the Material Plane and the Abyss. When the ritual is complete, demons will pour into Eltabbar. For now, an ominous haze hangs over the city, broken only by flashes of green lightning. Outdoor areas are in {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} in the daytime.

entries.name: Terror in the Streets
entries: Szass Tam's foul magic is splitting the souls of demons between the Material Plane and the {@book Abyss|XDMG|5|Abyss}, allowing demons to faintly see scenes of Eltabbar's cityscapes and the city's residents to faintly see those demons. The demons can't hurt anyone on the Material Plane, but seeing them still terrifies locals who don't realize the demons aren't real.

As the characters move through Eltabbar, roll on or pick a scene from the Eltabbar Demonic Scenes table. Describe the scene and bystanders' panicked reactions to it before allowing characters to examine it.

A character can take the {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine a scene and make a {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) check. On a success, the character recognizes the demons aren't real and can't hurt anyone. The character realizes the scenes are a result of Szass Tam's foul magic.

entries.caption: Eltabbar's Demonic Scenes
rows: A goristro slavers and roars while a hezrou chases panicking bystanders.
Two glabrezus chase passersby in a crowded square as an abveku (see {@area appendix B|36d|x}) pounces on bystanders.
A balor leaps from the top of a building onto a screaming crowd.
A marilith and two hezrous run across an empty bridge toward a crowd.

entries.name: Wrynn's Bespoke Vestments

entries.title: In Eltabbar, illusory scenes—such as this death knight commanding demons to attack—are harbingers of the horrors to come.

entries: The next time the characters approach Wrynn's Bespoke Vestments, read or paraphrase the following:
The once-gleaming windows of Wrynn's Bespoke Vestments are shattered. Inside, you can see the shop has been ransacked; clothing and mannequins are strewn about haphazardly.
Szass Tam's agents are raiding the shop, looking for information about Operation Deadfall.

entries.name: Wynston Wrynn's Fate
entries: Wrynn's fate depends on whether the characters allied with the militia in chapter 4.

entries.name: Mission Succeeded
entries: If the characters allied with the militia, Fallon Nor and other militia members recently learned that Szass Tam had discovered Operation Deadfall. Nor used her {@item Sending Stones|XDMG|Sending Stone} to warn Wrynn, who escaped the shop moments before Viln Crocus arrived. Wrynn arrives at the shop after the characters have dispatched Crocus (see "{@area Development|2a7|x}" below).

entries.name: Mission Failed
entries: If the characters didn't ally with the militia, Szass Tam's agents have killed Wrynn. The characters find the tailor's body near his desk in the shop's display and fitting space ({@area area W1|0d1|x} on map 3.2).

Wrynn has sustained terrible injuries to his throat. As a {@action Search|XPHB} action, a character can examine his wounds and make a {@dc 12} Wisdom ({@skill Medicine|XPHB}) check; on a success, they determine that a fanged creature killed the tailor.

The vampire Viln Crocus killed Wrynn. If the characters don't kill Crocus (see "Assault on the Shop" below) or raise Wrynn from the dead, the tailor rises the following sunset as a {@creature Vampire Spawn|XMM} under Crocus's control.
Wrynn knows who killed him and that Szass Tam deduced Operation Deadfall's secrets, but he doesn't know Zulkir Thrul's fate.

entries.name: Assault on the Shop
entries: When the characters enter the tailor shop (shown on {@adventure map 3.2|AUD|3|Map 3.2: Wrynn's Bespoke Vestments} in chapter 3), they hear frustrated shouting coming from the secret office ({@area area W3|0d1|x}).
As they enter the office, read or paraphrase the following:

The desk is upturned, and papers lie strewn across the floor. As three humans in dark robes emblazoned with a fist ransack the office, a bald, gaunt man with fangs and pupilless, black eyes rasps, "What else are they planning? There must be evidence somewhere!"

The fanged man is Viln Crocus (Medium {@creature Vampire Umbral Lord|XMM}), and the robed humans (Medium, Neutral Evil {@creature Archpriest|XMM|Archpriests}) are priests of Bane, god of tyranny. All four Szass Tam loyalists fight the characters on sight.

entries.name: Development
entries: If he escaped earlier, Wrynn returns to the shop after the characters have dispatched Szass Tam's agents. The tailor has been watching the shop from a distance in disguise.
Wrynn is terrified for Zulkir Thrul, whose fate he doesn't know. He tries to use his {@item Sending Stones|XDMG|Sending Stone} to contact her, to no avail.

entries.name: Wrynn's Stones
entries: The tailor carries a smooth, palm-size stone. Each side is engraved with an image of a crane identical to that of the {@item Masquerader's Brooch|AUD|Masquerader's Brooches} Thrul gave the characters in chapter 3—a reference to the zulkir's code name, the Crane.

The stone is imbued with a {@spell Programmed Illusion|XPHB} spell (detailed in "{@area Grim Message|25b|x}"). The zulkir instructed Wrynn to activate it with a command word in the event of her death or disappearance.

If Wrynn is alive, he activates the stone for the characters. If he's dead, the characters can find the stone on his body. A note in Wrynn's pocket (cloaked with an {@spell Illusory Script|XPHB} spell) says: "The stone is magical and contains a message from the Crane. Its command phrase is 'the Crane speaks.'"
If Wrynn is dead, the characters also find the {@item Sending Stones|XDMG} connected to Thrul and Fallon Nor on his body.

entries.name: Grim Message
entries: When the characters say the stone's command phrase, its illusion activates and the characters see an image of Zulkir Thrul.
Read or paraphrase the following:
Magical energy shimmers, and a translucent image appears: Zulkir Thrul sits behind her desk, looking stern.
"If you're seeing this, operatives, it means I'm incapacitated or dead," she says. "But you aren't, and therefore Thay has hope. Know that I am proud of you—but your work is not yet done.

"The Hydra is ensconced in his stronghold in Thaymount—the Citadel—where he is nearly unassailable. Layered wards protect the area from teleportation and scrying, and by now every inch of it crawls with malefites and fiends. We have mere days before he finishes his ritual, raises his hordes, and declares himself regent again.

"Use the Mavericks' ritual to travel to central Thaymount. From there, find the underground tunnel that leads from Castle Thrul—my ancestral home—into the Citadel. You must reach the Citadel without delay.

"The Hydra knows about this underground passage, and his allies may have magically barricaded Castle Thrul to prevent entry. In this case, seek the advice of Sabinia Dau in the Veiled Tower. If she's unsure, you'll need the help of her sister, Saraphine, the most brilliant magical theorist I've known. She's most likely in Thaymount.
"I've left magic items in my demiplane that might aid you. Consider them payment."
The zulkir exhales, then smiles grimly, head held high. "You can save Thay from the Hydra, operatives. I believe in you."

entries.name: Szass Tam's Barrier
entries: As Zulkir Thrul suspects, Szass Tam has erected a powerful barrier around Castle Thrul as described in "{@area Abyssal Barriers|273|x}" later in this chapter.

entries.name: Zulkir Thrul's Fate
entries: Zulkir Thrul is alive—barely—because Szass Tam wants her to witness his ritual's completion before he turns her into an undead servant. Thaymount's wards against scrying (see "{@area Magic on Thaymount|270|x}" later in this chapter) prevent the characters from locating or magically observing Thrul, but they'll have a chance to reunite with her in chapter 7.

entries.name: Zulkir Thrul's Demiplane
entries: If the characters can cast {@spell Demiplane|XPHB}, they can enter Zulkir Thrul's demiplane. If they do so, they find it exactly as described in chapter 3, except the following are neatly laid on the zulkir's desk:

items: {@item Plate Armor of Etherealness|XDMG|Plate Armor of Etherealness (Plate Armor)}
{@item Potion of Greater Healing|XDMG|Five Potions of Healing (greater)}

entries.title: The zulkir's payment includes {@item Potion of Greater Healing|XDMG|five Potions of Healing (greater)}.

entries.name: Reaching Thaymount
entries: The characters might debate traveling to Thaymount via teleportation to Szul—the only place in the region not warded against teleportation. Make it clear that doing so would be a death sentence, as Szass Tam has stationed an overwhelming force here that the characters can't overcome. They must rely on the Mavericks' ritual to teleport to a location in central Thaymount.
The characters' options for getting there depend on the outcome of their mission to recruit the Mavericks in chapter 5.

entries.name: The Mavericks Assist
entries: If the characters allied with the dissident Red Wizards, they can return to the Veiled Tower to obtain the mages' assistance with reaching Thaymount.
When the characters enter the tower, read or paraphrase the following:
In the tower's lounge, scattered notes, open books, and strange spell components cover the table. Before you stand the five dissident Red Wizards, looking weary. Darvyn Yev greets you.
"As promised, we have finished the ritual to teleport to central Thaymount. Given the situation, though, we have some concerns that you can help with."

entries.name: Speaking with Yev
entries: Yev reveals the following in conversation:

items.name: The Mavericks' Fears
items.entry: Yev explains condescendingly that the mages fear that Szass Tam's evil magic and marauding allies have made central Thaymount unsafe.

items.name: A Coward's Proposal
items.entry: Yev suggests that the Red Wizards teleport the characters to the Mouth of Despair (as described in {@area chapter 5|202|x}), while the Red Wizards stay in the Veiled Tower until the party tells them the Fortress of Opposition is safe.

entries.name: Speaking with Sabinia Dau
entries: If the characters ask Sabinia Dau about circumventing the barrier around Castle Thrul, she ponders their question carefully. Read or paraphrase the following:
"If Szass Tam is trying to prevent you from entering Castle Thrul, you won't be able to circumvent his barrier with everyday magic," Dau says.

"I doubt I could help even if I knew the details. However, my sister Saraphine is a genius when it comes to magical barriers. She'll know how to thwart it—and she's likely to have the magic on hand. Saraphine's in Thaymount, in our family's home, the Fortress of Opposition."

entries.name: Dau's Request
entries: Regardless whether the characters ask about traveling to Castle Thrul, before the mages begin the ritual, Dau asks them to investigate the Fortress of Opposition and confirm Saraphine's safety.

If the characters agree, Dau gives them the perfumes, rare oils, and coins (worth 40,000 GP in total) and the {@item Crystal Ball of Ominous Portent|AUD} (see appendix A) that she keeps in her bedroom (area {@area V5d|208|x} on {@adventure map 5.1|AUD|5|Map 5.1: Veiled Tower} in chapter 5).

Saraphine, a human, was residing at the fortress with five others when Szass Tam began his final ritual steps and Thaymount was thrown into chaos (see "{@area Thaymount in Chaos|271|x}" later in this chapter). More information about the fortress's inhabitants appears in "{@area Trapped Inhabitants|278|x}" later in this chapter.

entries.name: Performing the Teleportation Ritual
entries: When the characters are ready, the Red Wizards perform their ritual, which takes 10 minutes. Afterward, the characters arrive in the Mouth of Despair (see "{@area Central Thaymount|26b|x}").

entries.name: The Mavericks Don't Assist
entries: If the characters failed to impress the dissident Red Wizards—or killed them—they can still use the mages' ritual to reach Thaymount.

entries.name: The Mavericks Are Dead
entries: If the dissidents died, the characters can use the ritual notes and components in Darvyn Yev's bedroom (area {@adventure V5e|AUD|5|V5e: Yev's Bedroom} on {@adventure map 5.1|AUD|5} in chapter 5) to teleport to central Thaymount. However, the unfinished ritual proves difficult to perform.

The characters each must take an action to follow the notes and make a {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) check. On a success, a character teleports to central Thaymount and takes 22 ({@dice 5d8}) Force damage. On a failure, a character teleports there and takes 45 ({@dice 10d8}) Force damage.

entries.name: The Mavericks Are Unimpressed
entries: If the characters failed to impress the dissidents in chapter 5, they can return to the Veiled Tower and ask for the mages' help again.

A character must take the {@action Influence|XPHB} action to explain what has happened since their last meeting with the mages, then make a {@dc 15} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) check. On a success, the mages explain that they've finished the ritual to teleport to Thaymount and agree to help the characters. Proceed with "{@area Speaking with Yev|263|x}" above.

On a failure, the mages are enraged at the characters' incompetence and fight them. When one mage is {@status Bloodied|XPHB}, however, the Mavericks reassess the characters' abilities, stop fighting, and tell the characters they've finished their ritual to travel to Thaymount. Proceed with "{@area Speaking with Yev|263|x}" above.

entries.name: Central Thaymount
entries: When the characters teleport to central Thaymount, an area many miles across, they arrive in the Mouth of Despair, as shown on map 6.1. See "{@area Thaymount|05c|x}" in chapter 1 for details on the tharch.

entries.name: Mouth of Despair
entries: A natural fissure in the plateau, the Mouth of Despair divides the Fortress of Opposition, Castle Thrul, and the Citadel from the more populated areas to the west.

The dissident Red Wizards targeted this area to avoid Szass Tam knowing about their arrival in Thaymount. Now that the characters are involved, these mages are happy to let the characters face Thaymount's dangers and report back.
The Red Wizards' ritual deposits the characters in the middle of the Mouth of Despair, at the bottom of the fissure near its eastern wall. When they arrive, read or paraphrase the following:
You find yourselves at the bottom of a forty-foot-deep chasm. Above, green lightning flashes amid a gray, oppressive haze pierced only by Thaymount's volcanic peaks far overhead.
{@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} filters into the chasm during daytime.
Before the characters leave the Mouth of Despair, they see an illusion of Saraphine Dau, as described below.

entries.name: Saraphine's Plea
entries: If the characters reached the Mouth of Despair with the help of the dissident Red Wizards, Sabinia Dau told her sister via a {@item Spell Scroll|XDMG} {@i of} {@spell Sending|XPHB} where and when to expect the characters to arrive in Central Thaymount. Shortly afterward, demons began attacking the Fortress of Opposition. Saraphine hid in the fortress and, desperate for help, used a {@item Spell Scroll|XDMG} {@i of} {@spell Project Image|XPHB} to create an illusory copy of herself, which she sent into the Mouth of Despair to meet the characters.

If the dissident Red Wizards are dead, Saraphine sent her illusory copy here knowing that the mages were working on a way to reach the Mouth of Despair. It's a long shot, but she hopes her sister will arrive in the fissure and help her escape the fortress.
Read or paraphrase the following, changing Saraphine's recognition to surprise if she isn't expecting the characters to arrive:
Sitting on a nearby rock outcropping is the shimmering image of a young human woman, her navy blue cloak drawn around her. When she notices you, relief and excitement cross her face.

"You must be Sabinia's friends!" she says. "I'm Saraphine Dau, Sabinia's sister. You've got to help me! I'm stuck in the Fortress of Opposition. Fiends are destroying the place, and I fear they'll soon rip me to pieces. Others are hiding in the fortress too. Please help us!"

The characters recognize the image as an illusion. Saraphine Dau's image offers the characters the scrolls and magic items she keeps in the fortress (see {@area area F14|2a5|x}) in exchange for saving her and the others trapped in the fortress. She can tell the characters everything in the "{@area Trapped Inhabitants|278|x}" section.
If the characters ask Saraphine about the barrier around Castle Thrul, she won't discuss the matter until the characters agree to help her.

entries.name: Magic on Thaymount
entries: Ancient magical wards erected by paranoid Red Wizards block scrying and teleportation in most of Thaymount. The exception is Szul, one of Szass Tam's strongholds (see {@area chapter 1|05c|x}).
Spells and effects that would teleport creatures to other areas of Thaymount don't work. In addition, the following spells don't function in Thaymount:
If a creature tries to cast one of these spells, the spell slot is expended, but the spell has no effect.
Creatures with Legendary Actions that are in their lairs (such as {@creature Szass Tam|AUD} in chapter 7) ignore these impediments and can teleport or cast spells normally.

entries.name: Thaymount in Chaos
entries: With Szass Tam's ritual animating malefites and allowing demons to slip onto the Material Plane, Thaymount is in chaos. Central Thaymount is sparsely inhabited, though Castle Thrul and the Fortress of Opposition are both under attack, and magical barriers surround Castle Thrul and the Citadel (see "{@area Abyssal Barriers|273|x}"). Central Thaymount's layout is shown on {@adventure map 6.1|AUD|6|Map 6.1: Central Thaymount}.

Malefites and demons have overrun this area. Every mile the adventurers spend traveling, roll once on the Thaymount Encounters table below. As shown on map 6.1, the Mouth of Despair is about seven miles from the Fortress of Opposition, which is about eight miles from Castle Thrul.
Use {@adventure map 4.1|AUD|4|Map 4.1: Eastern Pyarados Trail} in chapter 4 for each encounter, but clarify to the players that its location is Thaymount.

entries.caption: Thaymount Encounters
rows: A {@creature Death Knight|XMM} directs four {@creature Hezrou|XMM|Hezrous} to dig in the rocky soil of an ancient graveyard. The demons search for dead spellcasters who will animate once Szass Tam completes his ritual.
A {@creature Balor|XMM} guarded by three {@creature Death Cultist|XMM|Death Cultists} tries to open a portal to the Abyss. Nearby are the corpses of a dozen Red Wizards who tried to stop them.
A {@creature Marilith|XMM} and three {@creature Death Knight Aspirant|XMM|Death Knight Aspirants} hunt for vulnerable people to slaughter.
Two {@creature Goristro|XMM|Goristros} make their way west to attack mages' fortresses nearby.

entries.name: Rising Evil Magic
entries: As in Eltabbar, Szass Tam's demonic magic has created an ominous haze over Thaymount. Outdoor areas are in {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} in the daytime, and green lightning flashes in the sky.

entries.name: Abyssal Barriers
entries: When Szass Tam discovered Operation Deadfall, he used Abyssal magic to erect powerful barriers around Castle Thrul and the Citadel. The barriers are shown on {@adventure map 6.1|AUD|6|Map 6.1: Central Thaymount} and look like thick, green, translucent domes.

entries.name: Castle Thrul
entries: A barrier surrounds {@area Castle Thrul|2b0|x} outside the crumbling stone walls that surround the complex. The barrier functions like a {@spell Wall of Force|XPHB} spell, but it's permanent and can't be destroyed with a {@spell Disintegrate|XPHB} spell. The barrier prevents entry into the areas described in "Castle Thrul" later in this chapter. The characters can punch a hole in this barrier using Saraphine Dau's instructions (see {@area area F14|2a5|x} in "{@area Fortress of Opposition|276|x}").

entries.name: The Citadel
entries: Another domed barrier surrounds the Citadel. It functions like the barrier surrounding Castle Thrul, but it can't be penetrated. However, the barrier doesn't extend far enough underground to impede the characters from reaching Szass Tam's ritual chamber via the tunnels under Castle Thrul.

The ritual's foul magic bathes the Citadel in green, malevolent energy that sweeps east, as shown on {@adventure map 6.1|AUD|6|Map 6.1: Central Thaymount}. This energy is harmless to the living, but if Szass Tam's ritual isn't stopped, the energy will envelop Thaymount, causing malefites to rise en masse.

entries.name: Fortress of Opposition
entries: The Fortress of Opposition comprises two structures that form one facility. The eastern portion stands atop a sixty-foot cliff, while the western portion sits at the cliff's base. A staircase connects the two sections.

The Dau family of Red Wizards has owned the fortress for centuries. While most family members prefer primary residences in more cosmopolitan parts of Thay, Saraphine Dau relishes the fortress's isolation. It's her primary residence. (For more about Saraphine, see "{@area Trapped Inhabitants|278|x}" below.)
Read or paraphrase the following when the characters approach the Fortress of Opposition:

A sturdy fortress rises before you in two sections: a broad structure with a central tower and numerous small towers around its perimeter, and a wide tower atop a sixty-foot cliff to the east connected to the structure below. Green lightning strikes the upper portion, while hulking demonic forms lumber near the lower towers.

entries.name: Trapped Inhabitants
entries: Saraphine Dau, her friend, and two Dau family staff are trapped inside the fortress. They were staying in the fortress when Szass Tam began escalating his ritual. When rampaging demons attacked the fortress, the staff and Saraphine's friend locked themselves in their bedrooms, while Saraphine, who was in the lab upstairs, locked herself inside and ordered the fortress's two guards to ward the lab's entrance.

The three hiding downstairs know each others' locations; they also know Saraphine was in the lab and the two guards were in the fortress's lounge, but they don't know that the guards have been killed or whether Saraphine is alive. Similarly, Saraphine is unaware of the fate of those downstairs.
The names and locations of these individuals are in the Trapped Inhabitants table below.

entries.name: Rescuing the Inhabitants
entries: If the characters defeat the monsters in the fortress courtyard ({@area area F1|281|x}), great hall ({@area area F2|283|x}), and library ({@area area F8|292|x}), and tell those trapped in the bedchambers (areas {@area F3–F5|285|x}) that they did so, those three inhabitants become {@variantrule Friendly [Attitude]|XPHB|Friendly} toward the party and unlock their doors. If the characters haven't rescued Saraphine in the lab ({@area area F14|2a5|x}), those downstairs beg the characters to rescue her before they'll talk further. Otherwise, they thank the characters profusely and offer to help the characters in any way they can, including giving them any treasure they have. See area F14 for Saraphine's response to rescue.
If the characters don't defeat all the creatures in the fortress, the besieging forces break through the locked doors—or smash holes in the walls—in one hour and kill Saraphine and the others.

entries.name: Assaulting Force
entries: When Sabinia Dau published her anti-Szass Tam pamphlet, "Death to Tyrants," the dragonborn Goreth Blacktooth took note. A low-ranking officer in Szass Tam's Dread Legion (see {@area chapter 1|02e|x}), Blacktooth recently mustered two undead knights and set off for the Fortress of Opposition, hoping to earn a position closer to Szass Tam's side by killing Sabinia Dau, who he assumes is in the fortress.
Blacktooth has marshaled demons and undead he encountered en route to attack the fortress. They are only loosely under his command and are mostly interested in causing destruction and suffering.

entries.name: Fortress Features
entries: The fortress is made of magically treated stone that has {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to all damage. The structure also has the following features.

entries.name: Ceilings
entries: Ceilings in the fortress are 50 feet high, except for the ceiling over the staircase leading from {@area area F2|283|x}

entries.name: Doors
entries: The fortress's doors are made of magically treated metal that has {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to all damage. The doors to most bedrooms (areas {@area F3–F6|285|x}) are locked; their locks are Complex (1 minute to pick) and of Superior quality ({@dc 20}). (See "Doors" in the {@book Dungeon Master's Guide|XDMG|2|Doors}.)

entries.name: Lighting
entries: Sconces with {@spell Continual Flame|XPHB} spells cast on them shed {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} in all interior areas. Outside, the evil magic haze swirling in the region allows only {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} to shine through during the day.

entries.name: Thaymount's Wards
entries: Like everywhere on the plateau, the fortress is affected by Thaymount's ancient magical wards (see "{@area Magic on Thaymount|270|x}" earlier in this chapter).

entries.name: Fortress Locations
entries: The following locations are keyed to map 6.2.

entries.name: F1: Fortress Courtyard

entries: The fortress's enormous metal doors lie shattered on the ground. A massive fiend resembling a nightmarish centaur slams a warhammer against the northwest wall, while two horned, toad-faced monsters drool and laugh evilly. Meanwhile, skeletons and zombies claw ineffectually at the fortress's outer wall.

A {@creature Rendelith|AUD} (see appendix B) works to smash its way into a bedchamber inside the fortress ({@area area F3|285|x}) while two {@creature Hezrou|XMM|Hezrous} rumble encouragement. The demons fight the characters as soon as they notice them.
Five groups of undead (each made up of five {@creature Skeleton|XMM|Skeletons} and five {@creature Zombie|XMM|Zombies}) scrabble at different sections of the outer wall, to no effect.

entries.name: F2: Great Hall

entries: Ripped carpets and smashed furniture litter this once-luxurious hall with soaring ceilings. A staircase in the northeast corner spirals upward.

Two fiendish horrors lumber purposefully toward the northwest: massive, horned creatures with black, bony spikes protruding from their crimson-furred backs. Elsewhere in the hall, skeletons and zombies shamble aimlessly.

The Fiends are two {@creature Goristro|XMM|Goristros}, which are searching for the inhabitants who have locked themselves in nearby bedchambers (areas {@area F3–F5|285|x}). The goristros fight the characters as soon as they notice them.

Lying in wait to the north of the library ({@area area F8|292|x}), out of sight of the entrance, is an {@creature Abveku|AUD} (see appendix B). It joins the fight when the goristros begin combat. Four groups of undead, each made up of five {@creature Skeleton|XMM|Skeletons} and five {@creature Zombie|XMM|Zombies}, scrabble at the doors that lead to bedchambers.

entries.name: F3: South Bedchamber
entries: The door to this room is locked as detailed in "Fortress Features."
A bed, nightstand, and wardrobe furnish this comfortable bedroom, and its textiles boast subtle patterns. A human man wearing a green-and-gold robe huddles on the bed.

Hiding here is Aventril (Medium {@creature Noble|XMM}), a personal assistant to Saraphine. A no-nonsense but friendly human man, Aventril manages Saraphine's calendar and stays here while Saraphine is in residence.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: Aventril has few valuable personal possessions, but he does keep a {@item Potion of Gaseous Form|XDMG} and a {@item Potion of Comprehension|XDMG} in his nightstand.

entries.name: F4: Southwest Bedchamber
entries: The door to this room is locked as detailed in "{@area Fortress Features|2ba|x}."
This comfortable bedroom is decorated in geometric patterns. A bed, wardrobe, and nightstand furnish the room. A human woman with waist-length black hair paces the floor.

Hiding here is Molly Malu (Medium {@creature Noble|XMM}), a personal assistant to Saraphine. The bubbly and passionate human woman provides Saraphine with social advice and organizes the parties Saraphine throws in Eltabbar.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: Malu enjoys fashion. Fifteen sets of {@item Fine Clothes|XPHB} hang in her wardrobe.

entries.name: F5: North Bedchamber
entries: The door to this room is locked as detailed in "{@area Fortress Features|27b|x}."

This bedroom is decorated with velvet curtains and bedclothes, a silk rug, and stylized wood carvings. It's furnished with a bed, a nightstand, and a wardrobe. A young, pale gnome woman sits on the bed scribbling notes in a journal.

Jerica Rey (Small {@creature Mage Apprentice|XMM}), Saraphine's close friend and fellow aspiring Red Wizard, hides here. The young gnome hasn't yet earned an apprenticeship with a Red Wizard, though it's her ardent wish. Rey is chronicling her ordeal in her journal when the characters arrive.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: Rey wears a {@item Cloak of Displacement|XDMG} but gripes about not having other magic items. She tells the characters about the repository of {@item Spell Scroll|XDMG|Spell Scrolls} and magic items in the magical lab ({@area area F14|2a5|x}).

entries.name: F6: Northeast Bedchamber
entries: The door to this room is locked as detailed in "{@area Fortress Features|2ba|x}."
In this comfortable bedroom, Red Wizard symbols adorn the duvet and rug. Sitting on the nightstand are a stoppered flask and a clay jug.
Sabinia Dau stays here when she visits.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: On the nightstand are an {@item Alchemy Jug|XDMG} and a {@item Decanter of Endless Water|XDMG}.

entries.name: F7: Southeast Bedchamber

entries: This bedroom lies in shambles. The door hangs open on its hinges. Someone has snapped the wooden bed frame, torn the rugs, and splintered the wardrobe and nightstand.
Normally the guards' bedroom, this chamber was destroyed by the {@creature Goristro|XMM|goristros} in the great hall ({@area area F2|283|x}).

entries.name: F8: Library

entries: Two enormous, board-headed beasts knock over bookshelves in this spacious library while a six-armed, serpentine fiend flings tables and scatters books around the room.
Two {@creature Nalfeshnee|XMM|Nalfeshnees} and a {@creature Marilith|XMM} wreak havoc here. They fight the characters as soon as they notice them.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: If the characters spend 10 minutes searching the toppled shelves, they find a {@item Spell Scroll|XDMG} of {@spell Circle of Power|XPHB} and a {@item Spell Scroll|XDMG} of {@spell Contact Other Plane|XPHB} among the wreckage.

entries.name: F9: Azuth Shrine

entries: A fifteen-foot-tall pyramid made of gold sits in this room's west alcove. Around it flit colored lights. A symbol emblazoned near the pyramid's apex depicts a hand holding up its index finger.
This room is a shrine to Azuth, god of spellcasting, whom the Dau family worships. Any character who has proficiency in {@skill Religion|XPHB} or worships Azuth recognizes the symbol.

entries.name: Praying at the Shrine
entries: Azuth, the Lord of Spells, is aware of the events unfolding and wants the characters to stop Szass Tam. If a creature takes an action to pray at the shrine, Azuth restores that creature's expended spell slots. A creature can benefit from the shrine only once every 24 hours.

entries.name: F10: Abyssal Vestibule

entries: A double door stands in the east wall here, and a spiral staircase leads down in its north end. A mirror and furniture lie smashed on the floor.
Scorched red banners bearing a pronged symbol hang in ripped ribbons from the hundred-foot ceiling. The portraits of red-robed mages that adorn the curved walls bear smears of filth and claw marks.

The mages in the paintings suddenly grow horns, and their eyes glow green. They try to scrabble out of the walls, hissing like demonic beasts, and an overwhelming sense of murderous chaos washes over you.

A {@creature Marilith|XMM} desecrated this place with Abyssal filth it brought when it slipped onto the Material Plane. Blacktooth and his death knights then urged it to proceed to the lounge (see {@area area F11|29b|x}).

entries.name: Demonic Possession
entries: When a character enters this area, they can take the {@action Study|XPHB} action to focus on the portraits' unsettling images and make a {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) check. On a success, the character realizes the portraits' movements aren't real and that the area is desecrated with Abyssal energy. The character knows that any player character who lingers in this room for 1 minute or longer will be subject to possession by demons.

If a character lingers in the room for 1 minute or longer, the character hears the mages speak with demonic voices. The mages say phrases in Abyssal such as "Bathe in their blood!" and "Chaos and murder reign supreme." The character is the target of Demonic Possession, as described in the {@book Dungeon Master's Guide|XDMG|2|Demonic Possession}. A character is targeted by this effect only once.

entries.name: F11: Lounge
