entries: What was once a beautiful lounge lies in disarray. Armchairs are toppled, and tables are smashed. Two bodies, blood dried on their dented plate armor, lie splayed on the floor. A hulking dragonborn man in black armor watches while a six-armed monster and two desiccated, black-armored knights with green, glowing eyes move to attack a double door to the northeast.

A {@creature Marilith|XMM} and two {@creature Death Knight Aspirant|XMM|Death Knight Aspirants} move to assault the locked doors to {@area area F14|2a5|x} as Goreth Blacktooth (Medium, Neutral Evil {@creature Warrior Commander|XMM}) looks on. When any of them notices the characters, they fight to the death; Goreth shrieks his devotion to Szass Tam all the while.

entries.name: Bodies
entries: The bodies are those of Dau family guards: the orc Gregesh and the human Karla. Saraphine asked them to guard the doors to the magical lab ({@area area F14|2a5|x}); Goreth and his allies slaughtered them before the characters arrived.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: A {@item +1 Greatsword|XDMG} lies near the western fallen guard.

entries.name: F12: Study

entries: This cozy space boasts comfortable chairs, a table, and many open books.
Saraphine was pouring through tomes here before Goreth Blacktooth attacked the fortress.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: If the characters spend 10 minutes searching this room, they find a {@item Tome of Leadership and Influence|XDMG} among the books.

entries.name: F13: Armory

entries: Suits of armor are stored here, and weapon racks stand against the east wall.
Weapons and armor are kept here for use by the family's guards.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: The armor stands and weapon racks hold the following items:

entries.name: F14: Magical Lab
entries: The double door to this area is locked with an {@spell Arcane Lock|XPHB} spell. When the characters enter this area, read or paraphrase the following:

An enormous desk curves along the south and east walls, supporting magical laboratory equipment. At the desk, a young human woman frantically scans a book and mumbles to herself. Shelves stand against the north and west walls.
The characters recognize the woman as Saraphine Dau (Medium {@creature Mage|XMM}), Sabinia's sister.

Saraphine is overjoyed if the characters have killed the monsters in the fortress. If they haven't yet freed the people trapped in the bedchambers (areas {@area F3–F5|285|x}), she begs the characters to do so. She feels terrible that the assault on the fortress began before she could usher the others into the safety of this lab and that the guards died trying to defend her.

Here, generations of the Dau family have researched magic and created new spells. Although she's not yet a Red Wizard, Saraphine covets the title and hopes to make magical advances to impress the mages and her family. She is an ingenious magical researcher and understands magical theory better than most Red Wizards, though she finds spellcasting difficult.

entries.name: Development
entries: If the characters defeat all the monsters in the Fortress of Opposition, Saraphine gladly answers their questions about magical barriers. When the characters describe the barrier around Castle Thrul, read or paraphrase the following:
Saraphine sighs thoughtfully, then snaps her fingers in triumph.

"Yes, of course!" she exclaims. "The barrier must be constructed from Abyssal energy. It's like a wall of force but more potent. You need disintegration magic designed specifically to affect the spiritual resonances of that realm.
"I've got a scroll I can make some adjustments to. You can use it to punch a hole in the barrier."

Saraphine rummages through a nearby table and finds a {@item Spell Scroll|XDMG} {@i of} {@spell Disintegrate|XPHB}. Over the course of 10 minutes, she makes adjustments to the scroll's writing and diagrams. She then offers the modified scroll to the characters.

Saraphine explains that a character must use the adjusted {@item Spell Scroll|XDMG} while within 30 feet of the barrier around Castle Thrul. Doing this will create a permanent 10-foot-by-10-foot hole in the barrier.

If no character can use the scroll, Saraphine instead scribbles a phonetic representation of the {@spell Disintegrate|XPHB} spell's modified verbal component. She modifies and then demonstrates the accompanying somatic component. She tells the characters that one of them must re-create these components within 30 feet of the barrier to create a permanent 10-foot-by-10-foot hole in it. This is dangerous; see "{@adventure Abyssal Barrier|AUD|6|Abyssal Barrier}" in "Castle Thrul."
Once the fortress is free of monsters, Saraphine musters the other trapped inhabitants to stay in the lab with her until the region is safe.
When the characters learn how to punch a hole in the barrier around Castle Thrul, each character earns 11,700 XP.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: Saraphine gives the characters the items she has stockpiled here to help their fight against Szass Tam:

items: Three {@item Potion of Superior Healing|XDMG|Potions of Healing (superior)}
Two {@item Spell Scroll|XDMG|Spell Scrolls} {@i of} {@spell Project Image|XPHB}

entries.name: F15: Storage

entries: Shelves full of linens and open boxes line the walls of this storage room.
This room holds household supplies.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: If the characters search this room, they find three vials each of {@item Acid|XPHB}, {@item Alchemist's Fire|XPHB}, {@item Antitoxin|XPHB}, and {@item Basic Poison|XPHB}.

entries.name: F16: Master Bedchamber

entries: Within this luxurious room, a gorgeous canopy bed with embroidered silk hangings occupies the northeast corner, an ornate wardrobe sits along the southwest wall, and an armchair nestles into the northwest corner.
This is Saraphine's bedroom.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: Twenty sets of {@item Fine Clothes|XPHB} hang in the wardrobe. A drawer inside the wardrobe holds five diamonds worth 25,000 GP total.

entries.name: Castle Thrul
entries: One of the oldest buildings in Thaymount, Castle Thrul is a sprawling stone complex that includes a main hall and a 130-foot central tower surrounded by a stone wall. A necropolis where esteemed family members are interred sits south of the primary complex. An underground tunnel in the necropolis's largest mausoleum leads into the castle's armory ({@area area C8|2db|x} on {@adventure map 6.3|AUD|6|Map 6.3: Castle Thrul}), while a passage in the northeast wing ({@area area C13|2ed|x}) leads to the Citadel, where Szass Tam weaves his ritual.

entries.name: Lich's Strike Force
entries: When Szass Tam discovered Zulkir Thrul was behind Operation Deadfall, he vowed to destroy her and everyone she loves, starting with those in Castle Thrul. The lich assigned this job to the demilich Yoreth, whose lair is in the Citadel, and the human Red Wizard Jarek.
Szass Tam instructed Yoreth and Jarek to marshal demonic and undead forces to descend on Castle Thrul and kill anyone they encountered.

entries.name: Keeping the Characters Out
entries: After Szass Tam dispatched Yoreth and Jarek to Castle Thrul, the lich erected a barrier around the castle grounds outside the stone wall as described in "{@area Abyssal Barriers|273|x}" earlier in this chapter.
As a contingency, Szass Tam instructed Yoreth to set a trap for the characters.

entries.name: False Zulkir
entries: Using a {@item Spell Scroll|XDMG} of {@spell Programmed Illusion|XPHB} ({@dc 17}), Jarek has created an illusion of Zulkir Thrul bound with magically glowing chains to the summit of the castle's tower ({@area area C15|2f2|x}). The illusion activates when the characters come within 150 feet of the castle. For five minutes, the illusion depicts Thrul struggling against the chains and shouting for help. After five minutes, it disappears; it reactivates after 10 minutes if the party moves anywhere outside the castle within 150 feet.
Jarek hopes the illusion will fool the characters into trying to rescue the zulkir so Jarek, Yoreth, and their balor ally can ambush them.

entries.name: Approaching the Castle
entries: Read or paraphrase the following when the characters come within 150 feet of Castle Thrul:

Black haze billows in the sky, where green lightning flashes. Behind a translucent green barrier, a stalwart fortress ringed by a stone wall rises along the hill before you. South of the fortress, squat buildings with interspersed gravestones stands somberly; four black-armored soldiers patrol the grounds with jerky movements.
Jutting from the fortress against the hazy horizon is a tower, around which flies a tiny orb that glows green. Lashed to the tower is a red-robed figure that shouts for help.

entries.name: Castle Features
entries: Castle Thrul is made of magically treated stone that has {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to all damage. The castle otherwise has the following features.

entries.name: Abyssal Barrier
entries: The characters must punch a hole through the Abyssal barrier surrounding the castle (see {@area area F14|2a5|x} in "Fortress of Opposition" earlier in this chapter). They can create this hole anywhere they want.

If the characters use Saraphine's modified verbal and somatic components to punch a hole in the barrier instead of her modified {@item Spell Scroll|XDMG} {@i of} {@spell Disintegrate|XPHB}, a character takes an action to follow Saraphine's instructions and makes a {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) check. On a successful check, the character punches a hole in the barrier and takes 13 ({@dice 3d8}) Necrotic damage from magical backlash. On a failure, the character punches a hole in the barrier, but the magical backlash rips through them, and they take 27 ({@dice 6d8}) Necrotic damage.

entries.name: Ceilings
entries: Ceilings in buildings in the necropolis ({@area area C1|2bf|x}) are 10 feet high. The ceiling in the guard tower ({@area area C2|2c5|x}) is 20 feet high. Those on the castle's main floor (areas {@area C4–C14|2cf|x}) are 30 feet high.

entries.name: Corpses
entries: Yoreth and Jarek's forces killed many of those who were in Castle Thrul when their strike force descended. Bodies of these victims are in areas {@area C2|2c5|x}–{@area C4|2cf|x}. The victims knew key information that can help the characters as they explore the castle.

The characters might communicate with or raise a victim from the dead, perhaps using the {@item Rod of Resurrection|XDMG} found in {@area area C1|2bf|x} to cast {@spell Resurrection|XPHB} on a victim. Each victim shares a different piece of information, beginning with "Door Passphrase," until the characters know all the following:

items.name: Door Passphrase
items.entry: The only way to open the door to the gallery ({@area area C10|2e2|x}) is to use the passphrase "Thay shall endure."

items.name: Lurking Balor
items.entry: The forces that are attacking the castle include a {@creature balor|XMM}.

items.name: Strike Force Leaders
items.entry: The forces that overran the castle were led by a demilich named Yoreth and a Red Wizard named Jarek, both of whom serve Szass Tam.

items.name: Tower Trap
items.entry: The leaders of the attack on the castle bragged about a trap involving an illusion of Zulkir Thrul lashed to the tower ({@area area C15|2f2|x}).

entries.name: Doors
entries: The castle's doors are made of metal and are unlocked, except for the double door leading into the gallery ({@area area C10|2e2|x}).

entries.name: Lighting
entries: Areas outside Castle Thrul have {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} during the day due to the evil magic that swirls through Thaymount. Inside the castle, sconces with {@spell Continual Flame|XPHB} spells cast on them shed {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB}.

entries.name: Structural Damage
entries: Castle Thrul has been under assault for days, during which time demons have damaged its structure—particularly the roof and walls on the west side of the fortress. The chunks of rubble on the ground in most of the western spaces (areas {@area C6|2d6|x}–{@area C9|2df|x}) make those areas {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB}.

entries.name: Thaymount's Wards
entries: Like everywhere on the plateau, the castle is affected by Thaymount's ancient magical wards (see "{@area Magic on Thaymount|270|x}" earlier in this chapter).

entries.name: Castle Locations
entries: The following locations are keyed to map 6.3.

entries.name: C1: Necropolis

entries: A side path branching off the road to Castle Thrul leads to an austere graveyard at the base of a low cliff. The gravestones, obelisks, and covered tombs bear the names of Thrul ancestors.
A mausoleum sits on the necropolis's north end. Four soldiers in black armor with green, glowing eyes patrol the area haltingly.
The patrolling soldiers are four {@creature Death Knight Aspirant|XMM|Death Knight Aspirants}; they fight the characters on sight.

entries.name: Graves
entries: All the graves, some as old as four hundred years, belong to members of the Thrul family.

entries.name: Mausoleum
entries: The mausoleum includes four sarcophagi, in which are interred prominent Thrul Red Wizards. The mausoleum includes a shrine for offerings and a secret door to a tunnel leading into the castle (see below for both).

entries.name: Secret Door
entries: The back of the mausoleum houses a secret door (marked with an S on the map; {@dc 20} to notice), behind which a staircase leads to an underground tunnel. The tunnel leads to the armory ({@area area C8|2db|x}). The door leading to area C8 is visible from inside the tunnel.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: An unlocked drawer in the shrine's base contains a {@item Rod of Resurrection|XDMG}. On the shrine, jewelry worth 10,000 GP in total is laid out as offerings.

entries.name: C2: Guard Tower

entries: A stone tower sits at the castle complex's southwest corner. Inside slumps an armored body, whose sword lies nearby. A ladder leads upward.
The death knights in the necropolis ({@area area C1|2bf|x}) have already swept through this area.

entries.name: Ladder
entries: The ladder leads to the top of the guard tower, where battlements surround the flat roof. Any creature on the roof has {@table Cover|XPHB|Half Cover} from creatures on the ground.

entries.name: Thuvia's Corpse
entries: The corpse belongs to Thuvia, captain of the Thruls' family guard. The rest of the guards fled the castle when Thuvia fell. See "{@area Castle Features|2d1|x}" for additional details on corpses.

entries.name: Journal
entries: Thuvia's small, leather-bound journal is tucked in a pouch on her belt. If the characters spend 10 minutes perusing it, they learn the passphrase to the locked door that leads to the gallery ({@area area C10|2e2|x}): "Thay shall endure."

entries.name: Treasure
entries: Thuvia's equipment includes a suit of {@item Plate Armor|XPHB} and a {@item +3 Longsword|XDMG}.

entries.name: C3: Courtyard

entries: Just west of the necropolis is a courtyard that holds a small well.
A peaked wooden roof tops the 5-foot-diameter stone well, which is 20 feet deep. The rope for the well's bucket has been cut, and the bucket has fallen into the well.

entries.name: Xelnius's Corpse
entries: In the well is the corpse of the human Red Wizard Xelnius Thrul, Zulkir Thrul's brother. Xelnius's body floats at the water's surface, 10 feet belowground, though it is easy to spot thanks to his red robes. Before he died, Xelnius was terrified for his sister, whom he loves dearly. See "{@area Castle Features|2d1|x}" for additional details on corpses.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: Xelnius wears a {@item Headband of Intellect|XDMG} and a set of crimson {@item Fine Clothes|XPHB}.

entries.name: C4: Great Hall

entries: A huge portcullis, ripped from its housing, lies dented here on the ground. Three enormous, crimson bipedal fiends with horns and massive claws rampage through the once-lavish great hall, knocking over pedestals, smashing busts and statues, and shredding crimson banners. Four armored bodies, their corpses twisted strangely, lie scattered about the room. A dais to the east leads to a large double door.
The fiends are three {@creature Goristro|XMM|Goristros}; they fight the characters on sight.
The hall was once decorated with tapestries and statuary depicting the glories of House Thrul over the centuries, but they've all been destroyed.

entries.name: Corpses
entries: The bodies are those of four Thrul family guards: the humans Retha and Rian and the orcs Wythe and Cadeth. See "{@area Castle Features|2d1|x}" for additional details on corpses.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: The guards' weapons and armor include the following:

entries.name: C5: North Library

entries: Undisturbed bookshelves fill this small library.
The demons haven't reached this area yet.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: If the characters spend 10 minutes searching the shelves, they find a {@item Tome of Clear Thought|XDMG} and a {@item Tome of Understanding|XDMG}.

entries.name: C6: South Library

entries: Chunks of masonry have fallen from the roof here and lie atop collapsed shelves. Fallen books are scattered about the area.
Demons smashed a hole through the roof, showering the room with masonry.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: A character can take the {@action Search|XPHB} action to sift through the rubble and make a {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check. On a success, the character finds a {@item Manual of Golems|XDMG}.

entries.name: C7: Mustering Yard

entries: The south end of this open yard is choked with rubble from a partially collapsed wall.
This yard is abandoned.

entries.name: C8: Armory

entries: Weapons and shields litter the floor, and suits of armor lie strewn about. Rubble from the damaged ceiling fills the northwest corner.
This chamber stored arms and armor for the Thrul family's guards, as well as household supplies. Demons damaged the roof and tore through the armory, leaving it in disarray.

entries.name: Secret Door
entries: A secret door (marked with an S on the map; {@dc 20} to notice) opens to a steep staircase down. The stairs lead to a tunnel that emerges in the mausoleum in the necropolis ({@area area C1|2bf|x}). The secret door to the necropolis is visible from inside the tunnel.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: The Thrul family generously outfitted the castle's guards. A character who searches the area finds the following:

items: Three {@item Scale Mail|XPHB|suits of Scale Mail}

entries.name: C9: Barrack

entries: Partial walls create a semblance of privacy in this crowded barrack. Rubble from a collapsed wall fills the southern half of the barrack.
This barrack once housed Thrul family guards and servants, as well as staff accompanying dignitaries. The servants were sent away when the situation in Thaymount escalated.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: As a {@action Search|XPHB} action, a character can look under the beds and make a {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check. On a success, the character finds rucksacks under three of the beds. The rucksacks each contain various coins worth 250 GP total.

entries.name: C10: Gallery
entries: When the characters approach the gallery's entrance, read or paraphrase the following:
This metal double door bears embossed images of eight mages in regal poses and flowing robes. Most are bald and bear tattoos. Above the image are the words "All Glory to Thrul" in Common.

This double door is protected with a magical, Invisible barrier similar to the effect of a {@spell Wall of Force|XPHB} spell, except it can't be suppressed and a {@spell Disintegrate|XPHB} spell doesn't destroy it. Only speaking the passphrase "Thay shall endure" removes the barrier. The barrier reappears 1 minute after the passphrase is spoken.

A character can take the {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine the barrier and make a {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) check. On a success, the character realizes a passphrase is the only way to bypass the barrier.

entries.name: Discovering the Passphrase
entries: The characters might learn the passphrase from one of the corpses in areas {@area C2|2c5|x}–{@area C4|2cf|x} (see "{@area Castle Features|2d1|x}" for more about learning from corpses). They might also learn the passphrase from the journal on Thuvia's body in {@area area C2|2c5|x}.
Once the characters enter this area, read or paraphrase the following:

Eight twenty-foot-tall portraits of mages in crimson robes ring this gallery. Each portrait bears a brass nameplate. The portraits overlook a cozy, undisturbed lounge, with plush armchairs in the center and a spiral staircase to the north.

The eight nameplates bear the names Renia Thrul, Darius Thrul, Zulkir Aznar Thrul, Ferene Thrul, Xander Thrul, Vernus Thrul, Geryn Thrul, and Zulkir Xelnene Thrul. The characters recognize the portrait of Xelnene, who bears a dour, regal expression matching those of her ancestors.

If the characters aren't already aware of Zulkir Aznar Thrul, a character can take the {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine Aznar's portrait and make a {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill History|XPHB}) check. On a success, the character knows everything in the "{@adventure History|AUD|9|Xelnene Thrul}" section of Xelnene Thrul's entry in appendix B.

entries.name: Staircase
entries: The staircase to the north ascends 130 feet to the top of the castle's tower ({@area area C15|2f2|x}).

entries.name: C11: Thuvia's Chamber

entries: This bedchamber displays an array of military medals. Along the south wall are two trunks.
This was the bedroom of guard captain Thuvia, whose body is in the guard tower ({@area area C2|2c5|x}). The Thruls considered her a member of the family.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: The left trunk holds Thuvia's emergency stash of coins. It totals 50,000 GP.
The trunk on the right contains five sets of {@item Traveler's Clothes|XPHB} and a {@item Dread Helm|XDMG} that was a gift from Xelnene Thrul's late father, Geryn.

entries.name: C12: Xelnius's Chamber

entries: This lavish chamber includes a bed with a blue duvet, a marble washbasin in a wooden stand, and two trunks to the north.
This was the bedroom of Xelnius Thrul, whose body was thrown into the well ({@area area C3|2cb|x}).

entries.name: Treasure
entries: The trunks and wardrobe are unlocked. The wardrobe holds ten sets of {@item Fine Clothes|XPHB}. The right trunk contains four {@item Potion of Superior Healing|XDMG|Potions of Healing (superior)}; the left one is empty.

entries.name: C13: Zulkir Thrul's Chamber

entries: This bedroom's red bedspread and nightstand bear a light layer of dust. A trapdoor is built into the stone floor.
This chamber is Xelnene Thrul's bedroom, though the zulkir rarely stays here. She keeps nothing of value in this room.

entries.name: Underground Passage
entries: The trapdoor on the south end of the room leads to a maze of tunnels underneath Thaymount. From this maze, the characters can reach the area of the Citadel where Szass Tam weaves his ritual. (See "{@area Next Steps|2f4|x}" when the characters descend into these tunnels.)

entries.name: C14: Family Lounge

entries: This rich-looking lounge contains plush crimson armchairs gathered around a central table.
Members of the family relax and eat their meals in this lounge.

entries.name: C15: Tower Summit

entries.title: Szass Tam's forces have created this illusion of Zulkir Thrul in danger.

entries: When the characters come within 10 feet of the outside of this tower on foot or via flight, read or paraphrase the following:

A massive, four-horned fiend leaps onto the top of the tower, laughing hideously. It is joined by a flying mage with red robes and facial tattoos and by a skull alight with green flames, which flies at you, screaming, "You shall pay with your lives for opposing Szass Tam!"

The skull is Yoreth ({@creature Demilich|XMM}), and the mage is the Red Wizard Jarek (Medium {@creature Archmage|XMM}). They are further described in "{@area Lich's Strike Force|2b1|x}." Accompanying them is a {@creature Balor|XMM} that slipped onto the Material Plane near the castle. Yoreth and Jarek enticed the fiendish general to assault the castle, promising the balor could kill powerful heroes—the characters. These three fight the characters to the death.

entries.name: Next Steps
entries: When the characters descend through the trapdoor in the zulkir's chamber ({@area area C13|2ed|x}), each character earns 14,200 XP. The trapdoor opens into a tunnel to the Citadel; this journey is described in chapter 7.

data.name: Chapter 7: Szass Tam Must Die
entries: {@i Fight Szass Tam and save Thay from destruction}.

entries.title: Szass Tam nears the end of his ritual to raise an overwhelming horde of malefites.

entries.name: Key Plot Points
entries: The following information is key to this chapter's story:

items.name: Sarrukh Guardians
items.entry: Magical serpentine creatures called sarrukhs guard the entrance to Szass Tam's ritual chamber. The characters must circumvent or dispatch the sarrukhs before they face the lich.

items.name: Stop Szass Tam
items.entry: When the characters arrive in the ritual chamber, they can confront Szass Tam and his allies and stop him from raising a malefite army that will destroy Thay.

entries.name: Preparation
entries: Before running this chapter, prepare as follows:

items.name: Step 1
items.entry: Read the "{@area Running This Chapter|2f8|x}" section, including "{@area Character Advancement|2f9|x}."

items.name: Step 2
items.entry: Familiarize yourself with the Key NPCs table below.

items.name: Step 3
items.entry: Bookmark the stat blocks below, which appear in the {@i Monster Manual} and on D&D Beyond unless otherwise noted. If a stat block appears in appendix B, an asterisk appears after its name:

entries.caption: Key NPCs
rows: Draconic malefite allied with Szass Tam
Lich plotting to unleash a malefite horde against Thay
Sarrukh clan leaders and Szass Tam's allies
Human zulkir of evocation and Operation Deadfall's leader

entries.name: Running This Chapter
entries: This chapter takes place after the characters have found the tunnel from Castle Thrul to the Citadel.

entries.name: Character Advancement
entries: The characters should be level 19 when this chapter begins. They should be level 20 by the time they face Szass Tam in {@area area Z14|32d|x}.

entries.name: Reaching the Citadel
entries: The tunnel in Castle Thrul leads to a labyrinthine underground structure of caverns and passageways. The route to the Citadel is about two miles.

These underground areas, which are in {@variantrule Darkness|XPHB}, are difficult to navigate. To keep the characters on the safest, most direct route, one character makes a {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Survival|XPHB}) check. On a success, the characters reach the sanctum without incident. Proceed with "{@area Szass Tam's Sanctum|300|x}."
On a failure, the characters stray into dangerous tunnels and encounter monsters, as described below.

entries.name: Underground Ambush
entries: Use any area on the Underdark Warren map in the {@book Dungeon Master's Guide|XDMG|9|Underdark Warren} for this encounter.
Read or paraphrase the following, which assumes the characters have a way to see in the dark:
Three hulking serpentine warriors wielding polearms patrol this passage.
These three {@creature Sarrukh Tyrant|AUD|Sarrukh Tyrants} serve Szass Tam and search the area for intruders.
When the sarrukhs notice the characters, read or paraphrase the following:
One of the serpentine horrors shrieks in Common, "Intruders! For nearing the sarrukh stronghold, you shall die. For defying Szass Tam, you shall become the lich's rotting puppets!"

entries.name: Sarrukh Lore
entries: A character can take the {@action Study|XPHB} action and make a {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill History|XPHB}) check. On a success, the character realizes the creatures are sarrukhs and recalls that these creatures once commanded a wicked empire that spanned Faerûn, but it fell millennia ago. The character knows sarrukhs are now nearly extinct.
The sarrukhs fight to the death. Once the characters defeat the sarrukhs, they can proceed to the Citadel, emerging in Szass Tam's sanctum.

entries.name: Szass Tam's Sanctum
entries: A subterranean level of the Citadel serves as Szass Tam's sanctum for weaving the Malefice Mortum ritual.

Like the rest of the Citadel, the sarrukhs built this area millennia ago. Szass Tam long ago allied with the sarrukhs still in this complex. He promised that once he controls Thay, he'll help them conquer the other peoples in the Underdark under Thaymount.

entries.name: Sanctum Features
entries: Szass Tam's sanctum has the following features.

entries.name: Ceilings
entries: Ceilings in the sanctum are 40 feet high, with the exception of areas {@area Z13|327|x} and {@area Z14|32d|x}. Ceilings in those areas are 100 feet high.

entries.name: Doors
entries: The sanctum's doors are made of stone. All are unlocked except the double door to the hall of corrupted lava ({@area area Z13|327|x}), which is locked with an {@spell Arcane Lock|XPHB} spell. (See "Doors" in the {@book Dungeon Master's Guide|XDMG|2|Doors}.)

entries.name: Lighting
entries: Sconces and braziers with {@spell Continual Flame|XPHB} spells cast on them illuminate the sanctum with green-tinted {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB}. The exception is {@area area Z13|327|x}, where the green lava's glow creates eerie {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB}.

entries.name: Szass Tam's Lair
entries: The sanctum is Szass Tam's lair. It exhibits the effects described in his entry in {@adventure appendix B|AUD|9|Szass Tam}.

entries.name: Unhallowed Ward
entries: Szass Tam's evil magic has created a permanent effect similar to that of a {@spell Hallow|XPHB} spell, but it affects the whole sanctum. Celestials can't willingly enter the sanctum, and Humanoids have {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} to Necrotic damage here. The effect is suppressed for any creature in the area of an {@spell Antimagic Field|XPHB} spell. The effect can't be dispelled.

entries.name: Sanctum Locations
entries: The following locations are keyed to map 7.1.

entries.name: Z1: Entryway

entries: An ancient statue of a serpentine warrior wielding a polearm stands against the far wall. Green light flickers off its carved armor and scales.

The statue depicts a hero of the long-lost sarrukh empire. A character can take the {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine the statue and make a {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill History|XPHB}) check. On a success, the character recalls the lore about sarrukhs described in "{@area Underground Ambush|2fb|x}."

entries.name: Poisoned Dart Traps
entries: The traps marked by the letter T on the map are poisoned dart traps, as described in the {@trap Poisoned Darts|XDMG|Dungeon Master's Guide}, except the darts—sarrukh fangs dripping with poison—deal 24 ({@dice 7d6}) Poison damage each.

entries.name: Z2: Communal Hall

entries: Two serpentine figures near a long table argue in a hissing, guttural tongue. Both have the heads and lower bodies of snakes but torsos like those of humanoids, albeit scaly. One is bulkier than the other and has glowing green eyes; black rot mottles its desiccated scales.
The bulky creature is Ssarthe ({@creature Arisen Sarrukh|AUD}), who achieved undeath long ago. Ssarthe argues in Draconic with Vartheeth ({@creature Sarrukh Tyrant|AUD}).

The sarrukhs fight the characters on noticing them. Ssarthe fights to the death, but if Ssarthe is killed or Vartheeth is {@status Bloodied|XPHB}, Vartheeth surrenders. Vartheeth reveals the following if the characters agree to let her flee:

items.name: Return to Glory
items.entry: Szass Tam has promised this sarrukh clan he'll help them conquer the other peoples under Thaymount once his ritual is complete. Vartheeth is skeptical, as the lich ignored their earlier requests for such help for centuries.

items.name: Ritual Chamber Guardians
items.entry: An undead dragon with glowing green eyes guards the lich's ritual chamber. The dragon is joined by undead sarrukhs named Vorsoth and Xileesh, the stronghold's leaders, whom the lich has promised to install as emperors in the future sarrukh empire. Szass Tam has also promised the dragon something valuable in exchange for his service, but Vartheeth doesn't know the details. Vartheeth suspects Szass Tam is lying about everything.

items.name: Sarrukh Superiority
items.entry: Like all sarrukhs, Vartheeth believes sarrukhs are superior to everyone else.

items.name: Undead Aspirations
items.entry: Like most sarrukhs, Vartheeth wants to become undead to ensure she'll witness the resurgence of the sarrukh empire.

entries.name: Z3: Hall of Tyranny

entries: Flickering green light from sconces forms shadowy scenes on the walls of serpentine creatures hoisting polearms. An overwhelming sense of dread fills you as the shadows leap from the walls and slither toward you.
This magical effect is an illusion.

entries.name: Illusory Danger
entries: When a character enters this area, they can take the {@action Study|XPHB} action and make a {@dc 18} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check to try to recognize the illusion.
On a failed check, a character makes a {@dc 15} Wisdom saving throw, taking 42 ({@dice 12d6}) Psychic damage on a failed save or half as much on a successful one.
A character is subject to this magical effect only once. A character who carries a figurine from {@area area Z9|31d|x} is immune to this effect.

entries.name: Z4: Library

entries: Bookcases filled with weathered tomes surround a reading table here. Two bulky serpentine figures peruse the volumes on the shelves.

Two {@creature Arisen Sarrukh|AUD|Arisen Sarrukhs} (see appendix B) search through these books about necromancy, seeking to better understand Szass Tam's ritual. The sarrukhs fight the characters on noticing them.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: The books contain all the Necromancy spells in the {@book Player's Handbook|XPHB}. A character can take the {@action Search|XPHB} action and make a {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check to examine the books. On a success, the character finds five tomes worth 500 GP each.

entries.name: Z5: South Sarrukh Chambers
entries: A wall divides this hall into two chambers with a doorless opening between them. Each chamber holds a nest of green cushions; the northern chamber also holds a desk.
The clan's sarrukh tyrants rest here and in {@area area Z6|314|x}.
In the northern chamber, an unlocked drawer in the northwest desk holds a {@item Potion of Vitality|XDMG}. In the southern chamber, underneath the cushions is a small pouch containing 100 PP.

entries.name: Z6: North Sarrukh Quarters

entries: Several nests made from blankets lie to the north.
If the characters spend 10 minutes searching the northwest nest, they find Vartheeth's journal, written in Draconic. It reveals the information she might mention in {@area area Z2|30b|x}.

entries.name: Z7: Magical Laboratory

entries: A twenty-foot-wide rune scribed on the floor glows green. Two serpentine figures chant incantations in a hissing, guttural tone, their eyes closed in concentration. Tables holding open books and vials of liquid sit along the walls.

The chanting figures are Tresshe and Yethel ({@creature Sarrukh Tyrant|AUD|Sarrukh Tyrants}; see appendix B). They know Szass Tam's ritual has bathed the area in unholy magic (see "{@area Unhallowed Ward|306|x}"). They hope the effect, mixed with their own magic, will turn them undead.

The sarrukhs fight the characters on sight but surrender if {@status Bloodied|XPHB}. In exchange for being allowed to escape, they reveal the information Vartheeth might share in {@area area Z2|30b|x}, though they believe Szass Tam's promise.

entries.name: Glowing Rune
entries: The rune on the floor thrums with ancient magic. As an action, a creature can stand on the rune and feel magical energy flow through them. For the next hour, whenever that creature casts a spell that forces a creature to make a saving throw, one target of the spellcaster's choice has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on saves against the spell.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: A {@item Potion of Supreme Healing|XDMG|Potion of Healing (supreme)} lies on the northeast table.

entries.name: Z8: Scriptorium

entries: The tables here bear writing supplies and coins. Three serpentine figures are writing furiously.

In this scriptorium, three {@creature Sarrukh Tyrant|AUD|Sarrukh Tyrants} (see appendix B) scribe {@item Spell Scroll|XDMG|Spell Scrolls} to help Szass Tam's cause. They fight the characters on noticing them.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: The tables hold three sets of {@item Calligrapher's Supplies|XPHB}, as well as {@item Ink|XPHB} and {@item Parchment|XPHB}. The tables also contain three {@item Spell Scroll|XDMG|Spell Scrolls} of {@spell Delayed Blast Fireball|XPHB}, a {@item Spell Scroll|XDMG} of {@spell Imprisonment|XPHB}, and a {@item Spell Scroll|XDMG} of {@spell Time Stop|XPHB}.
The coins on the tables amount to 1,000 GP total.

entries.name: Z9: Shrine

entries: Candles burn green here in a semicircle on the floor, and foot-tall serpentine figurines stand on velvet cloths. The east wall is carved with a relief of an enormous serpent biting its own tail.
This is a shrine to the enigmatic World Serpent and other gods the sarrukhs venerate. Characters proficient in {@skill Religion|XPHB} identify the World Serpent carving.

entries.name: Figurines
entries: The figurines on the ground depict snakelike or draconic deities that the sarrukhs believe are manifestations of the World Serpent. Characters proficient in {@skill Religion|XPHB} identify the figurines as depicting the following deities:

items.name: Asgorath:
items.entry: Dragon said to have created the world

items.name: Jazirian:
items.entry: Couatl deity

items.name: Shekinester:
items.entry: Patron god of nagas

entries: There is one figurine per character; more than one figurine can depict each deity if needed.

entries.name: Development
entries: A character carrying a figurine is immune to the effects of the illusion in {@area area Z3|30d|x}.

entries.name: Z10: Storage

entries: This room bears trunks and crates.
These trunks contain 50 {@item Rations|XPHB} total.

entries.name: Z11: Hall of Glories

entries: Dotting this corridor are frescoes and statues depicting serpentine conquerers cowing myriad other creatures depicted as terrified and weak.
Characters proficient in {@skill History|XPHB} recognize that the frescoes and statues depict sarrukh history.

entries.name: Z12: Antechamber of Skulls

entries.title: Heroes prepare to confront the sarrukhs who guard an antechamber in Szass Tam's sanctum.

entries: Two curved stairways rise five feet to a double door guarded by two serpentine warriors, one wielding a fauchard and the other a trident.
The guards are an {@creature Arisen Sarrukh|AUD} and {@creature Sarrukh Tyrant|AUD} (see appendix B for both), who fight the characters on noticing them.

entries.name: Explosive Glyph
entries: A nearly imperceptible glyph is scribed on the center of the double door (see area Z13). Noticing the glyph requires a successful {@dc 21} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check.

The glyph triggers when a creature touches the double door. When triggered, the glyph erupts with magical energy in a 30-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone} originating from the center of the door. Each creature in that area makes a Dexterity saving throw. A creature takes 22 ({@dice 5d8}) Acid damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

entries.name: Z13: Hall of Corrupted Lava
entries: The double door to this area is locked with an {@spell Arcane Lock|XPHB} spell. When the characters enter this area, read or paraphrase the following:

Heat rises off the green river of bubbling lava that snakes northward toward a dais, where an enormous dragon of bone and desiccated flesh looms. Two serpentine warriors with rotting scales, each brandishing a trident, stand near the dais. Rubble chokes alcoves to the east and west.

The dragon is Drevoralyx, a Huge {@creature Dracolich|XMM}. Two {@creature Arisen Sarrukh|AUD|Arisen Sarrukhs} (see appendix B) accompany him—Vorsoth and Xileesh, the sarrukh clan's leaders. Since Drevoralyx isn't a true dracolich, he has no lair (see "{@area Draconic Malefite|32a|x}").
When any of these creatures notice the characters, read or paraphrase the following:
The dragon shouts in a guttural voice, "You must be the maggots Szass Tam described. Leave now, or I shall squash you like the bugs you are!"

The creatures will entertain a question before they fight the characters to the death. If the characters ask why they're protecting Szass Tam, Drevoralyx reveals that Szass Tam has promised to install him as the malefites' general. Vorsoth and Xileesh reveal that Szass Tam has promised to help them become joint emperors of a new sarrukh empire in the Underdark.

entries.name: Draconic Malefite
entries: A character can take the {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine Drevoralyx and make a {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) check. On a success, the character realizes the foul magic from Szass Tam's ritual animated the dead dragon, who traveled here from another part of the Citadel. The character knows this means Drevoralyx has no lair, doesn't have the Soul Gem trait, and is destroyed when reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.

entries.name: Alcoves
entries: The alcoves are blocked with rubble from collapsed stairs. Szass Tam blocked these stairways to ensure no one could enter his sanctum from here.

entries.name: Lava River
entries: The lava flow here occurs naturally, fueled by a nearby volcano. Szass Tam's magic has corrupted it, turning it green. The lava is 5 feet deep and {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB}. A creature that enters the lava or begins its turn there takes 27 ({@dice 5d10}) Fire damage and 27 ({@dice 5d10}) Necrotic damage.

entries.name: Z14: Ritual Chamber
entries: If the characters failed to receive the help of the pirates in chapter 5, Szass Tam received a number of ritual-boosting demon skulls equal to the number of characters. Add the following to the description of the ritual chamber after the first paragraph:
The horned, fanged skulls of fiends rest along the ritual circle. Runes glowing with green light cover the skulls.
When the characters enter this chamber, read or paraphrase the following:

A wide circle inscribed with profane runes glows green on this chamber's floor. Around the circle, shimmering images of hulking fiends bend backward unnaturally. A corona of green energy flows from the fiends to Szass Tam, who floats high above the ground, clutching a blackened spellbook.
In the southwest corner, Zulkir Thrul stands unmoving with a look of horror frozen on her face. Nearby, a pale woman's hands pulse with shadowy magic, and two enormous boar-headed beasts slaver.
Szass Tam smiles. "Ah, maggots," he sneers. "You must truly wish to be crushed. You think yourselves bold, but you are simply this generation's sad excuse for those who futilely stand against me."
The zulkir of necromancy beckons you with a clawlike hand. "Come, rail and rant as you must. Then die and be reborn as I please!"

{@creature Szass Tam|AUD} (see appendix B) flies 50 feet above the chamber's floor. He's defended by the vampire Nara Crocus (Medium {@creature Vampire Umbral Lord|XMM}), whose lair is elsewhere in the Citadel, and by her two {@creature Nalfeshnee|XMM} bodyguards.

entries.name: Szass Tam
entries: When this combat begins, the lich is maintaining {@status Concentration|XPHB} on his ritual. If he's reduced to 250 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} or fewer, he stops concentrating on the ritual if his {@status Concentration|XPHB} is still unbroken. Szass Tam keeps his distance from the characters while his allies are alive and uses every {@variantrule Action|XPHB}, {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}, and Legendary Action at his disposal.

entries.name: Zulkir Thrul
entries: Under the effects of {@spell Power Word Stun|XPHB}, {@creature Xelnene Thrul|AUD} (see appendix B) has the {@condition Stunned|XPHB} condition and 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} remaining. Roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} for Thrul. At the end of each of her turns, roll a {@dc 21} Constitution saving throw for Thrul as she tries to shake off the spell. On a success, she no longer has the {@condition Stunned|XPHB} condition and joins the combat against the lich. Szass Tam targets her on his next turn.

entries.name: Ritual Skulls
entries: If present, the skulls discharge magical bolts that target the characters.

Every round on {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} count 0 (losing ties), each skull targets a random player character. The character makes a {@dc 15} Dexterity saving throw, taking 18 ({@dice 4d8}) Necrotic damage on a failed save or half as much on a successful one.

entries.name: Demon Conduits
entries: Szass Tam is channeling necromantic magic through a translucent glabrezu, goristro, marilith, and nalfeshnee. The demons' souls are split between the Material Plane and the Abyss; if Szass Tam is killed or stops concentrating, these demons return to the Abyss.

entries.name: Spirit-Binding Censer
entries: If the characters retrieved the {@item Spirit-Binding Censer|AUD} (see appendix A) from the temple of the Red Knight in {@area chapter 4|19c|x}, they can use it to trap Szass Tam's soul for a hundred years.

entries.name: Development
entries: If Szass Tam dies, a flash of golden light bathes the sanctum in virtuous energy. All evidence of the lich's ritual disappears. Further, the holy energy replaces Szass Tam's blackened spellbook with the {@item Book of Exalted Deeds|XDMG}, which lies closed in the center of the chamber.

entries.name: Conclusion
entries: The outcome of the final battle has significant ramifications for Thay.

entries.name: Success
entries: If the characters disrupt Szass Tam's ritual, they foil his plans. Red Wizards, perhaps with the characters' help, eventually defeat the malefites and demons that have attacked the nation. If the characters kill Szass Tam but don't have the censer, Szass Tam revives in {@dice 1d10} days with all his {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} in another part of the Citadel. Thay must contend with the enraged lich, though he won't try anything as dramatic as this for several years.
If the characters trap Szass Tam's soul in the censer, Thay has a century to fortify itself against the lich and reshape its future.

entries.name: Zulkir Thrul
entries: If Thrul survives (or if the characters raise her from the dead), read or paraphrase the following:
After a moment spent breathing deeply and smoothing her robes, Zulkir Thrul turns to you.
"Operatives—friends—you did it. You stopped Szass Tam. More importantly, you saved Thay."
A small smile crosses her face. "It's time for me to return to Eltabbar. Won't you join me, heroes? We must discuss your reward."
After they return to Eltabbar, Thrul awards each character any Legendary magic item they request. She invites the heroes to work with her to fight for a better Thay for as long as they are willing.

entries.name: New Zulkir of Necromancy
entries: If any character is a Wizard with the Necromancer subclass or can prove their proficiency at Necromancy, Thrul suggests they vie to replace Szass Tam as zulkir of necromancy. This could be a satisfying capstone to the character's adventuring career. In this case, Thrul convinces the other zulkirs that the character earned the position by helping defeat Szass Tam. The characters have an opportunity to bring political change to Thay. They might need to contend with the lich's return, but that's a later adventure.

entries.name: The Mavericks
entries: If the characters visit the dissident Red Wizards after defeating Szass Tam, the mages express their gratitude for saving Thay—in their own self-aggrandizing way—and Sabinia thanks them for saving her sister. Each mage extends a standing invitation to the characters to visit their many estates.

entries.name: Failure
entries: If the party fails to disrupt Szass Tam's ritual, their mission fails, and Szass Tam's army of malefites kills thousands. The other zulkirs are killed or driven into hiding. Szass Tam's forces hunt down the Mavericks and slay them. The lich declares himself regent. He then turns his sights to conquering neighboring Aglarond and Rashemen.

If they survive, the characters must flee Thay. They might later become generals in a force that opposes the malefites. They will need to confront Szass Tam's malefite leaders and sycophants before they can hope to weaken the lich's grip on the nation.
